Newly elected commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Fred Foster Jr. joined returning incumbents Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton, as interim appointees Pam H. Karriker and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. concluded their service. Annual Chair/Vice Chair rotation: Dec 10, 2012–Dec 1, 2013 Fred Foster Jr. (Chair) and Brenda A. Howerton (Vice Chair); Dec 2, 2013–Dec 4, 2016 Michael D. Page (Chair) and Brenda A. Howerton (Vice Chair).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Acquisition of 1003 Santee Road Open Space Property ($950,000)
conflicts.summary: The Board split 3-2 over purchasing 264+ acres at 1003 Santee Road in East Durham for $950,000, weighing pre-designated open space funding, Falls Lake watershed protection, and equity for East Durham against a projected $19 million FY 2013-2014 budget gap and possible tax increases.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the $950,000 acquisition using previously set-aside open space funds
side_a_arguments: Funds were already designated in prior budgets for open space and farmland protection, avoiding direct impact on the upcoming operating budget.

One-third of the purchase price is covered by a City of Raleigh grant, and 93% of the 264+ acre site lies within 300 feet of water with Falls Lake frontage, potentially generating Falls Lake nutrient reduction credits.
Represents Durham County's first Eastern Open Space land purchase in a rapidly growing East Durham community near Neal Middle School.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose discretionary land acquisition during a severe projected budget shortfall
side_b_arguments: County Manager projections indicate a potential $19 million budget gap and possible property tax increases in the upcoming budget cycle.
Residents consulted in Southeast Durham weighed discretionary spending against tax burdens and urgent household needs.
Fiscal conservatism warrants deferring discretionary capital purchases under current budget constraints.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 3-2, authorizing the County Manager to enter an offer to purchase 1003 Santee Road for $950,000 and close by March 27, 2013.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-06-06 9:00 AM - Worksession
conflicts.issue: Withdrawing vs. Discussing the Draft Naming and Renaming Policy and Setting Policy Criteria
conflicts.summary: Commissioners clashed procedurally over whether to pull the draft Naming and Renaming Policy from the worksession agenda pending a transcript of their prior stadium/Willie Bradshaw discussion, resulting in a 0-5 defeat of the withdrawal motion, and then diverged on whether facilities could be named for living people or restricted to interior spaces.
conflicts.side_a_position: Keep the item on the agenda for immediate policy direction; bar naming facilities for living individuals and restrict naming to interior features rather than entire buildings
side_a_arguments: The board should provide clear answers to the County Attorney's policy questions rather than delaying again.
Prior board consensus on the stadium/Willie Bradshaw discussion opposed naming entire buildings and favored naming interior features only.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer the draft policy until the prior meeting transcript is reviewed, and allow naming for living individuals or whole facilities where warranted
side_b_arguments: The draft policy did not accurately reflect the board's previous discussion, making immediate debate unproductive without the transcript.
Blanket prohibitions on naming entire buildings or honoring living individuals could prevent future honors.
conflicts.resolution: Reckhow's motion to withdraw the item failed 0-5 after Jacobs reversed her second; the board later answered the County Attorney's six policy questions with mixed views (Foster supporting naming for living individuals, Jacobs opposing; Reckhow opposing a strict limit to interior features) and directed staff to return a revised draft.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-05-11 7:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Elected-Official Voting Seat on the Restructured Durham Workforce Development Board (Item 15-407)
conflicts.summary: The board split 3-2 over whether to adopt staff-recommended Option 1 (Schedule B1), which replaced elected-official voting representation on the Durham Workforce Development Board with non-voting liaisons, versus Option B2 retaining a voting seat.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt Option 1 (Schedule B1) as recommended by staff, making the city and county elected-body appointees non-voting liaisons on a 25-member board.
side_a_arguments: Option 1 follows staff's recommended structure under the transition from WIA to WIOA.
The county already holds appointments on the board including vocational rehabilitation and educational slots such as Durham Technical Community College.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose Option 1 and preserve a voting elected-official voice (Option B2) to advocate directly for jobs and workforce development.
side_b_arguments: Job creation and employment opportunities are a top campaign and policy priority for county commissioners, so the county should not voluntarily give up its voting voice on the Workforce Development Board.
Option B2 would allow a voting board member slot alongside non-voting liaisons.
conflicts.resolution: Option 1 (Schedule B1) passed 3-2 by voice vote (Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. plus one additional commissioner in favor; Michael D. Page and one additional commissioner opposed, with Brenda A. Howerton having queried Option B2 before the vote).

conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 0-5)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (0-5)

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-05-09 7:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Changing Payment Timing for State-Mandated Water Quality Nutrient Offset Fees (Item 16-1034)
conflicts.summary: The board split 3-2 on whether to relax Durham's unwritten practice of requiring state-mandated water quality nutrient offset payments prior to land disturbance permit issuance, balancing developer cash-flow burdens after 2014 state fee increases against risks of incomplete subdivision infrastructure.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve developer-proposed timing change for nutrient offset fee payments
side_a_arguments: Requiring payment at site plan/land disturbance permit issuance was an unwritten practice rather than a statute or ordinance.

Late-2014 NC Division of Environmental Quality fee increases (tripling phosphorus rates) made upfront payment unnecessarily burdensome, whereas other infrastructure certifications occur later before certificates of occupancy.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain upfront payment prior to land disturbance permit issuance due to developer cash-flow risks
side_b_arguments: Changing payment timing to address developer cash-flow issues raises concern given past developments where residents were left with unfinished infrastructure.
Upfront payment prior to land disturbance permit issuance ensured compliance before construction proceeded.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to approve Item 16-1034 passed 3-2 on a voice vote moved by Fred Foster Jr. and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton; one additional commissioner voted Aye and two voted Nay among Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs, though individual voice-vote names were not recorded in the transcript.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Tax Administrator Market-Value Salary Adjustment ($120,500) and Insurance Credit
conflicts.summary: The Board divided 3-2 over bringing the Tax Administrator to market value at $120,500 in addition to applying two years of insurance credit, with a dissenter arguing the extra pay was unfair to other county employees.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve both the $120,500 market-value salary adjustment and two years of insurance credit for the Tax Administrator.
side_a_arguments: Adjusts the Tax Administrator's compensation to market value alongside the two-year insurance credit.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support the insurance credit but oppose the additional market salary adjustment as unfair to other employees.
side_b_arguments: Treating one appointed official differently with extra pay beyond standard increases undermines fairness toward the rest of the county workforce.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 3-2 by voice vote (confirmed Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; the third Aye and two Nays among Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, and Fred Foster Jr. were not named in the transcript).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Process and Oversight Organization for Joint County-City-DPS Youth Initiative MOU (Consent Item G)
conflicts.summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. pulled Consent Item G to oppose the interlocal MOU establishing oversight for a joint youth initiative with the City of Durham and Durham Public Schools, whereas Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and the majority urged moving forward after lengthy interlocal negotiations.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the negotiated MOU among Durham County, the City, and DPS to coordinate disconnected youth services while scheduling follow-up on community input and future budget structure.
side_a_arguments: Both the IBM and MDC studies identified disconnected youth services in Durham needing stronger coordination.
Negotiating the MOU among Durham Public Schools, the City, and the County took a long time and should not be stalled.
Broader process concerns and community input can be reviewed at the upcoming Board retreat and during the upcoming FY15 budget cycle.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the MOU because the selection process and oversight organization are unsatisfactory.
side_b_arguments: Did not support the process used to develop the oversight structure.
Did not support the specific organization designated to have oversight over the youth initiative.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to approve Consent Item G passed 4-1 (Ayes: Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: Fred Foster Jr.), with Chair Page adding the broader coordination process to the Board retreat agenda.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Appropriation of $1,000 Walmart Foundation Grant for Sheriff's Project Lifesaver Program (Item P)
conflicts.summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow pulled consent item P for discussion with Sheriff's Office staff; Reckhow subsequently moved approval and the item passed 4-1 with Foster voting Nay.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the $1,000 Walmart Foundation grant budget amendment for Project Lifesaver.
side_a_arguments: Staff confirmed Project Lifesaver program information is currently available to residents on the Sheriff's Department website.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose approving the budget amendment as presented.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. raised questions and concerns regarding the item after pulling it from consent (substantive mid-item exchange omitted in transcript gap).
conflicts.resolution: Budget ordinance amendment 14 BCC 0031 passed 4-1.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Bahama Volunteer Fire Department $50,859 Brush Truck Chassis Replacement (Item Q)
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over spending $50,859 from the Bahama Fire Tax fund balance to replace the chassis on a 2004 brush truck rather than purchasing a new vehicle.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the $50,859 chassis replacement while pursuing a unified VFD capital improvement plan.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners should defer to fire department fleet expertise on apparatus maintenance.
Fire staff testified the truck body lasts 20–25 years while a chassis lasts 9–12 years, making a two-chassis lifecycle cost-effective compared to ~$100,000 for a new brush truck.
Ellen W. Reckhow urged developing a unified capital improvement plan across all volunteer fire departments to address vehicles over 20 years old.
conflicts.side_b_position: Buy a new vehicle instead of repairing a 2004 brush truck.
side_b_arguments: Fred Foster Jr. argued the 2004 truck had passed its expected service life and spending $50,859 on a chassis without a long-range cost-comparison study risked 'buying more trouble' for taxpayers.
conflicts.resolution: Budget ordinance amendment 14 BCC 0032 passed 4-1.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Deferral of Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Appointment for Term-Limit Policy Review
conflicts.summary: The Board divided 4-1 on deferring the RDU Airport Authority appointment so commissioners could review their appointment term-limit rules at a work session rather than voting immediately.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer the RDU Airport Authority appointment to review board appointment rules at a work session
side_a_arguments: Commissioners had unresolved questions about amending or suspending board appointment term-limit guidelines for an applicant seeking reappointment.
The current appointment policy no longer contained the historical escape clause, warranting a deliberate work-session review rather than an ad-hoc decision during regular balloting.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose deferral and proceed without delaying the RDU Airport Authority appointment
side_b_arguments: Chair Fred Foster Jr. voted against deferring the appointment slate at the meeting.
conflicts.resolution: Deferral passed 4-1, postponing the RDU Airport Authority appointment to the February 4, 2013 Worksession.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-13 7:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Board Communication, Equity Across Communities, and Sidewalk Maintenance Package (Item 15-383)
conflicts.summary: Before voting unanimously to approve Item 15-383, commissioners disagreed over staff information distribution, why Solterra Way / Forest View Elementary was prioritized without appearing on the general list, and how to ensure equitable sidewalk investments and maintenance resources across all Durham communities.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support approving the three-item sidewalk maintenance package (including Forest View / Solterra Way and a countywide school pedestrian connectivity plan), clarifying that separate NCDOT funding pots drove the item.
side_a_arguments: Item 13 on the priority list (Randolph Road sidewalk from Pickett Road to Irwin Road) is funded from a different NCDOT pot than the Solterra Way project.
The three-item package pairs immediate action with a comprehensive plan for improved pedestrian connectivity focused on school facilities throughout Durham County.
conflicts.side_b_position: Express discomfort with one-commissioner staff communications, lack of awareness of NCDOT funding pots in other neighborhoods, and potential unfunded sidewalk maintenance liabilities.
side_b_arguments: Sending staff information to a single commissioner leaves the rest of the Board out of the loop; all materials should be distributed to the entire Board.

While Irwin and Randolph Roads need pedestrian safety measures, Durham County must inform other communities of available DOT funding pots and ensure resources are distributed equitably across the county.
Taking on sidewalk maintenance requires mobilizing dedicated maintenance funding before sidewalks deteriorate.
conflicts.resolution: The Board unanimously passed the three-item Item 15-383 package by voice vote, and Chair Page appointed Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton to a committee to advance the broader policy and resource framework.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-08-03 9:00 AM - Worksession
conflicts.issue: Board Oversight and Response to Durham County Jail Lockbacks and Audit Demands
conflicts.summary: Commissioners disagreed over how proactively the Board of County Commissioners should intervene with the Sheriff regarding prolonged jail lockbacks, inmate complaints, and community demands for an independent audit.
conflicts.side_a_position: Hold direct discussions with the Sheriff on inmate conditions and pursue constructive outside review or technical assistance.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners have a responsibility to respond to citizen and inmate complaints about excessive idle time during lockbacks and deteriorating conditions.

Inviting a nationally recognized body such as the Bureau of Justice Assistance or National Institute of Corrections for technical assistance would be better received and more constructive than a punitive audit.
conflicts.side_b_position: Recognize the Sheriff's independent authority as an elected official and avoid repeating adversarial confrontations over security measures.
side_b_arguments: The County Commissioners do not control jail operations because the Sheriff is an independently elected official.
The Sheriff implemented lockbacks to protect staff and inmates amid gang-related safety threats, and repeated questioning without new facts will not change conditions.
conflicts.resolution: Chair Page concluded the discussion by noting staff had direction on next steps and the board would revisit the matter with the Sheriff in closed session; no formal vote was taken.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-06 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: County Sidewalk Maintenance Responsibility and Geographic Equity (Forest View / Solterra vs. Other Communities)
conflicts.summary: Commissioners debated whether Durham County should adopt an interim policy accepting long-term maintenance for NCDOT-funded school sidewalks or act only on the urgent Forest View Elementary / Solterra Way offer while addressing equity concerns across other county corridors.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support a limited interim policy accepting long-term maintenance when NCDOT constructs sidewalks near county schools outside city limits, enabling immediate acceptance of the Forest View / Irwin-Randolph safety project before NCDOT's deadline.
side_a_arguments: NCDOT requires a decision by late April to spend funds by June and will not proceed without a local government maintenance commitment.
A narrow interim policy limited to NCDOT-funded school connections outside city limits addresses urgent student safety while leaving broader policy coordination for DPS and the City of Durham.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question why this specific intersection was prioritized over other underserved areas and warn against taking on open-ended maintenance obligations without assurances for other communities.
side_b_arguments: Other communities such as Cook Road also need pedestrian and safety improvements, and a policy without written assurances could leave them behind.
Approving a standalone resolution for Solterra on April 13 would avoid rushing a broader countywide policy before full multi-jurisdictional review.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken at the work session; staff was directed to get written scope confirmation from NCDOT and bring back both a draft resolution and a minimal draft policy for the April 13, 2015 regular session.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Chair Appointment Authority vs. Suspending Board Rules for Operation Breakthrough Seat Swap
conflicts.summary: Commissioners Michael D. Page and Ellen W. Reckhow clashed with Chair Fred Foster Jr. and the County Attorney over whether the Board could immediately swap Reckhow out of the Operation Breakthrough Board by suspending its rules rather than awaiting a new Chair appointment or work-session rule amendment.
conflicts.side_a_position: Treat commissioner board swaps as routine and suspend Board rules to enact the Operation Breakthrough swap immediately
side_a_arguments: Commissioner seat swaps for scheduling convenience or subject-matter alignment have historically been treated as routine the same evening.
Under Robert's Rules of Order, voluntarily adopted Board rules that do not violate state or local law can be suspended by Board vote, as the Board routinely does at work sessions.
conflicts.side_b_position: Preserve Chair appointment authority and avoid amending or suspending external-effect rules mid-meeting without work-session review
side_b_arguments: Board rules assign Operation Breakthrough appointments to the Chair, subject to Board ratification.
The County Attorney advised that under Robert's Rules, rules granting external authority beyond meeting procedure cannot be suspended—only amended after prior work-session discussion.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a 5-0 compromise motion allowing Michael D. Page to continue serving on Operation Breakthrough (covering the upcoming Thursday meeting) until the matter returns before the Board for formal reconsideration.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-11-28 7:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Surplus Property Disposal Policy vs. City Affordable Housing Conveyance (518 Boone Street and 704 Eva Street)
conflicts.summary: Following upset bids on surplus county lots at 518 Boone Street and 704 Eva Street, a policy tension arose over whether the County should reject private high bids to convey the parcels to the City of Durham for deed-restricted affordable housing, or honor the county's existing upset-bid guidelines. After splitting the two lots, commissioners voted 4-1 to award 518 Boone Street to private bidder Joshua Jensen and 5-0 to convey 704 Eva Street to the City.
conflicts.side_a_position: Honor the upset-bid process for 518 Boone Street by accepting Joshua Jensen's $60,000 high bid given his commitment to Section 8 housing, while conveying 704 Eva Street to the City.
side_a_arguments: Under county surplus property guidelines, once a bid is placed on a parcel it is no longer eligible for $10 nonprofit conveyance and follows the upset-bid process.

Joshua Jensen publicly committed to developing Section 8 / affordable housing on 518 Boone Street, and the county had begun the upset-bid process before the City's updated affordable housing policy took effect.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject private bids and convey the surplus lots to the City of Durham so statutory covenants can guarantee long-term affordable housing.
side_b_arguments: In a standard county upset-bid sale, the County cannot restrict whether a private buyer holds the lot or develops market-rate housing.
The City of Durham can convey parcels under state statutes that attach binding affordability restrictions in perpetuity through an RFP to affordable housing developers.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-1 to sell 518 Boone Street to Joshua Jensen for $60,000 (with Reckhow moving and Howerton seconding; the single dissenting commissioner was not identified by name in the voice vote) and passed 5-0 to sell 704 Eva Street to the City of Durham for $3,391.30.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-12-07 9:00 AM - Workession
conflicts.issue: Timing and Advisability of a County Resolution Opposing the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP)
conflicts.summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. asked staff to prepare a formal BOCC resolution opposing the federal Trans-Pacific Partnership trade deal based on labor union concerns, whereas Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and other commissioners urged deferring action until all business and labor stakeholders could provide input at an upcoming forum.
conflicts.side_a_position: Move forward with staff drafting an anti-TPP resolution for the Board to consider.
side_a_arguments: Labor unions and the AFL-CIO-affiliated NC Alliance for Retired Americans warn TPP will harm local manufacturing workers and erode Durham County's tax base.
Foreign investor provisions could limit local decision-making, and Wake County is already advancing a similar measure.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold off on a resolution until the Board receives broader education and input from business, RTP, and federal stakeholders.
side_b_arguments: TPP is complex and RTP companies as well as Congressman David Price have expressed support for it.
The Foreign Trade Zone board chaired by Tom White is organizing an informational forum in the coming months, so commissioners should hear all sides before adopting a formal position.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; commissioners directed staff to research the issue and identify stakeholders to inform the Board before any future action.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-03-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
conflicts.issue: Whether Durham County Should Accept Long-Term Sidewalk Maintenance Costs for NCDOT-Funded School Sidewalks
conflicts.summary: During the second work session review of sidewalk maintenance policy, commissioners disagreed over whether the county should adopt a limited policy to accept long-term maintenance for state-funded sidewalks near schools outside city limits or avoid taking on new taxpayer-funded maintenance obligations amid competing neighborhood needs.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt a limited policy accepting county maintenance when NCDOT pays to build sidewalks linking school sites to adjacent neighborhoods, aligning with strategic plan health and safety goals.
side_a_arguments: By building sidewalks around schools, Durham County is already in the sidewalk business, and leaving 100 homes across from Forest View Elementary without a safe crossing undermines strategic plan health and safety goals.
Limiting the policy to NCDOT-funded construction at school sites outside city limits caps county exposure while unlocking state construction funds.
conflicts.side_b_position: Caution against taking on unbudgeted taxpayer maintenance obligations and highlight unresolved sidewalk needs raised for years in other neighborhoods.
side_b_arguments: Long-term sidewalk maintenance imposes new costs on county taxpayers without dedicated budget funding, mirroring budget pressures faced by the City of Durham.
Residents such as Delma White have petitioned for years for sidewalks along corridors like Little River Road without action, so all communities must be considered fairly.
conflicts.resolution: No vote was taken at the March 2 work session; the policy returned for further work session deliberation on April 6 and formal action on April 13, 2015.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: 3% Salary Increase for Four Appointed Officials
conflicts.summary: After meeting in closed session to evaluate four appointed positions (County Attorney, Tax Assessor, Clerk to the Board, and Register of Deeds), the Board split 4-1 on granting all four a 3% increase.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support granting a 3% salary increase to all four appointed officials.
side_a_arguments: Board majority recommended the 3% compensation increase following closed-session evaluations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the 3% increase for all four appointed positions.
side_b_arguments: Single Nay voice vote cast without extended floor remarks; exact dissenting member not named in audio transcript.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-1 by voice vote (confirmed Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs; the remaining two Ayes and single Nay among Michael D. Page, Fred Foster Jr., and Ellen W. Reckhow were not named in the transcript).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Scope of Staff Modifications to Paid Fire Study Recommendations (Items 52, 58–61)
conflicts.summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. questioned why Interim County Manager Lee Worsley modified or recommended taking no immediate action on several Fire Study consultant recommendations after the County paid for the study, whereas Worsley and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow defended further staff vetting—particularly given New Hope Fire District concerns.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt Interim Manager Worsley's amended Fire Study recommendations, pausing/vetting complex consolidation items (Items 58–61) with stakeholders such as New Hope Fire District.
side_a_arguments: The consultant's scope did not permit parcel-level operational analysis (such as New Hope areas lacking hydrants and relying on tanker/pumper trucks, or state truck-funding issues).
New Hope Fire District felt left out of earlier Durham fire chief discussions and must be engaged before deciding on city/county service transfers.
conflicts.side_b_position: Questioned why staff was changing or dropping recommendations from a paid consultant study that was expected to be vetted before Board presentation.
side_b_arguments: County taxpayers paid consultants to study these items and bring vetted recommendations rather than having staff reverse or halt them.
Questioned who would conduct the additional comprehensive analysis for Items 58–61 if not the paid consultants.
conflicts.resolution: Following public hearing remarks from Bahama Fire Chief Lynn Needham, the Board unanimously approved (5-0) the Fire Study recommendations as amended by Interim Manager Worsley.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: UDO Text Amendment Article 6 Density Revisions (TC1200012)
conflicts.summary: The Board split 4-1 by voice vote on approving UDO Text Amendment TC1200012 modifying Article 6 density standards following public hearing remarks by applicant Ron Horvath.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve UDO Text Amendment TC1200012 modifying Article 6 density provisions.
side_a_arguments: Applicant argued developments face cumulative site constraints from 20–24% tree coverage, 20% stormwater requirements, and impervious limits.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose approval of TC1200012 (single Nay vote on voice vote; dissenter not named in transcript).
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-1 by voice vote (moved by Brenda A. Howerton, seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow; the other two Ayes and one Nay among Michael D. Page, Fred Foster Jr., and Wendy Jacobs were not named on microphone).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Appointment and Employment Contract of County Manager Wendell M. Davis
conflicts.summary: Following a personnel closed session, the Board split 4-1 by voice vote on appointing Wendell M. Davis as County Manager effective April 14, 2014 at $198,800 and approving his employment contract.
conflicts.side_a_position: Appoint Wendell M. Davis as County Manager effective April 14, 2014 at $198,800 and approve his employment contract.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the appointment/contract (single Nay vote on voice vote; dissenter not named in transcript).
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-1 by voice vote (moved by Fred Foster Jr., seconded by Brenda A. Howerton; the other two Ayes and single Nay among Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs were not named on microphone).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
conflicts.issue: Term-Limit Exception for Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Appointment
conflicts.summary: Commissioners clashed over whether to suspend or waive the Board's appointment term-limit rules to place an incumbent/former appointee on the RDU Airport Authority ballot despite having exceeded term limits.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow an exception to place the termed-out candidate on the ballot
side_a_arguments: Because RDU Airport Authority terms are only two years and officer progression takes multiple terms, a member can reach the threshold of becoming chair only after extended tenure.
The Board previously allowed a fifth two-year term (10 years total) for Steve Toler so he could serve as RDU chair.
conflicts.side_b_position: Enforce adopted term-limit rules and consider only eligible applicants
side_b_arguments: Supporting an applicant who has already exceeded term limits violates the Board's adopted appointment rules in bad faith.
Other qualified citizens applied in accordance with the rules and deserve fair consideration rather than being displaced for an incumbent.
conflicts.resolution: Chair Fred Foster Jr. offered to entertain a motion to add the name, which Ellen W. Reckhow declined to pursue; the Board voted exclusively among the six eligible applicants on the ballot and elected Clay C. Wheeler on the second ballot.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-11-07 9:00 AM - Worksession
conflicts.issue: Offline $50,000 Funding Request for Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative Health Task Force
conflicts.summary: Commissioners disagreed over how to respond to an unvetted, last-minute $50,000 request for an adult health/outreach position under the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative—weighing potential duplication with existing initiatives and preference for a broader paramedicine model against urgent support for low-income residents.
conflicts.side_a_position: Hold off on approving an offline $50,000 request until service gaps, annualization impacts, and broader alternatives such as community paramedicine are clarified.
side_a_arguments: Offline mid-year requests risk creating recurring annualized obligations in future county budgets without prior budget vetting.

The City funded a community liaison police officer (Officer Jennifer) and the County has already committed $609,000 to youth initiatives (Cure Violence and My Brother's Keeper) alongside EDCI and Durham Connects.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted that an evidence-based paramedicine follow-up model could serve a much wider area of the county than a single census tract.
conflicts.side_b_position: Commit promptly to the $50,000 request to address adult service gaps, mental health needs, and poverty in the target neighborhood without unnecessary delay.
side_b_arguments: The $50,000 request is minor relative to the county's multi-million-dollar fund balance and targets adults rather than children.
Community residents and congregations reported not seeing existing outreach workers on the ground, and serious mental health and service-access gaps persist daily.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; staff committed to delivering an explanatory memorandum by the end of the week detailing existing service coverage, gaps, and paramedicine options ahead of the November 28 meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-09-12 7:00 PM
conflicts.issue: City-County Cost Allocation and E-911 Parking Space Assignment at New Durham Police Headquarters
conflicts.summary: During the special session briefing on the City's $71 million Police Headquarters and joint E-911 Center, county commissioners pushed back against the City's proposed 911 cost allocation and the assignment of 80 parking spaces to 911 operations.
conflicts.side_a_position: Apply the existing City-County E-911 MOU cost allocation (roughly 20% of building square footage plus a separate garage allocation, totaling $13.9 million for 911 and $2.9 million from the County) and provide 80 parking spaces for 911 staff overlap.
side_a_arguments: Dedicated 911 square footage under the existing MOU came to roughly 20% of the building, with a separate parking garage formula layered in.
Half of 911 shift workers arrive while the outgoing shift is still present, requiring overlapping employee parking capacity.
City staff noted they could explain the current allocation math right away, but revisiting the broader MOU requires City Manager and City Council guidance.
conflicts.side_b_position: Scrutinize the cost-allocation disparity (19.5%–20% of cost versus 17.2% of building share) and reduce the 80-space parking allocation before finalizing county obligations.
side_b_arguments: Dividing the $13.9 million 911 budget by the $71 million total project cost yields ~19.5%, exceeding the ~17.2% physical share of the building.

Under emergency 12-hour shifts (6 AM and 6 PM) or staggered shifts, many other headquarters employees are not in the building simultaneously, making 80 spaces assigned to 911 appear to be an overreach.
conflicts.resolution: No vote was taken; commissioners requested a focused work-session review of the cost-allocation formula and potential MOU revisions in coordination with the City.

conflicts.side_a_position: Appoint Lee Worsley as Interim County Manager effective February 1, 2014 until a permanent manager starts, and approve his employment agreement (three Ayes among the four present commissioners).
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the interim appointment and employment agreement (one Nay among the four present commissioners; individual dissenter not named in transcript).
conflicts.resolution: Both motions passed 3-1 by voice vote ('Three in favor. One nay') without individual voters named on microphone; Chair Michael D. Page was excused absent.

conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the $400,000 incentive with local job/NCCU hospitality provisos and establish future historic-preservation grant criteria.

Including provisos for NCCU Hospitality Program, JobLink, and Work First directs job opportunities to Durham residents.
A follow-up resolution will establish clear criteria for future community development grants for historic preservation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed the $400,000 incentive motion (single Nay vote on 4-1 voice vote).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) Matching Grants ($41,370) vs. Revenue-Generating and Basic-Needs Priorities
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over approving $41,370 in DOST matching grants for four community park and trail projects (including Horton Grove, Sandy Creek Park, and Briggs Avenue community garden gazebo).
conflicts.side_a_position: Honor the prior fiscal year's budget allocation and citizen committee process by approving the four vetted DOST matching grants totaling $41,370.
side_a_arguments: The County previously budgeted roughly $77,000 for the program and invited citizens and nonprofits to submit elaborate proposals in good faith after a two-year suspension.
Projects like Sandy Creek Park and the Briggs Avenue gazebo reclaim unsafe spaces, make parks handicap-accessible, and support physical fitness and obesity prevention.

Funds could instead support revenue-producing sports tourism such as recruiting an AAU track and field meet (generating $10M+ annually in Greensboro) or addressing food and housing needs.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-11-28 7:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Surplus Property Disposal Policy vs. City Affordable Housing Conveyance (518 Boone Street and 704 Eva Street)
disagreements.summary: Following upset bids on surplus county lots at 518 Boone Street and 704 Eva Street, a policy tension arose over whether the County should reject private high bids to convey the parcels to the City of Durham for deed-restricted affordable housing, or honor the county's existing upset-bid guidelines. After splitting the two lots, commissioners voted 4-1 to award 518 Boone Street to private bidder Joshua Jensen and 5-0 to convey 704 Eva Street to the City.
disagreements.side_a_position: Honor the upset-bid process for 518 Boone Street by accepting Joshua Jensen's $60,000 high bid given his commitment to Section 8 housing, while conveying 704 Eva Street to the City.
side_a_arguments: Under county surplus property guidelines, once a bid is placed on a parcel it is no longer eligible for $10 nonprofit conveyance and follows the upset-bid process.

Joshua Jensen publicly committed to developing Section 8 / affordable housing on 518 Boone Street, and the county had begun the upset-bid process before the City's updated affordable housing policy took effect.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject private bids and convey the surplus lots to the City of Durham so statutory covenants can guarantee long-term affordable housing.
side_b_arguments: In a standard county upset-bid sale, the County cannot restrict whether a private buyer holds the lot or develops market-rate housing.
The City of Durham can convey parcels under state statutes that attach binding affordability restrictions in perpetuity through an RFP to affordable housing developers.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 to sell 518 Boone Street to Joshua Jensen for $60,000 (with Reckhow moving and Howerton seconding; the single dissenting commissioner was not identified by name in the voice vote) and passed 5-0 to sell 704 Eva Street to the City of Durham for $3,391.30.

Page with all five commissioners present, Chair Page read a joint community statement drafted with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs—alongside Durham Public Schools, Durham City Council, and Durham Tech—reaffirming Durham County's commitment to inclusivity and protection of immigrants, refugees, and all residents from discrimination or harassment. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-11-07 9:00 AM - Worksession
disagreements.issue: Offline $50,000 Funding Request for Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative Health Task Force
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed over how to respond to an unvetted, last-minute $50,000 request for an adult health/outreach position under the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative—weighing potential duplication with existing initiatives and preference for a broader paramedicine model against urgent support for low-income residents.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold off on approving an offline $50,000 request until service gaps, annualization impacts, and broader alternatives such as community paramedicine are clarified.
side_a_arguments: Offline mid-year requests risk creating recurring annualized obligations in future county budgets without prior budget vetting.

The City funded a community liaison police officer (Officer Jennifer) and the County has already committed $609,000 to youth initiatives (Cure Violence and My Brother's Keeper) alongside EDCI and Durham Connects.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted that an evidence-based paramedicine follow-up model could serve a much wider area of the county than a single census tract.
disagreements.side_b_position: Commit promptly to the $50,000 request to address adult service gaps, mental health needs, and poverty in the target neighborhood without unnecessary delay.
side_b_arguments: The $50,000 request is minor relative to the county's multi-million-dollar fund balance and targets adults rather than children.
Community residents and congregations reported not seeing existing outreach workers on the ground, and serious mental health and service-access gaps persist daily.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; staff committed to delivering an explanatory memorandum by the end of the week detailing existing service coverage, gaps, and paramedicine options ahead of the November 28 meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-10-24 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 24, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with Deputy County Manager Gail Harris filling in for the County Manager, the Board opened with announcements on the November 8 Durham Youth Work Summit, expanded early voting sites opening October 27, and Solid Waste's rollout of 18-gallon blue recycling carts. Commissioners approved four sets of June and October 2016 minutes (5-0), honored retiring Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers after 20 years of county service, and approved the consent agenda (5-0, highlighting Item 16-1329 for an integrated domestic violence response grant). Following public hearings at which Dr. Lavonia Allison spoke, the Board voted 5-0 to approve Item 16-1331 authorizing Public Finance Authority educational revenue bonds of up to $15 million for Kestrel Heights Charter School to purchase its facility—with no county fiscal liability and a request from Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow for an updated charter school report—and voted 5-0 to approve the FY 2018 Section 5311 Community Transportation administrative grant ($13,311 local match) before announcing board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Retirement Resolution for Delphine Sellers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced the Durham Youth Work Summit, additional early voting sites opening October 27 through November 5 (including The Frontier, Greater Emmanuel Temple, and Ivy Community Center), and Solid Waste's rollout of blue recycling carts in unincorporated Durham. The Board unanimously approved four sets of minutes (June 1, June 16, October 4, and October 10, 2016) and presented a retirement resolution honoring Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers for her career since 1996.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1275 through 16-1339)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled, a commissioner commended Item 16-1329, a DSS grant to implement an integrated domestic violence response system program. The Board unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 16-1331 — Public Finance Authority Revenue Bonds for Kestrel Heights School (Up to $15M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bond counsel Mary Nash Rusher and County Attorney Lowell Siler explained that the Wisconsin-based Public Finance Authority conduit bond (expected ~$13 million, capped at $15 million) would allow Kestrel Heights Charter School to purchase its existing building with zero fiscal impact on Durham County. Dr. Lavonia Allison raised data questions during the public hearing, and commissioners endorsed Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's request for an updated annual report on charter schools before approving the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2018 Federal Section 5311 Community Transportation Grant ($13,311 Match)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff presented the annual NCDOT-administered Section 5311 administrative-cost grant requiring a $13,311 county local match, unchanged from the prior year. Dr. Lavonia Allison complimented Access services while asking what administrative funds cover and commenting on Board of Elections staffing; the Board approved the grant application unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Hurricane Matthew Relief Announcement and Board/Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner announced GoTriangle's partnership with WRAL, United Way, and RDU Airport to collect Hurricane Matthew relief supplies. The County Attorney then announced citizen appointments to the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau, Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, Memorial Stadium Authority, and Women's Commission.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-10-10 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 10, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page—with Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs present as a three-member quorum while Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow were on excused absences granted September 26—the Board approved the September 26, 2016 minutes (3-0), celebrated national IT recognition for Durham County's IT Services and Technology Department, proclaimed End Hunger Week, and approved the consent agenda (3-0, noting Item 16-1306 for the library's Teen Tech Learning Lab). Following public hearings with no speakers signed up, the Board voted unanimously 3-0 to approve closeout reports for two federal grants: the FY 2011 CDBG Scattered Site Housing Program ($400,000 HUD plus ~$49,300 HOME funds) and the FY 2012 CDBG Rougemont Critical Water Infrastructure Improvement Project ($600,000 HUD plus state DEQ and county funds). Finally, the Board voted 3-0 on the consolidated East End Land Use Analysis to adopt Comprehensive Plan Amendment A1600005, Zoning Map Change Ordinance Z1600009 (rezoning 1215 Lynn Road from RS-20 to RU-5), and the statutory consistency statement before receiving a brief Hurricane Matthew EOC update from the County Manager.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Minutes Approval, IT Award, and End Hunger Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow absent on excused leave, Chair Page, Vice Chair Howerton, and Commissioner Jacobs formed a three-member quorum. Following announcements on an October 11 education town hall and October 13 Board of Health rabies rule hearing, the Board approved the September 26 minutes (3-0), recognized CIO Greg Marrow and the IT department for a national local-government IT award, and proclaimed End Hunger Week alongside DSS Director Michael Becketts.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1245 through 16-1327)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No consent items were pulled, though a commissioner highlighted Item 16-1306, a State Library of North Carolina grant funding Durham County Library's Teen Tech Learning Lab to employ high school students as homework tutors. Vice Chair Howerton moved and Commissioner Jacobs seconded approval of the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Closeout of FY 2011 CDBG Scattered Site Housing Grant (11-C-2309)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Drew Cummings presented the closeout report for the FY 2011 CDBG Scattered Site Housing Program ($400,000 HUD CDBG grant plus ~$49,300 City-County HOME funds for rehabilitating/reconstructing up to five deteriorated homes and emergency repairs on up to eight homes). With 92% expended and full completion expected ahead of the November 18, 2016 Commerce deadline with zero funds returned, the Board held a public hearing with no speakers and approved the closeout.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Closeout of FY 2012 CDBG Infrastructure Grant (06D-2405 — Rougemont Water)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Drew Cummings and Joe Pierce presented the closeout for the Rougemont Critical Water Infrastructure Improvement Project ($600,000 HUD CDBG, NC Department of Environmental Quality grants, and ~$1.5 million in additional project funding) ahead of the November 10, 2016 closeout deadline. Commissioners noted strong appreciation from Rougemont residents and approved the closeout report unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated East End Land Use Analysis (A1600005 and Z1600009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning's Lisa Miller presented Future Land Use Map Amendment A1600005 (affecting 12 parcels around NCDOT's East End Connector project) and Zoning Map Change Z1600009 (rezoning 1215 Lynn Road to a single Residential Urban 5 designation from RS-20/RU-5/CG). Following a public hearing with no speakers, Commissioner Jacobs moved and Vice Chair Howerton seconded approval of the plan amendment, zoning ordinance, and N.C.G.S. 153A-341 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: County Manager Hurricane Matthew Recovery Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager briefed the Board on weekend Emergency Operations Center operations and Hurricane Matthew response, thanking county staff and noting that Durham fared much better than neighboring eastern counties while promising a damage and mutual-aid briefing paper by the end of the week.

votes.notes: Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow were absent (excused on Sept 26); all three present members voted Aye.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-10-04 10:00 AM - Worksession (Tuesday meeting) 10:00 am
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 4, 2016 work session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (rescheduled to 10:00 AM so commissioners could attend the MED Week breakfast), the Board heard public comments requesting 1900–2016 Durham census records, supporting a North Carolina Central University (NCCU) light-rail station, urging 12-week paid parental and family caregiving leave, and questioning the timing of citizen comment before staff presentations. The Board voted 5-0 to suspend its rules and 5-0 to remove Jatinder Dhillon from the Women's Commission for excessive absences, then received informational updates from the Research Triangle Foundation on Park Center development, transit officials on adding an NCCU station ahead of engineering to preserve 50% federal FTA matching eligibility, Planning staff on two historic landmark cases including the Venable Center (LD1600002), and Tax staff on advancing from an eight-year octennial property reappraisal cycle toward a three-to-four-year cycle. Commissioners also reviewed draft paid parental leave, donated family leave, and $15/hour county minimum wage proposals (affecting ~800 hourly staff, with EMS and Detention targeted for January 1 rollout) before voting 5-0 to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments (Census Records, NCCU Transit Stop, Paid Parental Leave, and Comment Order)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: James Chavis requested funding to obtain 1900–2016 Durham census records, while other speakers backed adding an NCCU transit stop to connect campuses and urged adopting 12 weeks of paid parental leave without penalizing dual-county-employee parents or omitting broader FMLA caregiving needs. Jacqueline Wagstaff also criticized holding public comment before staff presentations on Urban Ministries and transit.

agenda_items.title: Item 2: Removal of Jatinder Dhillon from the Women's Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because Jatinder Dhillon did not meet attendance requirements (missing more than 50% of meetings in a calendar year or exceeding consecutive absence thresholds), the Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules and remove her from the Women's Commission.

agenda_items.title: Research Triangle Foundation Park Center Update and NCCU Light Rail Station Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Research Triangle Foundation representatives Bob Winston and John Brantley updated commissioners on the Park Center development and upcoming construction management discussions. Transit presenters then asked the Board to recommend to the MPO adding an NCCU light-rail station before entering the engineering phase so the station remains eligible for 50% FTA funding rather than 100% local cost; a subsequent midday portion of the digest was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Historic Landmark Cases (LD1600002 Venable Center) and Advancing the Octennial Reappraisal Cycle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reviewed two historic landmark items heading to City Council—one building/land designation (~$3,000 annual deferral) and LD1600002 (Venable Center at South Roxboro and East Pettigrew), seeking repeal of land-only designation and triggering ~$35,000 in back deferred taxes—with commissioners asking staff to verify tax figures. Tax Administration staff then presented a proposed resolution to move Durham County off its statutory eight-year reappraisal cycle (N.C.G.S. 105-286) toward a three-to-four-year cycle recommended by the Lincoln Institute and IAAO.

agenda_items.title: Paid Parental Leave, Donated Family Leave, and $15/Hour Minimum Wage Proposals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed three distinct leave policies (including sharing 12 weeks of paid parental coverage between dual-employee parents and allowing donated leave bank contributions at exit) and examined raising the county minimum hourly pay to $15/hour across ~800 hourly employees. The County Manager highlighted EMS and Detention Officers as the highest-impact retention areas, targeting January 1 implementation via over-hire budget capacity.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the County Attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege. Upon returning with three commissioners present at 4:19 PM, the Board reported giving directions to staff and adjourned.

votes.notes: Chair Page announced 'motion carries unanimously.'
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend the rules in a work session to take action removing a citizen from the Women's Commission due to poor attendance.

votes.notes: Chair Page announced 'motion carries unanimously.'
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to remove Jatinder Dhillon from the Women's Commission for violating attendance requirements.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn into closed session to consult with an attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

Page with all five commissioners present, the Board voted 5-0 to reschedule its October 4 work session start time from 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM for the MED Week breakfast and voted 5-0 to grant excused absences for Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-09-12 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: The September 12, 2016 Board of County Commissioners meeting—presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present—opened with a 5:00 PM special session reviewing Item 16-1271 (the City of Durham's $71 million new Police Headquarters Complex and joint City-County E-911 Communications Center, carrying a $2.9 million county 911 contribution) and downtown parking demands. Commissioners pushed back on the City's cost-allocation formula (questioning an effective 19.5%–20% share versus 17.2% of floor area and the assignment of 80 parking spaces to 911 despite staggered 12-hour shifts) and requested a focused work session to examine the formula and underlying MOU. Following the downtown parking discussion, the Board voted 5-0 to suspend its rules and 5-0 (moved by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr., seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-09-12 7:00 PM
disagreements.issue: City-County Cost Allocation and E-911 Parking Space Assignment at New Durham Police Headquarters
disagreements.summary: During the special session briefing on the City's $71 million Police Headquarters and joint E-911 Center, county commissioners pushed back against the City's proposed 911 cost allocation and the assignment of 80 parking spaces to 911 operations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Apply the existing City-County E-911 MOU cost allocation (roughly 20% of building square footage plus a separate garage allocation, totaling $13.9 million for 911 and $2.9 million from the County) and provide 80 parking spaces for 911 staff overlap.
side_a_arguments: Dedicated 911 square footage under the existing MOU came to roughly 20% of the building, with a separate parking garage formula layered in.
Half of 911 shift workers arrive while the outgoing shift is still present, requiring overlapping employee parking capacity.
City staff noted they could explain the current allocation math right away, but revisiting the broader MOU requires City Manager and City Council guidance.
disagreements.side_b_position: Scrutinize the cost-allocation disparity (19.5%–20% of cost versus 17.2% of building share) and reduce the 80-space parking allocation before finalizing county obligations.
side_b_arguments: Dividing the $13.9 million 911 budget by the $71 million total project cost yields ~19.5%, exceeding the ~17.2% physical share of the building.

Under emergency 12-hour shifts (6 AM and 6 PM) or staggered shifts, many other headquarters employees are not in the building simultaneously, making 80 spaces assigned to 911 appear to be an overreach.
disagreements.resolution: No vote was taken; commissioners requested a focused work-session review of the cost-allocation formula and potential MOU revisions in coordination with the City.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-09-06 9:00 AM - Worksession (Tuesday meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 6, 2016 Board of County Commissioners worksession, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided as commissioners reviewed employee deferred compensation options, property compensation for the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau (DCVB), and volunteer sheriff's deputy workers' compensation coverage. Staff and a state representative presented shifting Durham County's 457 deferred compensation plan to the State Treasurer's NC 457 Plan to transfer fiduciary liability to the state and consolidate employee portals with the 401(k) plan. Commissioners discussed three compensation options for DCVB after a 2011 $10 building conveyance failed due to statutory prohibitions on tourism development authorities owning real property and the county's decision to retain the building, directing staff to return with a budget recommendation for a three-year payout starting in FY 2017. The board also reviewed a resolution extending workers' compensation coverage to unpaid sworn volunteer sheriff's deputies, refined the 2017 legislative agenda (including aging services, public library funding, Medicaid expansion, and foster parent rates), and discussed launching a community paramedicine program with Duke Medicine; no formal votes or split disagreements occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Public Charge
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners opened the worksession, read the public charge, and noted a request to add an NCACC conference report at the end of the agenda. A commissioner noted needing to leave no later than 2:00 p.m., and members agreed to manage time accordingly.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Property Tax Assessment and Senior Exemption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident turning 77 addressed a more than 50 percent increase in property taxes over the prior year and asked for clarification regarding the $29,500 income limit for senior tax relief. Commissioners also asked staff to clarify county record retention comparisons raised during public comment.

agenda_items.title: NC 457 Deferred Compensation Plan Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A representative from the State Treasurer's Office presented the NC 457 deferred compensation plan as a potential replacement for Durham County's existing Nationwide/ICMA 457 plan. Shifting to the state-overseen plan would relieve Durham County of fiduciary liability, provide quarterly investment board oversight, and give employees a single website, representative, and call center alongside the state 401(k) plan.

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau (DCVB) Building Fair Compensation Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DCVB representative Shelley Green explained that although the board voted in November 2011 to convey the old building and visitor center to DCVB for $10 upon debt payoff, 2002 state legislation classifying tourism development authorities barred DCVB from owning real property, and the county later decided to keep the building. Commissioners discussed fair compensation options based on the $1,021,641 appraised value or DCVB's $1.2 million to $1.5 million investment; Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. favored options one or two over option three, while the board directed budget staff to evaluate paying out the lump sum over three years starting in FY 2017 and return next week.

agenda_items.title: Workers' Compensation Coverage for Unpaid Sworn Volunteer Sheriff's Deputies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Risk Manager David English and County Attorney Lowell Siler/Massey presented a resolution authorizing workers' compensation coverage for unpaid appointed and sworn volunteer reserve deputies in the Sheriff's Office. English explained that reserve deputies provide vital hospital detainee security and backfill coverage, and a manual records search back through the clerk's office showed no prior special resolution had been adopted to cover them.

agenda_items.title: 2017 Legislative Agenda and State Funding Goals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff reviewed legislative goal proposals for the 2017 General Assembly session, including aligning aging-in-place advocacy with the 2015–2019 North Carolina Aging Services Plan, Adult Protective Services funding, the Home and Community Care Block Grant, and optional Medicaid services. Additional proposals covered restoring state aid for public libraries to the pre-2011 level of $15.7 million (per Library Director Tammy Baggett), clarifying retirement system statutory language, supporting full Medicaid expansion (requested by Social Services Director Michael Becket), and raising foster parent payment rates that had remained flat since 2008 despite 12 percent inflation.

agenda_items.title: Community Paramedicine Program Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: EMS leadership and commissioners examined community paramedicine models from other counties (including New Hanover and Wake counties and Fort Worth, Texas) that cut non-emergency 911 calls and emergency room visits through 24- to 72-hour post-discharge follow-up and medication delivery. Commissioners discussed conducting a cost-benefit analysis relative to ambulance replacement costs and partnering with Duke Medicine leadership, including Kevin Sowers and Dr. Washington, as part of population health management.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-08-22 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 22, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Board of County Commissioners congratulated Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton on becoming NCACC President-elect, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow on joining the NCACC Board of Directors, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs on earning mentor status in the Local Elected Leadership Academy, and proclaimed September as National Recovery Month. The board unanimously (5-0) approved prior meeting minutes and the consent agenda after Commissioner Reckhow pulled Judicial Building renovation items (16-1232, 16-1240, and 16-1241) for a public design update from O'Brien/Atkins. Following public hearings, commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to adopt Comprehensive Plan amendments adding Compact Neighborhood tier tapering and affordable housing policies near future light rail stations, approve a zoning map change (Z1600005) for Moe's Tavern in Rougemont to allow restroom and community water connections, and adopt the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Corridor Plan. The meeting concluded with balloted board and commission appointments and a return to closed session before adjourning at 10:39 p.m., with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report, Public Charge, Pledge, and Commissioner Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting noting the board had met in closed session and would return afterward, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Commissioners recognized Brenda A. Howerton's swearing-in as NCACC President-elect, Ellen W. Reckhow's appointment to the NCACC Board of Directors, and Wendy Jacobs' mentor status recognition in the Local Elected Leadership Academy.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (April 4, May 9, and August 8, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered approval of minutes from the April 4, 2016 worksession and the May 9 and August 8, 2016 regular sessions. No corrections were raised.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Designating September as National Recovery Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented a proclamation designating September as National Recovery Month with the theme emphasizing behavioral health and addiction as public health medical conditions rather than solely criminal justice issues. Recipient Robert Thomas thanked the board and invited commissioners and community members to the recovery celebration at Durham Central Park.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1161 to 16-1241, Excluding Pulled Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow pulled items 16-1232, 16-1240, and 16-1241 regarding the Judicial Building Renovation Project to review updated architectural drawings for transparency before approving final funding amounts. The board approved the remainder of the consent agenda unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 16-1232, 16-1240, and 16-1241: Judicial Building Renovation Project Design Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Moved to the front of the discussion items out of respect for attending architects Josh and Kevin from O'Brien/Atkins, the board reviewed updated design renderings for the East Main Street courthouse/judicial building, including horizontal proportions, ground plaza openness, and sunscreens for southern exposure. Subsequent portions of the discussion and final action were omitted due to transcript digest middle truncation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Compact Neighborhood Tier Policy Updates (Item 16-1200)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented two Comprehensive Plan text amendments adding policies to taper compact neighborhood density outward from transit stations and formally incorporate the city-county affordable housing resolution for areas within a half-mile of future light rail stations. Staff noted the Planning Commission recommended approval 13-1, and no citizens signed up to speak at the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Moe's Tavern (Z1600005 / Item 16-1211)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Kyle Taylor presented Z1600005 to rezone a 0.455-acre rear portion of 12911 North Roxboro Road from RS-10 to Commercial Neighborhood (CN) within the rural tier and MLRB watershed overlay, the first rezoning under the Rougemont commercial node. Applicant representative Dan Jewell noted the rezoning would allow Moe's Tavern to add customer bathrooms and connect to the community water system.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Corridor Plan Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman with the Planning Department presented the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Corridor Plan prepared with GoTriangle for parallel adoption by Durham County and the City of Durham to preserve the transit alignment through development, subdivision, and rezoning review. Commissioners had been briefed earlier in the day and approved the plan without additional questions.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Return to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners corrected clerical errors on the printed appointment ballots and voted by ballot before resuming closed session briefly. Upon returning to open session, the County Attorney announced appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (Trisha Howard, Marjorie Lipscomb, Athena Jackson, Chase McGee), Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (Umar Mahameh, Selena Richards), Library Board of Trustees (Center of Chambers, Angela Wilson, Phillip Harris, Sean Miller), and Women's Commission (Joelle Carter, Sandra Howell).

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (April 4, May 9, and August 8, 2016)
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve minutes from the May 9, 2016 regular session, April 4, 2016 worksession, and August 8, 2016 regular session.

votes.item_title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Compact Neighborhood Tier Policy Updates (Item 16-1200)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Comprehensive Plan text amendments adding transition/tapering policies in compact neighborhoods and incorporating the half-mile light rail affordable housing resolution.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved rezoning 0.455 acres at 12911 North Roxboro Road from RS-10 to CN in the rural tier under the Rougemont commercial node.

votes.item_title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Corridor Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Corridor Plan with GoTriangle to preserve corridor right-of-way through development review.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-08-08 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 8, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved prior meeting minutes, the consent agenda (items 16-1085 through 16-1198), and a resolution authorizing Series 2016 General Obligation Refunding Bonds after a required public hearing on maturity date changes for bond anticipation notes. The board held a major public hearing on bond orders for a November 2016 General Obligation Bond Referendum not to exceed $170 million—comprising $90,870,000 for schools, $44,725,000 for libraries, $20,195,000 for Durham Technical Community College, and $14,210,000 for the Museum of Life and Science—hearing supportive testimony from Durham Tech and Durham Public Schools representatives before the truncated middle of the transcript. agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting, reviewed the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements included a joint DSS and NC Division of Aging and Adult Services community listening session on August 9 focusing on Adult Protective Services and guardianship.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (January 11, January 25, and July 11, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved minutes from the January 11, January 25, and July 11, 2016 regular sessions without amendments.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1085 to 16-1198)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow made a brief comment on item 16-1187 regarding the property tax settlement report, and no items were pulled. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: 2016 General Obligation Refunding Bonds Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff explained that although bond refundings do not typically require a public hearing, converting bond anticipation notes into long-term debt altered maturity dates and required a public hearing. agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: 2016 General Obligation Bond Referendum Bond Orders (Items 16-1165 to 16-1169)

Speakers advocated for Durham Technical Community College workforce training, libraries, and Durham Public Schools capital needs before the transcript digest was truncated prior to the vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Ambulance Franchise Award to North State Medical Transport
agenda_items.discussion_summary: EMS staff recommended granting a franchise to North State Medical Transport for non-emergency and interfacility advanced/basic life support transport, backup ambulance service, and special events coverage after amending the county ambulance ordinance in response to Duke University Health System's request for greater patient discharge capacity. Healthcare speakers noted moving discharged patients efficiently from Duke University Hospital and Duke Regional Hospital frees inpatient beds for acute patients, and the board approved the franchise unanimously.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-08-01 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 1, 2016 Board of County Commissioners worksession presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the board heard citizen comments on job training for formerly incarcerated and recovering individuals, $15/hour wages, and tax/housing pressures on roughly 500 low-income households. Commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to suspend the rules and appoint David Williams to fill a vacancy on the 2016 Special Board of Equalization and Review. The Durham County Women's Commission presented data on affordable housing instability, female and youth rental burdens, childcare needs, and integrated mental health services, while Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the FY 2016-17 Planning Department work program highlighting compact neighborhood zoning standards, infrastructure planning, Angier-Driver commercial infill rezoning, and draft FEMA flood maps. Later in the session, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow delivered an NACo conference report on the opioid epidemic and Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs)/toxic stress, and the board voted unanimously (5-0) to enter a working closed session on personnel and attorney-client matters before requesting a September discussion of the Human Services parking lot and adjourning without any split votes.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Job Training, Living Wages, and Housing Cost Impacts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Alvin Foote (a TROSA graduate) and others discussed literacy, math, job training, recovery support, and reaching $15-per-hour employment opportunities. Another speaker urged the board and County Manager Wendell Davis to address property tax/housing cost increases affecting roughly 500 low-income households ahead of the September 13 Joint City-County Committee meeting.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Appointment to 2016 Special Board of Equalization and Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To fill a vacancy on the 2016 Special Board of Equalization and Review, the board first voted unanimously to suspend its rules and then voted unanimously to appoint David Williams to the board.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Women's Commission Update on Affordable Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Women's Commission Chair Zion Tankard, Lisa Gabriel, and Rosa Anderson presented findings from the commission's 2016 needs assessment survey and forum on affordable housing, detailing homelessness and rental cost burdens among women and young households by age and sex. They recommended increased childcare funding to reduce household housing burdens and integrating mental health services into existing social services.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2016-17 City-County Planning Department Work Program and Draft Flood Maps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the FY 2016-17 work program developed with the Joint City-County Planning Committee, emphasizing compact neighborhood tier zoning standards, the SACI strategic infrastructure plan, and Angier-Driver commercial infill rezoning. Medlin and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow also discussed well-attended public meetings on draft FEMA floodplain maps—noting some mapped floodplains expanded in developed areas while others shrank under newer studies—and background work for a comprehensive plan update (middle portion omitted in digest).

agenda_items.title: NACo Conference Report on Opioid Epidemic, Toxic Stress, and Youth Interventions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented a conference report from the NACo annual meeting highlighting sessions on the opioid epidemic, Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) screening, and toxic stress, recommending Paul Tough's book 'Helping Children Succeed' and a James Redford documentary. Commissioners connected those trauma-informed findings to Durham's Cure Violence program, the Becoming youth program, and My Brother's Keeper (MBK).

agenda_items.title: Working Closed Session and Post-Closed Session Announcements
