meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-07-11 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 11, 2016 regular meeting, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided in the excused absence of Chair Michael D. Page (who had been granted leave on June 27), opening with a moment of silence for victims of violence in Dallas and Baton Rouge and acknowledging a $99,926 Department of Social Services grant. The four present commissioners voted unanimously (4-0) to approve prior minutes, adopted a resolution honoring the 40th anniversary of the Durham County General Services Department, and heard public comments regarding police shootings, Black Lives Matter, and disaggregated data. On the consent agenda, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted Wake County's entry into the renamed Triangle Tax District for regional transit (item 16-1156) and Vice Chair Howerton emphasized timely annual audits (item 16-1167) before the board approved the unpulled items 4-0. Commissioners then voted 4-0 to approve pulled item 16-1153 with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's amendment adding Durham Public Schools alongside Duke, NCCU, and Durham Tech in the Chamber of Commerce workforce scope of services, and voted 4-0 to adjourn into closed session with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Pledge, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. She read a board statement and led a moment of silence for victims of violence in Dallas, Annapolis, and Baton Rouge, calling for addressing both police and citizen violence, and acknowledged a $99,926 DSS grant award.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (June 6 Worksession and June 27 Regular Session — Item 16-1139)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the June 6, 2016 worksession minutes and June 27, 2016 regular session minutes. All four present commissioners voted in favor.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing the 40th Anniversary of Durham County General Services Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Howerton read a resolution celebrating the 40th anniversary of the General Services Department, tracing its growth since July 1, 1976 from 6 employees overseeing 12 buildings to 77 employees managing 72 buildings and 2.1 million square feet under Director Motiryo Keambiroiro. agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Police Violence and Disaggregated Data

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1145 to 16-1167, Excluding Pulled Item 16-1153)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow pulled item 16-1153 for a minor amendment. Before the vote, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted item 16-1156 adding Wake County to the renamed Triangle Tax District and approving the Wake County Transit Plan and multi-party interlocal agreement, and Vice Chair Howerton put on the record for item 16-1167 that Manager Jodi Miller committed to timely annual audits next year; the remaining consent items passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 16-1153: Chamber of Commerce Scope of Services Amendment

Reckhow proposed adding 'and the Durham Public Schools' to Attachment 1, Section 1D of the Chamber of Commerce scope of services alongside Duke University, North Carolina Central University, and Durham Technical Community College so high school students are also prepared for jobs with relocating or expanding companies that do not require a college degree. Reckhow noted Chamber officials agreed to the addition, and the amended item passed 4-0.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-06-27 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 27, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously excused Page from the July 11 meeting, acknowledged the passing of community leader Ann Atwater, approved prior minutes, and recognized Vulnerable and Elder Abuse Awareness Month alongside an AIA Triangle award with architect Phil Freelon. The board unanimously (5-0) approved the consent agenda—excluding pulled items 16-1102 ($60,000 adoption promotion funds) and 16-1137 (FY 2016-17 budget adoption)—while highlighting item 16-1098, an economic development agreement with Premier Research International bringing 260 jobs at a $73,000 average salary. Following a public hearing on tax-exempt bond refinancing for Trinity School of Durham and Chapel Hill (whose middle-section vote was omitted in digest truncation), commissioners adopted the FY 2016-17 County Budget (item 16-1137) unanimously (5-0), maintaining a revenue-neutral tax rate after revaluation while funding a mental health court, jail discharge transitional housing, a jail mental health pod, a full-time public defender in jail court, and the Cure the Violence initiative. The board concluded by announcing balloted board appointments and voting unanimously (5-0) to enter closed session, with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Pledge of Allegiance, Excusal of Chair Page from July 11 Meeting, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the Pledge of Allegiance, Chair Michael D. Page requested and was unanimously excused from the July 11, 2016 board meeting. Commissioners announced the single July meeting schedule and paid tribute to the life and funeral of community leader Ann Atwater, agreeing to bring forward a formal memorial resolution later to allow the family time.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 2 Worksession and June 13 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved minutes from the May 2, 2016 worksession and June 13, 2016 regular session without changes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for Vulnerable and Elder Abuse Awareness Month & AIA Triangle Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation recognizing June as Vulnerable and Elder Abuse Awareness Month with representatives of the Nursing Home Advisory Committee. Commissioners also received an award from the Triangle Chapter of the American Institute of Architects alongside architect Phil Freelon.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1088 to 16-1146, Excluding 16-1102 and 16-1137)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Items 16-1102 ($60,000 adoption promotion funds budget ordinance) and 16-1137 (FY 2016-17 budget adoption) were pulled for public speakers and separate consideration. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted item 16-1098, an economic development agreement with Premier Research International expected to create 260 full-time jobs at an average salary of $73,000, and the remaining consent items passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Trinity School of Durham and Chapel Hill Tax-Exempt Bond Refinancing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Brandon Lofton presented a request on behalf of Trinity School of Durham and Chapel Hill to refinance 2006 tax-exempt 501(c)(3) bonds with 2016 bonds for existing facilities, noting the county bore zero financial obligation and held the hearing under federal IRS rules. A public speaker requested disaggregated student, teacher, and administrative data for publicly funded institutions before the digest truncated ahead of the vote.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-17 County Budget Adoption (Item 16-1137)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment criticizing school board/contract matters, commissioners praised Budget Director Claudia Hager and staff for delivering a revenue-neutral tax rate amid property revaluations. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow, Fred Foster Jr., Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, and Michael D. Page highlighted new justice and public health investments—including a mental health court with two positions, transitional housing and linkage staff for jail discharges, a special jail mental health pod starting January 1, a full-time public defender in jail court, and Public Health Director Gayle Harris's Cure the Violence initiative—before unanimously adopting the budget.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments and Adjournment to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney announced balloted board appointments, including Jerome Washington to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee and selections for the Criminal Justice Advisory Committee. The board then voted unanimously to adjourn to closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) (real property negotiation) and (a)(6) (personnel).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of the May 2, 2016 worksession and June 13, 2016 regular session.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the FY 2016-17 Durham County budget maintaining a revenue-neutral tax rate while funding mental health court, jail discharge transitional housing, a jail mental health pod, a full-time public defender, and Cure the Violence.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Adjourned to closed session to instruct staff on real property contract negotiations and consider personnel matters.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-06-06 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 6, 2016 Board of County Commissioners worksession presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, a sharp procedural debate opened over whether to pull the draft Naming and Renaming Policy until the clerk transcribed the board's prior stadium/Willie Bradshaw discussion: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's motion to withdraw the item (initially seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs) failed unanimously 0-5 (Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Fred Foster Jr., Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs all opposing/not supporting withdrawal after Jacobs reversed course to keep it on for direction). Commissioners then voted 5-0 to add an item requesting a corrective action plan from the Durham Board of Elections and heard citizen comments from Gregory Williams (Inside-Outside Alliance) criticizing jail medical fees and calling for an independent jail investigation. When the board later debated the Naming and Renaming Policy questions, members split on substantive rules—such as Fred Foster Jr. supporting naming facilities for living individuals while Wendy Jacobs and others opposed it, and differing views between Ellen W. Reckhow and colleagues over restricting naming strictly to interior spaces rather than whole buildings. Commissioners also instructed the County Manager to send a written letter confirming the $90 million school bond figure (while noting a potential 2018 bond if enrollment grows), voted 5-0 twice on closed-session motions, and returned to open session to vote 5-0 to set Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's salary at $87,500 retroactive to her appointment.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments: Naming Policy Withdrawal Debate and Board of Elections Corrective Action Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow sought to withdraw the draft Naming and Renaming Policy until the clerk transcribed prior discussion regarding not naming entire buildings (referencing Willie Bradshaw and the stadium), and to add an item asking the Durham Board of Elections for a corrective action plan. After Commissioner Wendy Jacobs initially seconded withdrawing the naming policy but changed her position during debate to seek board direction on policy questions—and after a point of order over debate during a vote—the motion to withdraw failed 0-5, while adding the Board of Elections corrective action plan discussion passed 5-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Withdrawal Failed 0-5; Board of Elections Addition Passed 5-0

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on County Jail Conditions and Independent Investigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Gregory Williams of the Inside-Outside Alliance delivered a response from the inmate First Five Grievance Committee to the Sheriff's reply on nine jail complaints, highlighting a $20 fee for non-emergency medical visits and lack of intake screening, and reiterated calls for an independent community-based jail investigation. Additional speakers Edwin Harris and Kate Fairwood were called before the digest truncated the middle of the morning agenda.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Proposed Naming and Renaming Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After resolving confusion over whether the item remained on the agenda, the County Attorney walked commissioners through a Saturday email of six policy questions compiled from other jurisdictions, including application procedures and public hearings. Commissioners diverged on key rules—Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. favored allowing naming for living individuals while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and others said no, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow pushed back on limiting naming solely to interior spaces rather than whole buildings—before instructing staff to return with a revised policy for adoption.

agenda_items.title: Closed Sessions and Retroactive Salary for Register of Deeds Sharon Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session for personnel and later added an attorney-client privilege closed session item by a 5-0 vote. Returning to open session at 06:06:35, commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to set Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's salary at $87,500 retroactive to the date of her appointment before adjourning at 3:15 p.m.

agenda_items.title: School Bond Communications ($90 Million Cap and Potential 2018 Bond)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a motion to enter closed session, commissioners and the County Attorney paused to address discrepancies in figures reported by the school board and newspaper regarding the school bond. Commissioners agreed to stay at $90 million for the current bond while instructing the County Manager to put in writing to the school board that Durham County would consider another school bond in 2018 if enrollment growth justifies it.

votes.item_title: Motion to Withdraw Proposed Naming and Renaming Policy Discussion Until Further Notice
votes.discussion_detail: Reckhow moved to pull the naming policy pending a transcript of prior board comments; Jacobs initially seconded but switched to oppose withdrawal so the board could discuss the County Attorney's policy questions, and the Chair declared the motion failed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Add Item Requesting Durham Board of Elections Corrective Action Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Added a discussion item before closed session asking the Durham Board of Elections to prepare a corrective action plan following the State Board of Elections meeting.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (Personnel)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session following the Naming and Renaming Policy discussion.

votes.item_title: Add Closed Session Item: Attorney-Client Privilege (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Added consultation with the county attorney under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to the closed session.

votes.item_title: Set Salary of Register of Deeds Sharon Davis at $87,500 Retroactive to Appointment
votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning from closed session, established Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's annual salary at $87,500 retroactive to the date of her appointment.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-06-06 9:00 AM - Worksession
disagreements.issue: Withdrawing vs. Discussing the Draft Naming and Renaming Policy and Setting Policy Criteria
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed procedurally over whether to pull the draft Naming and Renaming Policy from the worksession agenda pending a transcript of their prior stadium/Willie Bradshaw discussion, resulting in a 0-5 defeat of the withdrawal motion, and then diverged on whether facilities could be named for living people or restricted to interior spaces.
disagreements.side_a_position: Keep the item on the agenda for immediate policy direction; bar naming facilities for living individuals and restrict naming to interior features rather than entire buildings
side_a_arguments: The board should provide clear answers to the County Attorney's policy questions rather than delaying again.
Prior board consensus on the stadium/Willie Bradshaw discussion opposed naming entire buildings and favored naming interior features only.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer the draft policy until the prior meeting transcript is reviewed, and allow naming for living individuals or whole facilities where warranted
side_b_arguments: The draft policy did not accurately reflect the board's previous discussion, making immediate debate unproductive without the transcript.
Blanket prohibitions on naming entire buildings or honoring living individuals could prevent future honors.
disagreements.resolution: Reckhow's motion to withdraw the item failed 0-5 after Jacobs reversed her second; the board later answered the County Attorney's six policy questions with mixed views (Foster supporting naming for living individuals, Jacobs opposing; Reckhow opposing a strict limit to interior features) and directed staff to return a revised draft.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-05-23 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 23, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, County Manager Wendell Davis presented the FY 2016-17 Recommended Budget, highlighting his 'Managing for Results' data framework, an 11.1 percent average property valuation jump after the eight-year revaluation, and a proposed tax rate representing a one-cent increase above the revenue-neutral rate. The recommended budget funded Durham Public Schools enrollment growth and teacher mentoring, EMS, fire district, and detention center increases, school nurses, Cure Violence, 2 to 3 percent merit pay, a pay plan review, and reserves for federal overtime rules and public safety retention, ahead of a May 31 public hearing and June 27 adoption. Commissioners also pulled Sports Commission appointments until member terms are established, made balloted appointments to the City-County Appearance Commission and Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, and voted unanimously (5-0) to enter closed session on personnel matters with no split votes.

Recommended investments covered DPS enrollment growth and teacher mentoring, EMS, fire district, detention center, school nurses, Cure Violence, 2–3 percent merit pay, a pay plan review, higher state retirement contributions, and reserves for federal overtime changes and public safety retention.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-05-09 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 9, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved prior minutes, presented four ceremonial proclamations (National Foster Care Awareness Month, Older Americans Month, Drug Treatment Court, and County Employee Appreciation), and passed the consent agenda (items 16-1026 to 16-1058 and 16-1062) after pulling item 16-1060. The board split 3-2 on item 16-1034, a developer-proposed change to the timing of state-mandated water quality nutrient offset fee payments following late-2014 state fee increases: Fred Foster Jr. (mover) and Brenda A. Howerton (seconder) voted Aye alongside one other commissioner, while two members voted Nay after concerns were raised about developer cash-flow risk and unfinished subdivision infrastructure (individual voice-vote positions beyond Foster and Howerton among Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs were not named on the record). On pulled consent item 16-1060, commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to adopt the Public Health Nuisance Abatement amendments to the Durham County Solid Waste Ordinance—adding property lien cost-recovery tools—along with an amendment to Section 20-6 clarifying that residential recyclable materials must be removed biweekly (every 14 days), before adjourning at 9:05 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements highlighted a children's artwork contest for the 'Clean Up After Your Canine or Face a Fine' campaign and the May 21 Hollow Rock Nature Park grand opening.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (April 25 Regular Session and April 16 PAC 1 Meeting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved minutes from the April 25, 2016 regular session and the April 16, 2016 PAC 1 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations (Foster Care, Older Americans, Drug Treatment Court, Employee Appreciation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners presented four proclamations: National Foster Care Awareness Month (noting a 47 percent increase in youth in foster care over two years and preventive efforts), Older Americans Month (highlighting the second annual Senior Summit and a projected 40 percent senior population increase over 10 years), Drug Treatment Court (with Judge Battaglia noting $13,000 in savings per graduate), and County Employee Appreciation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-1026 to 16-1058 and 16-1062, Excluding Pulled Item 16-1060)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner pulled item 16-1060 (Solid Waste Ordinance) for clarification, and Chair Page confirmed the remaining consent agenda covered items 16-1026 through 16-1058 plus 16-1062. The unpulled items passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Developer-Proposed Changes to Timing and Payment of Water Quality Nutrient Offset Fees (Item 16-1034)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resource speaker Dan Jewell explained that Durham's unwritten practice required state-mandated nutrient offset payments at site plan approval / prior to land disturbance permit issuance, which had become burdensome after late-2014 NC Division of Environmental Quality fee increases (tripling phosphorus fees). Opposing concerns cited developer cash-flow motivations and past cases where residents were left with unfinished infrastructure, before the board voted 3-2 on a voice vote moved by Fred Foster Jr. and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton to approve the timing change.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 16-1060: Public Health Nuisance Abatement Amendments to Solid Waste Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Solid Waste Manager Brian Haynesworth presented a clarifying sentence amending Section 20-6 so residential recyclables must be removed at least once every 14 days (matching biweekly county pickup) rather than seven days, alongside amendments to Sections 20-4, 20-5, 20-16, and new Section 20-18 allowing property liens to recover nuisance cleanup costs. Commissioners thanked staff for extensive rural community outreach and approved the ordinance with the Section 20-6 amendment unanimously.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of the April 25, 2016 regular session and April 16, 2016 PAC 1 meeting.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted amendments to Durham County Solid Waste Ordinance Sections 20-4, 20-5, 20-16, added Section 20-18 on public health nuisance abatement and cost-recovery liens, and amended Section 20-6 to specify biweekly (14-day) residential recycling removal.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-05-09 7:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Changing Payment Timing for State-Mandated Water Quality Nutrient Offset Fees (Item 16-1034)
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-2 on whether to relax Durham's unwritten practice of requiring state-mandated water quality nutrient offset payments prior to land disturbance permit issuance, balancing developer cash-flow burdens after 2014 state fee increases against risks of incomplete subdivision infrastructure.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve developer-proposed timing change for nutrient offset fee payments
side_a_arguments: Requiring payment at site plan/land disturbance permit issuance was an unwritten practice rather than a statute or ordinance.

Late-2014 NC Division of Environmental Quality fee increases (tripling phosphorus rates) made upfront payment unnecessarily burdensome, whereas other infrastructure certifications occur later before certificates of occupancy.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain upfront payment prior to land disturbance permit issuance due to developer cash-flow risks
side_b_arguments: Changing payment timing to address developer cash-flow issues raises concern given past developments where residents were left with unfinished infrastructure.
Upfront payment prior to land disturbance permit issuance ensured compliance before construction proceeded.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve Item 16-1034 passed 3-2 on a voice vote moved by Fred Foster Jr. and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton; one additional commissioner voted Aye and two voted Nay among Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs, though individual voice-vote names were not recorded in the transcript.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-05-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 2, 2016 Board of County Commissioners work session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Board opened by voting 4-0 to excuse Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. and heard citizen comments advocating for Southeast Durham EMS funding near Leesville and Doc Nichols roads as well as an independent community-based investigation into Durham County Jail conditions. Commissioners then received presentations on Capital Improvement Program (CIP) general obligation bond referendum proposals—including the Museum of Life and Science and Durham Public Schools—alongside plans for public polling on four bond questions and potential tax-rate impacts. Staff also updated the Board on due diligence for redeveloping the Human Services parking lot and bundling county and city downtown parcels for mixed-income affordable housing. At the close of the session, the Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and 4-0 to approve a resolution originating with the Durham Association of Educators to increase per-pupil funding, with no split votes or formal disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Excusal of Commissioner Fred Foster Jr., and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page noted that Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. would be absent and the Board voted 4-0 to excuse him. During citizen comments, Loretta Woodall (representing Carolina Arbors homeowners in Southeast Durham) requested Phase 1 CIP bond funding for a new EMS station near Leesville and Doc Nichols roads and temporary ambulance co-location at Fire Station 17. Gregory Williams and Edwin Harris of the Inside-Outside Alliance pressed for an independent community-based jail investigation rather than relying solely on the National Institute of Corrections, citing complaints over kitchen retaliation, 12-hour overnight lockbacks, high bonds, religious access, law library access, and age caps on GED programming.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Bond Referendum Presentations and Public Polling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff and partner organizations presented Capital Improvement Program (CIP) bond referendum requests, beginning with the Museum of Life and Science (including attendance trends, preliminary lower-elevation parking deck designs, and transit bus turnaround challenges) and referencing Durham Public Schools' initial $186 million request. Later in the discussion, staff outlined upcoming public polling across four bond questions—testing support with and without a modest or three-cent tax-rate increase—with results due by May 16 and legally required worst-case tax-rate disclosures for educational mailings.

agenda_items.title: Human Services Parking Lot Development and Downtown Affordable Housing Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported on due diligence for redeveloping the Human Services parking lot and evaluating broader county- and city-owned downtown parcels with partners such as the Development Finance Initiative (DFI) or Urban Land Institute (ULI). Commissioners discussed bundling county and city sites to wrap parking decks with affordable housing, following up on commitments made at a Durham CAN meeting, and targeting multiple income levels (such as households earning $30,000 versus $60,000).

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Increase Per-Pupil Funding (Durham Association of Educators)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a resolution forwarded from the Durham Association of Educators supporting increased per-pupil funding, noting that two other non-time-sensitive resolutions remained under staff review while this signed resolution still needed Commissioner Foster's signature. After clarifying work-session procedure with staff, the Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and 4-0 to approve the resolution before adjourning at 1:55 PM.

votes.notes: Chair Page announced the motion carried unanimously with Foster absent.

votes.notes: Approved by voice vote with Foster absent.

votes.item_title: Approve Resolution to Increase Per-Pupil Funding
votes.notes: Commissioners briefly discussed whether a formal vote was required since members had already signed the document; motion carried with Foster absent.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-04-11 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 11, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners participating, the Board approved the March 28, 2016 minutes (5-0), welcomed new Human Resources Director Kathy, and presented a signed resolution condemning and urging immediate repeal of North Carolina's House Bill 2 (the Public Facilities Privacy and Security Act), with commissioners emphasizing its harm to civil rights, workers, and Durham's economy. Following unanimous approval of Consent Agenda Items 16-955 through 16-1004 (5-0), the Board held a public hearing on Item 16-997 and voted 5-0 to approve up to $200,000 in economic development incentives over five years for Aurobindo Pharma USA, Inc. ($100,000 tied to a $31.7 million capital investment and up to $100,000 in $1,000 hiring reimbursements for Durham residents across 200 new jobs). The Board also voted 5-0 to approve $62,500 for free downtown community programming at Moogfest and adjourned into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) on a 5-0 vote, with no split votes or disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, March 28, 2016 Minutes, and Introduction of Human Resources Director
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced Seniors Bold City Play Streets (April 23), Durham Housing Authority site-based waiting list openings, and the Durham Roots Farmers Market grand opening at Northgate Mall (April 16). The Board approved the March 28, 2016 regular session minutes 5-0, and County Manager Wendell Davis introduced Kathy as the new Human Resources Director transitioning from the County Attorney's Office.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Condemning the Public Facilities Privacy and Security Act (House Bill 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With State Senator Mike Woodard in attendance, Chair Page read a resolution signed by all five commissioners condemning House Bill 2 and urging Governor Pat McCrory and legislative leaders to repeal it, citing economic threats, potential loss of federal funding, impacts on livable-wage advocacy, and elimination of state civil discrimination remedies. Commissioners Reckhow, Howerton, and Jacobs spoke in strong support, with Jacobs noting HB2 was also a 'smokescreen for a labor bill.'

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-955 to 16-1004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled and no public speakers signed up, the Board approved Consent Agenda Items 16-955 through 16-1004 by a 5-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 16-997 Economic Development Incentive for Aurobindo Pharma USA, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Marketa Walton presented a proposed $200,000 performance-based General Fund incentive over five years for Aurobindo Pharma USA ($100,000 tied to a $31.7 million capital investment and up to $100,000 in $1,000 training reimbursements per Durham resident hired) for an expansion creating 200 jobs, including 113 manufacturing jobs. After Durham Chamber of Commerce representative Ted Connor spoke in support and noted a Durham Tech training partnership, the Board approved Item 16-997 unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Moogfest Free Community Programming Funding Request and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a $62,500 funding request to support free downtown installations and community programming at Moogfest so residents unable to afford festival tickets could participate; a Moogfest organizer also thanked the Board for its HB2 resolution, noting keynote speaker Dr. Martine Rothblatt and other transgender speakers. The Board approved the $62,500 allocation 5-0 and then voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-04-04 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 4, 2016 Board of County Commissioners work session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (opening with two commissioners absent before Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. joined), citizens from the Durham Jail Investigation Team and Inside-Outside Alliance reiterated demands for independent community access to inspect the Durham County Jail, interview detainees, and review records following three jail deaths in the past year, including an opioid overdose where Narcan was raised as needed. The Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules and remove three members of the Women's Commission (Johnson Harper, Joanne Pinnix, and Gloria Trotter) for poor attendance, and then reviewed a draft resolution opposing North Carolina's House Bill 2 alongside a legal briefing on the bill's provisions, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requesting added language on economic development and education impacts. In the afternoon, staff and County Manager Wendell M. Davis reviewed a proposed $285 million Capital Improvement Program (CIP) general obligation bond scenario, polling plans, and long-term operating budget impacts (deferred to May), and presented an informational administrative reorganization adopting a matrix Managing for Results structure with Claudia Hager and Marketa Walton in elevated executive and economic development roles. There were no split votes or formal disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Durham County Jail Conditions and Independent Investigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page opened the work session noting two commissioners were missing and recognized two citizen speakers. A representative of the Durham Jail Investigation Team demanded access to survey 100 detainees, inspect facilities, and obtain grievance, vendor revenue, and out-of-cell time records, citing three inmate deaths in the prior year (Matthew McCain, Dennis McMurray from a fentanyl/heroin overdose reversible by Narcan, and Raphael Bennett). Gregory Williams (Inside-Outside Alliance) read a detainee letter from Tony King and called for an investigation led independently of the Sheriff's Office.

agenda_items.title: Removal of Three Women's Commission Members for Poor Attendance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page reported that three members of the Women's Commission—Johnson Harper, Joanne Pinnix, and Gloria Trotter—had failed attendance standards and had not responded to clerk outreach. The Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules and unanimously to remove all three members.

agenda_items.title: Review and Legal Briefing on Draft Resolution Opposing House Bill 2
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed a draft resolution opposing and seeking repeal of the Public Facilities Privacy and Security Act (House Bill 2), which had just been distributed at 9:00 AM. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton asked that economic development and education impacts be clearly addressed in the text, and staff member Danielle Briggs provided a legal overview of HB2's passage following Charlotte's local nondiscrimination ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and 2016 Bond Referendum Sizing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and County Manager Wendell Davis discussed expanding projected general obligation bond capacity from $250 million to $285 million based on slower project spend-out schedules, potential three-cent tax-rate impacts tested in spring voter polling, and peer county bond activity in Orange and Wake counties. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned sharp projected staffing increases in the facilities master plan compared to historical growth, and commissioners deferred detailed CIP comments until May due to the late hour.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Government Administrative Reorganization Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell M. Davis presented an administrative matrix reorganization aligned with Managing for Results, detailing executive team oversight including General Manager for Financial Affairs, Process Improvement, and Government Efficiency Claudia Hager, a new Assistant General Manager / Chief of Staff position, and a new Economic Development Officer role filled by Marketa Walton to lead marketing, manufacturing focus, infrastructure planning, and website development. Commissioners confirmed the update was strictly informational, and the meeting adjourned at 4:45 PM.

votes.notes: Chair Page stated two commissioners were absent at 00:00:00; Page, Howerton, and Reckhow are confirmed present here, while Fred Foster Jr. seconded the next motion 31 seconds later and Wendy Jacobs's attendance is unconfirmed in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend the rules at a work session to take action on removing three Women's Commission members for poor attendance.

votes.notes: Page, Howerton, Reckhow, and Foster are confirmed present; Wendy Jacobs's attendance is not confirmed in the transcript digest. Chair Page announced 'Motion carries.'
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to remove Johnson Harper, Joanne Pinnix, and Gloria Trotter from the Women's Commission due to lack of attendance.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-03-28 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 28, 2016 meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, Chair Page delivered the annual State of the County address, congratulating re-elected Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, and Ellen W. Reckhow along with incoming commissioners Heidi Carter and Jim Hill, highlighting national departmental awards, My Brother's Keeper Durham's draft action plan, Managing for Results performance budgeting, and Durham's #4 national ranking for best places to live. Following public hearings with no citizen speakers, the Board voted 5-0 to approve the Statement of Consistency and 5-0 to adopt a Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) omnibus text amendment revising historic district initiation rules (removing the 25% petition minimum) and adding intent language in Section 1.2 encouraging affordable housing, equity, and socioeconomic diversity. The Board also voted 5-0 on Item 16-0965 to remove 2.04 acres from the Research Triangle Park (RTP) Service District for a residential development by Bald Eagle Land Development NC LLC. After announcing ballot appointments to five boards and commissions, the Board voted 5-0 to adjourn to closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) on real property negotiations, with no split votes or disagreements.

agenda_items.title: State of the County Address by Chair Michael D. Page
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page delivered the State of the County remarks, recognizing departing senior leaders Jeff Batten and Lee Worsley, congratulating incoming commissioners Heidi Carter and Jim Hill alongside re-elected colleagues, and celebrating awards across the Tax Office, Engineering and Environmental Services, Library, Criminal Justice Resource Center, Sheriff's Office, and Cooperative Extension. He detailed progress on My Brother's Keeper (MBK) Durham's four policy committees, the countywide rollout of Managing for Results performance metrics by FY 2017-18, economic development job commitments, and U.S. News & World Report ranking Durham fourth among best places to live.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Omnibus Text Amendment (Sections 1.2, 2.5, 3.16, and Wireless Facilities)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented omnibus Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) amendments covering state agency naming, Historic Preservation Commission procedures in Section 2.5, removing the 25% petition minimum for local historic districts in Section 3.16, wireless communication facility standards (TC120013), and intent statements in Section 1.2 proposed by the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit encouraging affordable housing, equity, and socioeconomic diversity. Noting the Planning Commission's 10-1 recommendation (Tom Miller dissenting) and no public hearing speakers, the Board approved the Statement of Consistency 5-0 and adopted the UDO ordinance amendment 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 16-0965 Removal of 2.04 Acres from RTP Service District
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and developer attorney Joseph Bass III presented a statutory petition under N.C.G.S. 153A-314.1 to remove 2.04 acres (a strip north of SoHi) from the Research and Production Service District of RTP so it could be included in a residential project by Bald Eagle Land Development NC LLC, confirming the RTP Foundation had weighed in. With no speakers at the public hearing, the Board approved the removal resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following ballot voting, the County Attorney announced appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (Jeffrey L. Austin and Corey Dunn), Animal Services Advisory Committee (Sue Darling), Boxing and Wrestling Commission (Marion Dillahunt Andrews), Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee (Dana Pearson), and Public Health Board (Almond Curtis and Tammy Levbark). The Board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding real property acquisition negotiations.

votes.item_title: Approve Statement of Consistency for UDO Omnibus Text Amendment
votes.notes: Carried unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve Attachment B, the Statement of Consistency for the UDO omnibus text amendment.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO)
votes.notes: Carried unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adopt the ordinance amending the UDO (Attachment A), incorporating revisions to Article 1 regarding affordable housing, equity, and socioeconomic diversity intent, Section 3.16 historic district initiation, and technical corrections.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 16-0965 Resolution Removing 2.04 Acres from RTP Service District
votes.notes: Approved by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the resolution authorizing removal of 2.04 acres from the RTP Research and Production Service District for Bald Eagle Land Development NC LLC.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5))
votes.notes: Approved by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session to instruct staff on price and material terms for real property acquisition by purchase, option, exchange, or lease.

meetings.executive_summary: At the March 14, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Board approved the February 1 and February 8, 2016 minutes (5-0) and presented departmental recognitions to Budget and Management Services for the GFOA Distinguished Budget Presentation Award and to Information Services and Technology (IS&T) for a national IT effectiveness award, along with a memorial resolution honoring late Assistant Fire Marshal John Gentry Jr. II. The Board then heard public support for pulled Consent Item 16-0919 (the county's pet waste ordinance) and approved it 5-0, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs emphasizing a six-month fine enforcement grace period and seeking 75% state grant support for bag stations at county parks and trails. After announcing Juvenile Crime Prevention Council FY 2016-17 RFP training details, the Board adjourned at 8:04 PM with no split votes or disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Minutes Approval and Departmental / Memorial Recognitions

Chair Page then recognized Budget and Management Services (Director Claudia Odom Hager and staff) for earning the GFOA Distinguished Budget Presentation Award, recognized IS&T (CIO Greg Marrow and staff) for a national IT effectiveness award, and presented a memorial resolution honoring Assistant Fire Marshal John Gentry Jr. II, who passed away on February 5, 2016.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 16-0919)

With no public hearing speakers, the Board approved the update 5-0 and approved the accompanying consistency statement 5-0.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-02-08 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 8, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Board recognized the Durham Soil and Water Conservation District for winning a $100,000 Duke Energy Water Resources Fund grant for Jordan Lake watershed conservation, passed a resolution honoring Drew Cummings for eight years as Assistant County Manager and service as Interim Deputy County Manager, and formally introduced new Deputy County Manager Jody Miller. The Board voted 5-0 to approve Consent Agenda Items 16-0843 through 16-0889, with Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs highlighting the 25th anniversary of the Durham Open Space and Trails Matching Grants program (Item 16-0878, committing $62,000 to leverage $154,000 in community trail and playground projects). Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board voted 5-0 to approve a resolution authorizing Series 2016 refunding bonds for the 2009A Health and Human Services Complex bonds to save over $2 million (roughly $250,000 annually). Commissioners then voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6), returned to report giving staff direction, and adjourned at 9:35 PM with no split votes or disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Soil and Water Conservation Grant Recognition, Drew Cummings Resolution, and Deputy Manager Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced that the February 22 regular meeting was canceled and recognized the Durham Soil and Water Conservation District for receiving a maximum $100,000 Duke Energy Water Resources Fund grant for Upper New Hope Creek / Jordan Lake watershed best management practices. The Board then presented Item 16-0887 honoring Assistant County Manager Drew Cummings for serving as Interim Deputy County Manager from July 2015 to February 1, 2016, and introduced new Deputy County Manager Jody Miller (formerly Deputy City Manager of Williamsburg, Virginia).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-0843 to 16-0889) and Open Space & Trails Grants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled and no public speakers, the Board approved Consent Agenda Items 16-0843 through 16-0889 by a 5-0 vote. Commissioner Reckhow highlighted Item 16-0878 marking the 25th year of the Durham Open Space and Trails Matching Grants program ($62,000 in county funds matched to $154,000 total across eight projects), and Commissioner Jacobs added supportive remarks.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Series 2016 Bond Refunding (2009A Health & Human Services Bonds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Financial Officer George Quick presented a plan to refund the Series 2009A bonds originally issued for the Health and Human Services Complex, projecting slightly more than $2 million in total savings (over $250,000 per year over the remaining nine-plus years). After holding a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved the refunding bond resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development and Personnel) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business location or expansion and (a)(6) to evaluate public officer or employee qualifications and performance. Upon returning to open session at 02:31:28, the Board reported it had provided direction to staff and adjourned at 9:35 PM.

meetings.executive_summary: At the February 1, 2016 Board of County Commissioners work session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs arriving shortly after opening due to traffic on NC-147), County Manager Wendell M. Davis welcomed new Deputy County Manager Jody Miller on her first day. During an extended citizen comment period—approved via unanimous 5-0 votes to suspend the rules and extend time—speakers urged early CIP funding for a Southeast Durham EMS station near Leesville and Doc Nichols roads, sought a county resolution backing nonpartisan redistricting under House Bill 92, and highlighted local VITA tax assistance. The Board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to remove Judy Ingram from the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee for poor attendance, and then received an ETC Institute presentation on the countywide resident satisfaction survey for Managing for Results. agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis introduced new Deputy County Manager Jody Miller on her first day and noted Commissioner Wendy Jacobs was delayed by a traffic accident on NC-147 before joining the meeting. agenda_items.title: Rougemont Water System Operations, Rate Structure, and Draft Utility Ordinance Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Utilities staff briefed commissioners on items slated for the February 8 consent agenda—including a budget amendment, interfund startup loan, service agreements, and utility ordinance for the Rougemont water system—estimating typical residential bills at $40–$50 per month and noting septic/wastewater constraints in the area. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-01-25 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 25, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton (with Chair Michael D. Page excused), Presiding Chair Howerton announced that the Durham County Department of Public Health had launched an independent investigation into the January 19, 2016 death of a Durham County jail inmate, including a medical chart and grievance review alongside Correct Care Solutions and detention staff with findings expected in about three weeks. The Board approved three sets of prior minutes (4-0) and issued proclamations for Durham School Choice Week (January 24–30, 2016) and Durham County Goes Red Day (February 4, 2016) for women's heart health. Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items 16-0812 through 16-0857 on a 4-0 vote, with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow highlighting Item 16-0857—a $200,000 county contribution paired with City of Durham, City of Raleigh, and Trust for Public Land funds to purchase 134 acres in eastern Durham protecting the Falls Lake watershed and Mountains-to-Sea Trail. In board and commission ballot voting, the Board filled eight positions and deferred tie votes on the Animal Services Advisory Committee and one Public Health Board seat to the next meeting before adjourning at 7:35 PM.

agenda_items.title: Statement on Independent Public Health Investigation of January 19, 2016 Jail Death
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Brenda A. Howerton read a prepared statement announcing that the Durham County Department of Public Health had launched an independent investigation into the January 19, 2016 death of a detainee in the Durham County jail, assessing nursing compliance with N.C. Board of Nursing and NCCHC standards, sick-call requests, and grievances alongside Correct Care Solutions. The Public Health Director reported receiving the full medical record that day and participating in a February 11 medical review, estimating findings within three weeks, as commissioners extended condolences to the family.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Storm Staff Acknowledgment, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Howerton announced 2016 Durham County Cares nonprofit grant applications and the February 6 YouthWork job fair at the Holton Career and Resource Center, and thanked General Services Director Mo and county staff who worked around the clock during the recent winter storm. The Board voted 4-0 to approve the December 7, 2015 work session, December 14, 2015 regular session, and January 4, 2016 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Durham School Choice Week and Durham County Goes Red Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Howerton read proclamations recognizing January 24–30, 2016 as Durham School Choice Week and February 4, 2016 as Durham County Goes Red Day in support of American Heart Month. Public Health educator Chastity Newkirk encouraged participation in the February 4 preventive health event, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs emphasized educating women on heart attack symptoms.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 16-0812 through 16-0857) and Falls Lake 134-Acre Acquisition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Prior to voting, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow highlighted Item 16-0857, a multi-partner acquisition of 134 acres in eastern Durham leveraging $200,000 from Durham County, $250,000 from the City of Durham, and funding from the Trust for Public Land and City of Raleigh at less than half of appraised value to protect the Falls Lake watershed and support a future city park and Mountains-to-Sea Trail connection. The Board approved Consent Agenda Items 16-0812 through 16-0857 on a 4-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Ballot Ties Deferred)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After tabulating ballots, the County Attorney announced selections including Daniel Colvard (Boxing and Wrestling Commission), Jeffrey Wolf (Firefighters' Relief Fund Board of Trustees), Eric Mein (Historic Preservation Commission), Karen Carpenter and Marilyn Cash (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee), George Brine (Planning Commission), Rosemary Jackson (Public Health Board), Zach Hawkins (Transportation Advisory Board), and Roger C. Schumet (Workforce Development Board). Due to ties on the Animal Services Advisory Committee and the second Public Health Board seat, commissioners agreed to bring those two seats back at the next meeting before adjourning at 7:35 PM.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript; Vice Chair Howerton presided and announced the 4-0 vote with Chair Michael D. Page excused.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-01-04 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 4, 2016 Board of County Commissioners Worksession, Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting with a moment of acknowledgment for the passing of community leader Sharon Biman before hearing citizen comments, where Carolina Arbors resident Loretta Woodall urged the board to accelerate a Phase 1 EMS facility near Brier Creek and staff discussed ambulance staffing limits and scheduled a February EMS facility master study briefing. Public commenters also alleged unsanitary conditions and suppressed inmate participation in a National Commission on Correctional Health Care (NCCHC) survey at the Durham County Detention Facility, after which staff presented an update on the Durham County Space Needs Analysis and Facility Master Plan following the prior year's decision to pause Capital Improvements Program updates. Commissioners next reviewed proposed Solid Waste Ordinance amendments—such as shortening bulky waste and trash set-out periods, reinvesting revenues into convenience sites and 96-gallon containers, and establishing prima facie illegal dumping evidence—to be brought back for action on January 11. The Department of Social Services Director concluded the substantive agenda with a briefing on upcoming state 20-hour work or volunteer requirements for able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs) receiving Food and Nutrition Services, and the board adjourned by routine voice vote with no substantive votes or split disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Memorial Acknowledgment, and Citizen Comments on EMS and Detention Facility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the work session, noted a future resolution honoring recently deceased community leader Sharon Biman, and invited public comment. Carolina Arbors resident Loretta Woodall requested early Phase 1 construction of a nearby EMS station recommended in the EMS capital improvement study to serve over 800 existing 55+ homeowners and surrounding new developments, leading to discussion with EMS staff and the County Manager about ambulance availability, recent medical emergencies, and scheduling an EMS facility master study update for the February work session. Another commenter read excerpts from inmate letters alleging unsanitary detention facility cells and accusing Correct Care Solutions and jail staff of suppressing inmate participation in a December NCCHC survey.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Space Needs Analysis and Facility Master Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff led by Jay Gibson and Brian Atkins presented the Durham County Space Needs Analysis and Facility Master Plan Update. Introductory remarks noted that the board had consciously decided the previous year to hold off on updating the Capital Improvements Program pending completion of this facility planning work. Staff began outlining the purpose, process, findings, and recommendations of the master plan update (with the middle portion of the presentation omitted in the transcript digest).

agenda_items.title: Solid Waste Ordinance Revisions Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff reviewed proposed Solid Waste Ordinance updates, including reducing allowable bulky waste set-out time from 72 to 24 hours, shortening violation cleanup windows from 14 to 7 days, and introducing prima facie evidence rules (such as license plates and address identifiers) to penalize illegal dumpers rather than innocent property owners. Staff explained that collected revenues would be reinvested into the solid waste utility for convenience site renovations and additional 96-gallon containers, and described compliance-focused inspection workflows alongside employee orientation and shared site coordination. Staff indicated the finalized ordinance changes would return for consideration at the January 11 meeting.

agenda_items.title: DSS Report on Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Policy Changes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Department of Social Services (DSS) Director briefed commissioners on an impending state policy requiring able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs) receiving Food and Nutrition Services to complete at least 20 hours per week of work or qualifying volunteer or training activity. DSS highlighted community mitigation efforts including a Human Services Building resource fair with NCWorks, the Volunteer Center, nonprofits, and employers, as well as interview preparation and an NCWorks employment specialist integrated onsite four days a week. Staff and commissioners also discussed interagency coordination and maintaining a 95% state compliance threshold from January through June to protect approximately $70 million in statewide funding.

Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners celebrated Durham County Access Transportation Awareness and Customer Service Week, recognized Smart Commute awardees (Duke University, American Tobacco Campus, the Durham VA Medical Center, and the East Coast Greenway Alliance), and adopted a resolution honoring the NCDOT Public Transportation Division signed by all five commissioners. Following a middle truncation in the transcript, the Board closed a public hearing and voted unanimously by voice vote to approve a $26,000 economic development investment fund agreement with Premier Research International in partnership with Durham Tech, and then received the FY 2015 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) audit briefing. Commissioners also discussed five pulled consent agenda items—covering misdemeanor diversion/faith-team re-entry grants (Item 786), MWBE contract metrics (Item 788), the Durham County Access Title VI program resolution (Item 782), and greenhouse gas/sustainability reporting (Items 777 and 771)—before approving all five unanimously by voice vote. The Board concluded by voting unanimously to enter closed session for attorney-client litigation consultation and economic development discussions, with no split or contested votes occurring during the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Eno River Association 50th Anniversary Presentation, Announcements, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and asked audience members to refrain from interrupting during agenda adjustments. Eno River Association Executive Director Robin Jacobs and Vice President Malo Pine presented their 2016 50th-anniversary calendar and noted the upcoming statewide bond referendum supporting Eno River State Park improvements. After clerk announcements, the Board unanimously approved the November 23, 2015 regular session minutes on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, followed by personal holiday remarks from a commissioner.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Proclamations, Smart Commute Awards, and NCDOT Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page proclaimed the week of December 14, 2015 as Durham County Access Transportation Awareness and Customer Service Week. Officials recognized local Smart Commute award winners—including Duke University, American Tobacco Campus, Peter Tillman of the Durham VA Medical Center, and the East Coast Greenway Alliance—while noting U.S. Census data ranking Durham-Chapel Hill third nationally for commute-trip reduction between 2007 and 2013. The Board also presented a resolution signed by all five commissioners honoring the NCDOT Public Transportation Division.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Economic Development Agreement: Premier Research International
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle truncation in the transcript digest, Durham Chamber of Commerce Senior VP Ted Conner spoke during the public hearing on recent job announcements in Durham including Harrison Corporation, Ontario Communications, Willatory, and Fidelity Investments. Chair Page closed the public hearing with no additional speakers. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board unanimously approved an investment fund agreement allocating $26,000 to Premier Research International in partnership with Durham Tech.

agenda_items.title: FY 2015 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Audit Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff and external auditors presented the FY 2015 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR), covering the county's financial statements as well as federal and state grant compliance reviews. Auditors reviewed audit findings and classifications—noting a statewide reporting change that delayed county audits—and Chair Page thanked finance staff for their work.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Agenda Items (786, 788, 782, 777, and 771)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton explained she pulled Item 786 to publicly highlight county misdemeanor diversion and faith-team re-entry work funded through a Governor's Crime Commission grant. Commissioners also reviewed Item 788 on MWBE contract-value metrics ($1.5 million initial target) and FY 2016-17 budget analytics, Item 782 adopting an updated Durham County Access Title VI program resolution with Transportation Advisory Board diversity and ESL translation provisions, and Items 777 and 771 including greenhouse gas plan reporting. The Board then unanimously approved all five pulled consent items.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-12-07 9:00 AM - Workession
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 7, 2015 organizational work session with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened under statutory procedure and unanimously re-elected Michael D. Page as Chair and Brenda A. Howerton as Vice Chair by 5-0 voice votes, deferring public official bonds briefly due to the risk manager's absence. During citizen comments, speakers addressed opposition to the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), requested a joint city-county pet-waste enforcement ordinance, raised concerns over winter weekend gym closures at Holton Career and Resource Center, and urged aligning affordable housing with transit, before Lisa Gordon-Steller presented an update on Durham's 13 charter schools. After a truncated middle section of the transcript, the Board voted 5-0 to suspend its rules and then voted 5-0—on a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, seconded by Vice Chair Howerton, with a friendly amendment from Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow—to allocate $1.1 million for Durham Public Schools classified staff raises while urging DPS to identify matching resources for FY 2016-17. Commissioners then debated a request by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. to have staff prepare a resolution opposing the TPP trade agreement, with Commissioner Reckhow and colleagues urging broader stakeholder and RTP business input before taking a formal position; no vote was taken on TPP, and no split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Annual Organizational Election of Chair and Vice Chair and Bond Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In accordance with North Carolina General Statutes for the first Monday in December, a county official opened the floor for nominations and commissioners unanimously elected Michael D. Page to another term as Chair. Chair Page then opened nominations for Vice Chair, and commissioners unanimously re-elected Brenda A. Howerton. Approval of public official bonds was postponed temporarily because the county risk manager was not yet present.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments (TPP, Pet Waste Ordinance, Holton Center Hours, Transit Housing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Five residents addressed the Board: Heather McLaughlin (NC Alliance for Retired Americans) asked commissioners to oppose the Trans-Pacific Partnership via a resolution shared with Commissioner Fred Foster Jr.; James Chavis and John Tarantino urged a city-county dog-waste ordinance to protect water quality, prompting staff/commissioners to note county legal and animal control review of public right-of-way coverage; Gwen Silver criticized January–February weekend open-gym closures at Holton Career and Resource Center; and Ms. Michael advocated strategically locating affordable housing around transit.

agenda_items.title: Charter School Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Gordon-Steller began a presentation compiled from North Carolina Department of Public Instruction data, audited charter school financials, and Durham Public Schools budget resolutions. She noted Durham County had 13 charter schools in 2015–16, including two newly opened schools (KIPP and Excelsior/Excel Academy), before the middle portion of the transcript digest was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Classified Staff Salary Increase ($1.1 Million Allocation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after truncation during public comment criticizing DPS budget management, commissioners agreed they did not want classified school workers caught in the middle and voted 5-0 to suspend the rules for immediate action. On a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, amended by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved the County Manager's recommendation of $1.1 million for DPS classified staff raises while challenging DPS to find remaining matching funds, utilize enrollment variance data, and incorporate matching resources into the FY 2016-17 budget.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Resolution Opposing the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) Trade Agreement

Reckhow and other commissioners urged deferring action until all business and labor stakeholders could provide input at an upcoming forum.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move forward with staff drafting an anti-TPP resolution for the Board to consider.
side_a_arguments: Labor unions and the AFL-CIO-affiliated NC Alliance for Retired Americans warn TPP will harm local manufacturing workers and erode Durham County's tax base.

meetings.executive_summary: At its November 23, 2015 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (with Deputy County Attorney Willie Darby substituting for Lowell Siler), the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the November 2 and November 9 meeting minutes and approved Consent Agenda Items 15-731 through 15-768—including creation of a Pre-K expansion and early literacy task force highlighted by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs—while pulling Item 15-752. Reckhow, Chair Page and Reckhow clarified that the Board was awaiting financial and budget documentation requested over a month earlier from Durham Public Schools before acting on DPS classified staff pay increases. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page welcomed Deputy County Attorney Willie Darby sitting in for Lowell Siler, added Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's requested Item 5A on DPS classified staff pay increases, and read announcements on United Way healthcare marketplace assistance and senior holiday food drives and events. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the November 2 work session and November 9 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Item 5A: Status Update on Durham Public Schools Classified Staff Pay Increases
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Chair Michael D. Page provided a public update on the status of Durham Public Schools classified employee pay increases. agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 15-731 through 15-768, Excluding Pulled Item 15-752)

agenda_items.title: 2016 Property Reappraisal Briefing and Appeals Schedule

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-11-09 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 9, 2015 regular session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the October 12, 2015 meeting minutes and Consent Agenda Items 729–744 with no items pulled. Commissioners welcomed new Fire Marshal and Emergency Management Director Jim Groves (while honoring interim director Mark Schell), adopted a Veterans Day resolution clarifying that Durham County's Veterans Service Office was not closing, honored 107-year-old World War II veteran Sammy Anderson posthumously, and recognized Hospice and Palliative Care and health-services hotlines. Following public hearings, the Board voted unanimously to approve up to $450,000 in five-year economic development investment funds for Fidelity Investments in Research Triangle Park and a $2.65 million public-private project agreement with Harris Beverage Company for a new headquarters, warehouse, distribution center, and free community meeting space on Junction Road in East Durham. The Board adjourned into closed session for business/industry location discussions by unanimous voice vote, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of October 12, 2015 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting, read announcements including the Low-Income Energy Assistance Program, a county cybersecurity seminar, Veterans Day and Youth Work Summit events, and the My Brother's Keeper feedback session. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board unanimously approved the October 12, 2015 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Staff Introduction and Ceremonial Resolutions (Veterans Day, Sammy Anderson, Hospice Care)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager introduced new Fire Marshal and Emergency Management Director Jim Groves and praised Mark Schell's service as interim director. Chair Page presented a Veterans Day resolution to Veterans Services Director Lois Harvin-Ravin and Reverend Lindsay Atkins (assuring veterans that the county's office was not closing), read a memorial resolution signed by all five commissioners honoring Durham's oldest WWII veteran Sammy Anderson who passed away at age 107, and delivered health and hospice proclamations.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 729–744)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled by commissioners or the public, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded approval of Consent Agenda Items 729 through 744. The motion carried unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Investment Funds for Fidelity Investments ($450,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a five-year, up-to-$450,000 General Fund economic development performance contract supporting Fidelity Investments' job retention and expansion in RTP, aligning with Goal 1 of the county strategic plan. After questions from Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, an uncontested public hearing with no speakers, and commissioner remarks linking corporate incentives to workforce and AP computer science education metrics, the Board unanimously approved the allocation on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Public-Private Project Agreement with Harris Beverage Company ($2.65 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Welton presented a $2.65 million public-private partnership agreement with Harris Beverage Company to build a new headquarters, warehouse, and distribution facility on Junction Road in East Durham, incorporating a community center with meeting space free to residents. Speakers Patrick Byker and Jay Harris addressed the Board during the public hearing, after which commissioners voted unanimously to approve the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location or expansion.
