meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-11-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 2, 2015 work session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard public comments critiquing the Durham–Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS), urging county support for Durham Public Schools (DPS) classified staff raises amid prorated state bonuses, and alleging ADA compliance issues at Durham Technical Community College. Staff presented redevelopment concepts for the Health and Human Services parking lot on the 500 block of East Main Street (Item 15-735), proposing a phased five-story parking deck wrapped with ground-floor commercial, business space, and upper-floor housing, with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow urging coordination with the City and GoTriangle. Following a Juvenile Crime Prevention Council briefing and a truncated middle section of the transcript, commissioners and budget staff reviewed seven analytics pilots and discussed needing clearer, Wake County–style cost-center budget reporting from DPS and possibly an objective facilitator or community education task force before considering a school funding formula. Commissioners also requested staff reports on prisoner re-entry services and state 'sanctuary cities' legislation, reviewed revisions to the draft Pre-K expansion resolution, and adjourned without taking any formal votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment (Light Rail DEIS, DPS Classified Staff Pay, Durham Tech ADA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three speakers addressed the Board: Terry Reckhow submitted 11 pages of objections to the Durham–Orange Light Rail DEIS (citing 35 at-grade crossings and calling for an independent transit consultant); Rachel Efron urged the Board to fund wage increases for DPS classified employees because the state's $750 December bonus was prorated on an eight-hour day; and Victoria Peterson alleged ADA violations at Durham Tech and objected to correspondence from Durham Tech's attorney.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-735: Redevelopment of Health and Human Services Parking Lot (500 Block East Main Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff sought board guidance to focus redevelopment studies on the south side of the 500 block of East Main Street rather than the 300 block, outlining a phased five-story parking structure that doubles parking capacity without losing spaces during construction while wrapping the deck with ground-floor commercial, second-floor walk-up business space, and upper-floor housing. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow referenced a GoTriangle letter on parking needs, emphasized activating the East Main streetscape near the planned City police station, and asked the County Manager to initiate conversations with the City.

agenda_items.title: Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before the middle section of the transcript digest was truncated, presenters noted that JCPC-funded evidence-based community programs provided delinquency and substance-abuse services to over 4,000 young people and families in Durham County.

agenda_items.title: DPS Budget Transparency, Funding Formula, and Education Collaboration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after truncation, budget staff and commissioners discussed seven performance-analytics pilots and pressed for Wake County–style cost-center transparency from Durham Public Schools (noted as the third-highest funded district in North Carolina) before considering a funding formula or MOU changes. Commissioners also discussed teacher satisfaction surveys, the manager's proposal for a community education 'brain trust' or an Excellence in Education task force, and whether an objective facilitator is needed to reduce friction between BOCC and the School Board.

agenda_items.title: Staff Follow-Ups (Re-Entry, Sanctuary City Law) and Pre-K Resolution Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners requested staff information on prisoner re-entry tracking and programs in Durham as well as how newly passed state 'sanctuary cities' legislation would affect local law enforcement, families, and schoolchildren. Commissioners also reviewed minor staff wording updates to the draft Pre-K expansion resolution—envisioning a multi-year pilot scaling toward universal pre-K—before adjourning.

meetings.executive_summary: At its October 12, 2015 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners confirmed participating, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the September 8, 2015 work session minutes, held a ceremonial signing of the Park Center Phase 1 public-private agreement with the Research Triangle Foundation, and adopted proclamations for Residents' Rights Month, Lead Poisoning Prevention Month (Item 703), and National Youth Justice Awareness Month (Item 711). Because no October work session was held, the Board included a 10-speaker citizen comment period (Item 689), during which the middle portion of the transcript digest was truncated just before an unspecified earlier motion concluded. In major economic development and transit actions, the Board voted 5-0 by voice vote to approve a $1.2 million public-private project agreement with Wexford Chesterfield Parking, LLC for redevelopment of the historic Chesterfield Building, voted 5-0 to approve the Durham Innovation District Phase 1 public-private partnership agreement, and voted 5-0 to authorize Chair Page to sign Durham County's comment letter to GoTriangle supporting the Durham–Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement (Item 17-709). Commissioners then met in closed session for nearly an hour on business/industry expansion and adjourned at 9:55 p.m. with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of September 8, 2015 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read the public charge, announced My Brother's Keeper meetings, October 20 and October 27 Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map public meetings for light-rail compact neighborhoods, tree-banding workshops, and Project Access medical equipment loans. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the September 8, 2015 work session minutes, with a commissioner requesting follow-up on baseline data from Alliance Behavioral Health.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Signing (Park Center Phase 1) and Proclamations (Items 703, 711)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners participated in the ceremonial signing of the Park Center Phase 1 public-private agreement with the Research Triangle Foundation to revitalize Research Triangle Park. The Board also presented proclamations recognizing Residents' Rights Month (highlighting 994 residents in adult and family care facilities), Lead Poisoning Prevention Month (Item 703), and National Youth Justice Awareness Month (Item 711).

agenda_items.title: Item 689: Citizen Comment Period (Truncated Middle Section)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page opened the added citizen comment period—scheduled because no October work session was held—with 10 speakers allotted three minutes each. The transcript digest was truncated from 00:49:01 until 01:20:39, where the Board confirmed passage of an unspecified motion from the omitted segment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Not captured in transcript digest (middle truncated)

agenda_items.title: Item 8: Public-Private Project Agreement with Wexford Chesterfield Parking, LLC ($1.2 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marquetta Welton presented a $1.2 million public-private project agreement with Wexford Chesterfield Parking, LLC to redevelop the historic Chesterfield Building and associated parking, citing expected property tax, sales tax, and job gains, with Justin Parker representing Wexford. After thanking staff for new contractor language included in the agreement, the Board approved the partnership 5-0 on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Public-Private Project Agreement for Durham Innovation District Phase 1 Developers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners reviewed the companion public-private partnership agreement for Phase 1 of the Durham Innovation District, aligning with Goal 1 (community prosperity) to create downtown public parking, tax base growth, and renovation of the historic tobacco factory area with ground-floor retail. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board approved the agreement 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-709: Durham–Orange Light Rail DEIS Comment Letter to GoTriangle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With the DEIS public comment period closing October 13, staff and Triangle Transit representatives presented Durham County's draft response letter to GoTriangle. Commissioners expressed strong support for the light-rail project as vital for population growth alongside bus improvements while acknowledging resident feedback and warning against site rework that would delay the project. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board voted 5-0 to authorize Chair Page to sign the letter.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting no items were pulled from the consent agenda, the Board voted 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business/industry location or expansion. Returning to open session at 02:53:24 with direction given to staff, the Board adjourned at 9:55 p.m. on a motion seconded by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-09-28 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 28, 2015 regular meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners announced upcoming My Brother's Keeper feedback sessions, the October 1 public hearing on the Durham–Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement, and a September 29 war memorial meeting, before unanimously approving the September 15, 2015 minutes. Commissioners recognized Durham County's Misdemeanor Diversion Program for winning a Local Government Federal Credit Union Excellence and Innovation Award (noting its expansion to age 21), and issued proclamations for Life Insurance Awareness and Minority Enterprise Development (MED) Week. After a middle truncation in the transcript digest (during which speakers noted the Board voted earlier on zoning), commissioners heard strong support from IBM, former GSK leadership, real estate developers, and CED before unanimously approving Item 680—a $20 million, 10-year public-private project agreement with the Research Triangle Foundation for Park Center Phase 1—on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs. The Board concluded by announcing 13 advisory board and commission appointments across 10 bodies and voting unanimously to enter closed session, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of September 15, 2015 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page led the Pledge of Allegiance, reviewed the public charge, and announced the My Brother's Keeper Durham update and feedback session and a September 29 war memorial enhancement community meeting. At Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's prompt, Page also read announcements for the October 1 light-rail DEIS public hearing and October 13 comment deadline. On a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board unanimously approved the September 15, 2015 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition (Misdemeanor Diversion Program) and Proclamations (Life Insurance, MED Week)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored Durham County's Misdemeanor Diversion Program for receiving a Local Government Federal Credit Union Excellence and Innovation Award at the NCACC conference, noting Commissioner Wendy Jacobs served as a judge and the program had recently expanded through age 21. The Board also presented a Life Insurance Awareness proclamation and proclaimed October 5–9, 2015 as Minority Enterprise Development (MED) Week under Durham County's MWBE ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Item 680: Public-Private Project Agreement with Research Triangle Foundation for Park Center Phase 1 ($20 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a middle transcript truncation (during which speakers noted an earlier zoning vote supporting the project), business and civic leaders—including representatives from IBM, interim CEO Bill Shore, real estate leadership, and Council for Entrepreneurial Development President Joan Rose—urged approval of Park Center Phase 1 to transition RTP toward a walkable live-work-play center. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the $20 million, 10-year public-private project agreement.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page reminded commissioners to reply to the clerk regarding attendance for an upcoming meeting where two members were scheduled out, and the clerk read appointment selections across 10 boards including the Oversight Committee (Harrison Shannon Jr.), DCVB/TDA (Caesar Swift), Historic Preservation Commission (James Lees), Library Board (Beth Fowler), Triangle J Water Resources (Michael Brewer), Workforce Development Board (Farat Ali and James R. Alston), and others. The Board then voted unanimously on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow to adjourn to closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $20 million public-private project agreement over a 10-year period negotiated with the Research Triangle Foundation of North Carolina to support Park Center Phase 1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-09-15 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton with Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Wendy Jacobs present (and Chair Michael D. Page formally excused on September 8 alongside a second absent commissioner, Ellen W. Reckhow), the Durham Board of County Commissioners conducted its September 15, 2015 regular session with all actions passing unanimously 3-0. After approving the August 10 and August 24, 2015 minutes 3-0, the Board proclaimed World Rabies Day (September 28), Bull City Stand Down (September 18), and National POW/MIA Recognition Day—with Commissioner Foster reading the stand-down proclamation and a former Vietnam POW and Duke NROTC commander speaking on the POW/MIA Chair of Honor—as well as Hispanic Heritage Month. Commissioners voted 3-0 to approve Consent Agenda Items 15-592 through 15-649 excluding Items 15-629 and 15-638 pulled by Commissioner Jacobs, held a statutory public hearing with no speakers or required vote on the 2016 Reappraisal Schedule of Values, Standards, and Rules, and then voted 3-0 to approve the two pulled items: a janitorial services contract (Item 15-629) and a $516,887 capital fund balance amendment bringing the Rougemont Community Water System capital budget to $2,636,887 (Item 15-638). No split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Light Rail DEIS Announcements, and Approval of August 10 and 24 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the meeting, read the public charge, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and announced public review details and the September 19 information session and October 1 public hearing for the Durham–Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement. The three present commissioners voted 3-0 by voice vote to approve the August 10 and August 24, 2015 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations (World Rabies Day, Bull City Stand Down / POW-MIA, Hispanic Heritage)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners issued a World Rabies Day proclamation highlighting a free September 28 Sheriff's Office vaccination clinic and noting 28 animal rabies cases in Durham County since 2009. Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. read the 2015 Bull City Stand Down proclamation for homeless veterans at Durham County Memorial Stadium alongside National POW/MIA Recognition Day remarks from a former Vietnam POW and Duke NROTC commander regarding the POW/MIA Chair of Honor, followed by a Hispanic Heritage Month announcement.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 15-592 through 15-649, Excluding 15-629 and 15-638)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs pulled Items 15-629 and 15-638 for discussion and offered supportive comments on Items 15-592 and 15-649, recognizing library staff present in shirts commemorating Congressman John Lewis's visit. The Board approved the remainder of the consent agenda 3-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Public Hearing on 2016 Reappraisal Schedule of Values, Standards, and Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the public hearing required under G.S. 105-317 for the 2016 reappraisal schedule of values, standards, and rules submitted on August 24, 2015. No citizens signed up to speak, and staff confirmed no board vote was required at the hearing.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: Janitorial Contract (15-629) and Rougemont Water System Budget Amendment (15-638)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On Item 15-629 (janitorial services contract), Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned the ranking system and staffing/hour variables across bidders, and staff confirmed thorough vetting. On Item 15-638 (Capital Project Amendment No. 16CPA0002 appropriating $516,887 of capital financing fund balance for a $2,636,887 total Rougemont Community Water System capital budget), Jacobs asked about potential state/EPA Region 4 grants, and staff confirmed the budget reflects re-bid construction maximums that could be lowered if state funds arrive. Both items passed 3-0 by voice vote before adjournment.

votes.notes: Passed 3-0 by voice vote ('Passes 3 to 0'); mover and seconder were not named on microphone. Chair Michael D. Page (formally excused on Sept. 8) and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow were absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the regular session minutes of August 10 and August 24, 2015.

votes.item_title: Approval of Pulled Consent Items 15-629 (Janitorial Contract) and 15-638 (Rougemont Water System Budget Amendment)
votes.notes: Passed 3-0 by voice vote ('Motion passes 3 to 0'); mover and seconder were not named on microphone.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved award of janitorial services contract (Item 15-629) and Budget Ordinance/Capital Project Amendment No. 16CPA0002 appropriating $516,887 in capital financing fund balance for a $2,636,887 total Rougemont Community Water System project budget (Item 15-638).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-09-08 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 8, 2015 meeting presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard public comment alleging severe abuses and medical neglect at the Durham County Jail, pressing for a pet-waste ordinance and investigation of unchained dogs, opposing the renaming of Durham County Memorial Stadium after Willie Bradshaw/Ratcher, and urging swift formation of a Sports Commission/Authority to attract national track meets worth up to $20 million. Commissioners discussed referring the pet-waste enforcement issue to both the Environmental Affairs Board and the Animal Control Advisory Board, and the County Manager began reading a Stadium Authority resolution before a lengthy middle truncation in the transcript digest. Resuming late in the session, commissioners heard tax staff note challenges identifying deed-restricted affordable housing properties during reappraisal, discussed a two-step Board of Health rule and 1993 smoking ordinance update to restrict e-cigarettes (plus a resolution against state tobacco preemption), and reviewed an unbudgeted FY 2016 county property insurance premium increase alongside a planned facility appraisal—placing both the health rule and insurance appraisal on the September 28 consent agenda. Before adjourning at 3:55 p.m., the Board voted unanimously to suspend its rules and excuse Chair Page from the September 15 meeting to attend a My Brother's Keeper event, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment (County Jail Abuse Allegations, Pet Waste Ordinance, Stadium Naming, Sports Authority)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Tiffany alleged unsanitary conditions, guard violence, denial of medication, and falsified diabetic blood-sugar testing at the Durham County Jail, while Eloise Johnson urged adoption of a pet-waste ordinance and investigation of unchained/barking dogs on Evergreen Street and Park Avenue—leading commissioners to refer the ordinance question to both the Environmental Affairs Board and Animal Control Advisory Board. A 30-year Durham County Memorial Stadium Authority member opposed renaming the stadium from its veterans memorial designation (suggesting a plaque or field name instead), while a Durham Striders track coach urged rapid passage of a Sports Commission/Authority resolution before middle transcript truncation.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Reappraisal Identification, E-Cigarettes Health Rule, and Property Insurance Appraisal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following truncation, tax staff noted difficulty obtaining deed-restriction lists from the City to avoid over-assessing affordable housing properties. Public Health staff then outlined a Board of Health rule restricting e-cigarettes (to go on the September 28 consent agenda, followed later by a public hearing to amend the 1993 business smoking ordinance and a resolution opposing state tobacco preemption), and the Risk Manager explained an unplanned FY 2016 property insurance premium increase driven by higher insurable property values, proposing a decennial facility-by-facility appraisal (placed on the September 28 consent agenda).

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Chair Michael D. Page from September 15, 2015 Meeting and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page requested to be excused from the September 15, 2015 meeting to attend a My Brother's Keeper event, while confirming quorum with another commissioner noting she would also be out. The Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules and excuse Chair Page before adjourning at 3:55 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed by unopposed voice vote ('Motion carries unanimously'). Chair Page stated mover as 'Commissioner How[erton]' after earlier cross-talk with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-08-24 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Michael D. Page absent on an excused absence, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 24, 2015 regular meeting with four commissioners present. The board approved excused absences for Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. for the October work session (4-0), approved prior meeting minutes (4-0), and adopted the full consent agenda (4-0), highlighting a $37,498 NCDOT apprentice program grant for Durham County Access (Item 15-621). Ceremonial recognitions included proclaiming September as National Recovery Month in Durham County, acknowledging a 2015 Local Government Federal Credit Union Excellence in Innovation Award for the Criminal Justice Resource Center's Teen Misdemeanor Diversion Program, and issuing a childhood cancer awareness proclamation. Announcements covered the 2016 general tax reappraisal schedule of values opening for public inspection on August 25 ahead of a September 15 public hearing, the upcoming August 28 Federal Register publication and public hearing schedule for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Draft Environmental Impact Statement, and a request to discuss the General Assembly's overdue state budget affecting schools at the next work session. All formal votes were unanimous (4-0), though a tie vote in the ballot appointment for the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee was resolved when one commissioner changed their vote to select Max Bushle.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Excused Absences for October Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton noted Chair Michael D. Page's excused absence and asked for agenda adjustments. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. requested excused absences from the October work session due to a conflicting conference.

agenda_items.title: Announcements: NCACC Election, Tax Reappraisal Schedule, and Light Rail DEIS
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow congratulated Vice Chair Howerton on her election as First Vice President of the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners and displayed the Criminal Justice Resource Center's innovation award for its teen misdemeanor diversion program. Staff and commissioners announced that the 2016 tax reappraisal schedule of values would open for inspection August 25 ahead of a September 15 public hearing, and detailed September 15 and 19 information sessions and an October 1 public hearing on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Draft Environmental Impact Statement.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (July 27, 2015 Regular Session and August 3, 2015 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes for the July 27, 2015 regular session and August 3, 2015 work session. No corrections were offered before a motion to approve.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: National Recovery Month, CJRC Award, and Childhood Cancer Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Foster read a proclamation declaring September as National Recovery Month in Durham County, citing SAMHSA data on co-occurring mental and substance use disorders and treatment gaps. The board also recognized the Criminal Justice Resource Center for its misdemeanor diversion program award and read a childhood cancer proclamation, noting a minor typo to be corrected by the clerk.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 15-593 through 15-621)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the consent agenda. Following the unanimous approval, a commissioner commended staff on Item 15-621, a resolution of support and $37,498 NCDOT PTD apprentice program grant for Durham County Access to expand transportation career internships and apprenticeships.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Request Regarding Delayed State School Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner urged the board to place the state budget impasse on the next work session agenda and raise it at the county commissioners' association level. The speaker noted that counties are legally required to pass budgets by June 30 while the General Assembly had still not enacted a state budget for public schools.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: By ballot, commissioners selected Jerry Link, David Atwater and Mimi Koker (Dangerous Dog Appeal Board), Matthew Herman (Environmental Affairs Board), and Nikita J. Dings (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council). An initial tie for the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee was broken after a commissioner changed their vote, resulting in the selection of Max Bushle.

votes.item_title: Excused Absences for Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. (October Work Session)
votes.notes: Chair Michael D. Page was absent on a previously approved excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioners Reckhow and Foster requested excused absences from the October work session due to a conference conflict.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (July 27, 2015 Regular Session and August 3, 2015 Work Session)

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-08-10 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the August 10, 2015 regular meeting, which opened after a closed-session evaluation of the Sheriff with a unanimous 5-0 vote granting the Sheriff a 3% salary increase retroactive to July 1, 2015. The board unanimously approved (5-0) the 2014 Evaluation and Assessment Report of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (Item 15-579 / Case A-150001) to align city and county Future Land Use Maps and highlight demographic, gentrification, and infrastructure challenges. Staff also presented UDO text amendment TC150003 (Item 15-595) to eliminate off-street parking requirements for affordable housing and expand the density bonus from 1:1 to 3:1 in future rail transit compact neighborhood tiers, though the middle portion of the meeting transcript was truncated before the conclusion of that item. Following an evidentiary public hearing on Wet Rock Farms Conservation Subdivision's non-discharge community water and wastewater pre-treatment system, the board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the Major Special Use Permit, adopt the formal approval order, and approve the Major Site Plan (Item 15-616), with commissioners praising the project as an environmentally sensitive model for Northern Durham.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Action: Sheriff Performance Evaluation and 3% Salary Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a closed-session evaluation with the Sheriff, Chair Michael D. Page thanked the Sheriff for his service in the jail and county system. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved, seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, to grant the Sheriff a 3% salary increase retroactive to July 1, 2015.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Consent Agenda Introduction (Items 15-574 through 15-618)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner announced local events for the September 21 UN International Day of Peace. Chair Page introduced the consent agenda (Items 15-574 through 15-618) and clarified that Item 15-595 was a public hearing item rather than part of consent, before the transcript moved directly to public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-579: Public Hearing on 2014 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (Case A-150001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carla Rosenberg of the Planning Department presented the 2014 EAR, rectifying city and county Future Land Use Maps (including the Rougemont county amendment), updating open space and agricultural layers, and noting an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Commissioners praised the report's analysis of demographic shifts, gentrification, walkability, and infrastructure deficits, and closed the public hearing with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-595: Public Hearing on UDO Text Amendment — Affordable Housing Parking and Density Bonus (TC150003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Aaron King of the Planning Department presented TC150003, stemming from the four-part affordable housing strategy around future rail transit stations, to remove off-street parking minimums for affordable dwelling units and expand the density bonus from 1:1 to 3:1 (with a by-right height bonus) in the compact neighborhood tier. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 10-1 on June 9, 2015; the transcript digest is truncated during commissioner Q&A before any vote is recorded.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Wet Rock Farms Conservation Subdivision — Major Special Use Permit and Approval Order
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board heard technical testimony regarding a non-discharge community water and wastewater pre-treatment system for the Wet Rock Farms conservation subdivision, featuring cluster wells, telemetry controls, backup generators, a state-licensed operator, and daily inspections exceeding state weekly mandates. Applicant counsel argued all UDO requirements were met, and the board approved both the Major Special Use Permit and the formal approval order.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-616: Wet Rock Farms Conservation Subdivision — Major Site Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners praised the Wet Rock Farms major site plan for exceeding primary open space requirements, harmonizing with rural public roads, and serving as a model residential development for Northern Durham soils. One commissioner also encouraged incorporating a future US 501 bus shelter into the plan.

votes.item_title: 3% Retroactive Salary Increase for Sheriff
votes.discussion_detail: Motion made immediately upon returning from a closed-session performance evaluation with the Sheriff, granting a 3% salary increase retroactive to July 1, 2015.

votes.item_title: Item 15-579: 2014 Evaluation and Assessment Report of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (Case A-150001)
votes.notes: Planning Commission recommended approval 11-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved following Planning Department presentation and public hearing with no speakers.

votes.item_title: Wet Rock Farms Conservation Subdivision Major Special Use Permit
votes.notes: Staff confirmed recommendation of approval based on evidence in the staff report and hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: Quasi-judicial approval of the Major Special Use Permit for a non-discharge community water and wastewater system serving Wet Rock Farms conservation subdivision.

votes.item_title: Order Approving Wet Rock Farms Conservation Subdivision Major Special Use Permit
votes.notes: Mover and seconder names were garbled in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Formal adoption of the written order approving the Major Special Use Permit as directed.

votes.item_title: Item 15-616: Wet Rock Farms Conservation Subdivision Major Site Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the major site plan after commissioners praised its open-space preservation and compatibility with rural Northern Durham.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-08-03 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the August 3, 2015 work session, where no formal policy votes were taken beyond adjournment. During citizen comments, residents raised concerns over staffing and a $1 lease at the Holton Career and Resource Center, urged action on stadium naming without awaiting a formal policy, and asked commissioners to strengthen the wireless communication facilities (cell tower) UDO text amendment with ongoing structural inspection and maintenance protocols. Following a truncated middle segment, commissioners discussed potential board and commission rule revisions—including a one-year cooling-off period after eight years of service, exempting partial unexpired terms under one year from term limits, and creating a hot-vacancy list. The session concluded with a substantive debate over how to respond to the Inside-Outside Alliance campaign and a News & Observer article on County Jail lockback restrictions, with Chair Page and Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow urging direct discussions with the Sheriff and potential outside technical review by the National Institute of Corrections or Bureau of Justice Assistance, while another commissioner argued the board lacked authority over an independently elected Sheriff and noted lockbacks were implemented to address gang violence.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Holton Resource Center, Facility Naming, and Cell Tower UDO Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: James Shavers criticized understaffing at the Holton Career and Resource Center's special-needs youth programs and the $1 lease of an East Durham recreation facility to East DCI, while another speaker urged the board to vote on a stadium naming request without delay. Neighborhood speakers including Dolly Baremahr (Good Neighbors of 751 Durham) raised concerns that revised cell tower UDO drafts lacked post-construction structural integrity and maintenance inspection protocols; Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked to add the item ahead of Wednesday's JCCPC meeting, though Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton noted she was unprepared to debate an unscheduled topic.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Rules, Term Limits, and Vacancy Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the work session, commissioners reviewed rules governing board and commission appointments, including displaying current term numbers online and requiring a one-year break after eight years of service. Commissioners discussed amending the rules so unexpired terms of less than one year do not count toward maximum term limits and considered publishing a hot-vacancy list to aid recruitment.

agenda_items.title: County Jail Lockback Policy and Inside-Outside Alliance Demands
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff alerted the board to an expected surge of constituent inquiries following a News & Observer article on jail restrictions and an Inside-Outside Alliance letter-writing campaign demanding an end to lockbacks, an independent jail audit, and elimination of jail fees. Commissioners debated whether to press the Sheriff in closed session and invite outside technical assistance from the Bureau of Justice Assistance or National Institute of Corrections, or avoid an adversarial confrontation given the Sheriff's independent authority and security concerns over gang violence.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-08-03 9:00 AM - Worksession
disagreements.issue: Board Oversight and Response to Durham County Jail Lockbacks and Audit Demands
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed over how proactively the Board of County Commissioners should intervene with the Sheriff regarding prolonged jail lockbacks, inmate complaints, and community demands for an independent audit.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold direct discussions with the Sheriff on inmate conditions and pursue constructive outside review or technical assistance.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners have a responsibility to respond to citizen and inmate complaints about excessive idle time during lockbacks and deteriorating conditions.

Inviting a nationally recognized body such as the Bureau of Justice Assistance or National Institute of Corrections for technical assistance would be better received and more constructive than a punitive audit.
disagreements.side_b_position: Recognize the Sheriff's independent authority as an elected official and avoid repeating adversarial confrontations over security measures.
side_b_arguments: The County Commissioners do not control jail operations because the Sheriff is an independently elected official.
The Sheriff implemented lockbacks to protect staff and inmates amid gang-related safety threats, and repeated questioning without new facts will not change conditions.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Page concluded the discussion by noting staff had direction on next steps and the board would revisit the matter with the Sheriff in closed session; no formal vote was taken.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-07-27 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the July 27, 2015 regular meeting, which featured six unanimous 5-0 votes and zero split decisions. The board granted excused absences to Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow for September 14 and Chair Page for August 24, approved prior meeting minutes, and celebrated multiple NACo Achievement Awards won by Durham County's Information Services and Technology, Library, and Tax Administration departments. Commissioners approved the consent agenda (Items 15-497 through 15-577) excluding pulled Item 15-531 while highlighting nearly $100,000 in new library grants, and subsequently passed pulled Item 15-531 (six county parking lot restorations) 5-0 after Commissioner Reckhow added a strict compliance-with-laws contract clause. After making balloted appointments to five boards and commissions and returning from a recessed closed session reviewing county appointees, the board voted 5-0 to award a 3% salary increase effective July 1, 2015 to the County Manager, County Attorney, Tax Administrator, Register of Deeds, and Clerk to the Board.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, NACo Awards, and Commissioner Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced 2015 NACo Achievement Awards for IS&T's EMS Protocol mobile website, three Durham County Library initiatives, and Tax Administration's online property tax appeal system. Commissioners granted excused absences for Ellen W. Reckhow (September 14) and Michael D. Page (August 24), and noted their recent tour of Charlotte's light rail and maintenance facility during the NACo conference.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (April 13, June 1, and June 22, 2015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered minutes from the April 13 regular session, June 1 work session, and June 22 regular session. Commissioner Reckhow moved and Commissioner Jacobs seconded approval.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-538: Citizen Comments and Ceremonial Recognition of IS&T Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No citizens signed up to speak during the Item 15-538 comment period. The board then recognized IS&T Director Greg Merrill for six national awards won across three IT effectiveness areas, alongside Library Director Tammy Baggett and EMS Director Skip Kirkwood.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 15-497 through 15-577, excluding Item 15-531)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted three library grants totaling nearly $100,000 in the consent agenda (Teen Tech Learning Lab, Latino Americans 500 Years of History, and Digital Bridge Project Initiative). After Commissioner Reckhow pulled Item 15-531 for separate discussion, the remaining consent agenda was approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners cast ballots for appointments to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, Women's Commission, Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (Marjorie Lipscomb and Dayia Salt), Durham-Wake Counties Research and Production Service District (Eddie Sales, Stephanie McDougall, Juanita Julian, Chris F. Bootbooks), and Industrial Facilities & Pollution Control Financing Authority (Anthony Gallup and John Mars).

agenda_items.title: Item 15-531: Six Parking Lots Restoration Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow pulled Item 15-531, covering restoration of six county parking lots (Agricultural Building, Criminal Justice Resource Center, Milton Road EMS Station 6, Animal Shelter, East Main Street, and Liberty Street), to insert an explicit clause requiring strict compliance with all federal, state, and local laws. The board approved the contract with the added clause.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Evaluations and 3% Salary Increase for Appointed County Officials
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recessed back into closed session to complete performance evaluations of the County Manager, County Attorney, Tax Administrator, Register of Deeds, and Clerk to the Board. Upon returning to open session, the board approved a 3% salary increase for all five officials effective July 1, 2015.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Ellen W. Reckhow (September 14, 2015 Meeting)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Reckhow requested an excused absence for September 14 while attending Advanced Leadership Training.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Michael D. Page (August 24, 2015 Meeting)
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Page requested an excused absence from the August 24, 2015 regular meeting because he would be out of town.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (April 13, June 1, and June 22, 2015)
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of three sets of prior meeting minutes.

votes.item_title: Item 15-531: Six Parking Lots Restoration Contract (with Compliance with Laws Clause)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved restoration contract for six county parking lots with an added clause requiring strict contractor compliance with all federal, state, and local laws.

votes.item_title: 3% Salary Increase for Appointed County Officials (Effective July 1, 2015)
votes.discussion_detail: Following closed-session performance evaluations, the board approved a 3% salary increase effective July 1, 2015 for the County Manager, County Attorney, Tax Administrator, Register of Deeds, and Clerk to the Board.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-06-22 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the June 22, 2015 regular meeting with a moment of silence for former Commissioner Lewis Cheek and the victims in Charleston, South Carolina, followed by unanimous approval (5-0) of prior minutes and ceremonial recognitions for Public Health nurses Kathy Hines and Jacqueline Melvin, Tax Administrator Kim for a NACo online tax appeal award, and outgoing Deputy County Manager E. Lee Worsley. County Manager Wendell Davis presented the FY 2015–16 budget ordinance (without a tax increase), though the middle portion of the transcript digest was truncated before the budget vote occurred. Following a public hearing on a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment to restore independent senior living facilities with reduced parking (highlighted by the Bartlett Reserve adaptive reuse project), the board unanimously adopted both the NCGS 153A-341 consistency statement (5-0) and the UDO ordinance amendment (5-0). Commissioners also discussed releasing the Sheriff's written answers regarding jail conditions, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs flagging inaccuracies regarding an unapproved $10-to-$20 jail medical fee increase and the lack of weekend mental health coverage, before entering closed session (5-0) on economic development.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence and Approval of Minutes (May 4, June 1, and June 8, 2015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board observed a moment of silence for former County Commissioner Lewis Cheek and the Charleston, South Carolina tragedy. Commissioners then unanimously approved the minutes from May 4, June 1, and June 8, 2015.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Public Health Staff, Tax Administration Award, and Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board honored Public Health Nurse Kathy Hines (2015 Communicable Disease Nurse Spirit Award) and Community Disease Control Specialist Jacqueline Melvin (21 years combating HIV/AIDS), as well as Tax Administrator Kim for a NACo Achievement Award for the online property tax appeal system ahead of the 2016 revaluation. Commissioners also adopted and presented a farewell resolution honoring outgoing Deputy County Manager E. Lee Worsley, who was departing to lead Triangle J Council of Governments.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Presentation of FY 2015–16 Budget Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis introduced the FY 2015–16 budget ordinance as a strategic maintenance plan achieved without a property tax increase as directed at the March retreat. The transcript digest is truncated shortly after his opening remarks, omitting subsequent deliberations and any vote on the budget ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment for Independent Senior Living Facilities (Articles 5, 10, and 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker spoke in support of the applicant-initiated UDO text amendment facilitating independent senior living facilities such as Bartlett Reserve's adaptive reuse of an extended-stay hotel off Highway 55, noting the recent passing of developer Morgan Burkett. Commissioners Reckhow, Jacobs, and Howerton praised the amendment for restoring a missing senior housing category with lower parking ratios, and passed both the consistency statement and the ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-511: Board Appointments and Public Release of Sheriff's Jail Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While board and commission ballots were tallied, commissioners discussed making the Sheriff's written answers on jail conditions public. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs objected to an answer implying BOCC approved doubling the jail medical copay from $10 to $20—requesting a factual addendum noting commissioners never discussed or approved the fee hike and that indigent inmates are not charged—and raised concern over the absence of weekend mental health services at the jail.

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Closed Session on Economic Development (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business location or expansion matters. Upon returning in open session at 10:57 PM, Chair Page stated the board provided direction to staff before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (June 8 Regular, June 1 Budget Work Session, May 4 Work Session)
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of minutes from three May and June 2015 meetings.

votes.item_title: Statement of Consistency (NCGS 153A-341) for Independent Senior Living UDO Text Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the statutory statement of consistency ahead of adopting the UDO text amendment for independent senior living facilities.

votes.item_title: Ordinance Amending UDO Articles 5, 10, and 16 (Independent Senior Living Facilities)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO revisions to Article 5 (Use Regulations), Article 10 (Parking and Loading), and Article 16 (Definitions) to support independent senior living housing.

votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session to discuss matters relating to the location or expansion of a business or industry.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-06-08 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: With Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presiding in Chair Michael D. Page's absence, the four commissioners present unanimously approved (4-0) prior minutes and the consent agenda (Items 15-444 through 15-489) excluding pulled Item 15-444. The board held a major public hearing on the FY 2015–16 recommended budget with over 50 registered speakers—including Durham Public Schools teachers, parents, and Teamsters-represented bus drivers and classified staff—who urged commissioners to fully fund the School Board's budget request and provide 3% raises for support personnel. Following two separate public hearings on Item 15-434 presented by Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley to finalize the Parkwood-Bethesda fire merger at a unified 13-cent tax rate, the board voted 4-0 to create the Durham County Fire and Rescue Service District and 4-0 to abolish the Bethesda Fire and Rescue Service Tax District. Commissioners also approved pulled Item 15-444 (4-0) after Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requested staff follow-up on serious repair needs at the Animal Protection Society shelter, and voted 4-0 to enter closed session on economic development.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes (May 11 and May 26, 2015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requested an end-of-meeting discussion on listening remotely to the June 15 Joint County and School Board budget meeting, and an announcement recognized the Health Department opening five school-based health assessment clinics. The board unanimously approved the May 11 and May 26, 2015 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 15-444 through 15-489, excluding Item 15-444)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner pulled Item 15-444 for follow-up questions at the end of the agenda. The board unanimously approved the remainder of the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2015–16 Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With 51–52 speakers signed up (allotted two minutes each), residents, veterans' advocates, DPS teachers, parents, and Teamsters-affiliated bus drivers, custodians, and cafeteria staff urged the board to fully fund the School Board's budget and end multi-year pay freezes with a 3% classified staff raise. Commissioners thanked the overflow crowd for their participation and closed the public hearing without holding budget deliberations that evening.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-434: Public Hearings Creating Durham County Fire and Rescue Service District and Abolishing Bethesda District
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley explained that the two resolutions completed the merger of the Parkwood and Bethesda fire departments serving RTP and South Durham under a unified 13-cent tax rate (with Parkwood's legacy rural district set to zero). After hearing one speaker on the creation hearing and none on the abolishment hearing, the board adopted both resolutions unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-444: Animal Protection Society (APS) Budget and Shelter Facility Repairs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs pulled Item 15-444 to ask how serious facility repair needs flagged in an APS letter—including roof leaks, peeling ceiling paint, security and phone systems, and covered cages—would be addressed under the county's contract. Staff agreed to investigate and report back, and the board approved the item 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Remote Participation Protocol for June 15 Joint Meeting and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff agreed to check the protocol for Commissioner Jacobs to listen remotely to the June 15 Joint County and School Board budget meeting while away, noting Commissioner Reckhow had previously listened by phone without voting. The board then voted 4-0 to enter closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business location or expansion.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (May 11, 2015 and May 26, 2015 Regular Sessions)

Page presided over the June 1, 2015 work session, which opened with a joint presentation from downtown churches (including First Presbyterian Church) urging the county to pursue a public-private partnership wrapping affordable housing and retail around the planned East Main Street parking deck near the future light rail station rather than building a standalone garage. agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Removal of Board/Commission Members for Lack of Attendance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After verifying that the notice deadline had passed the previous Friday, commissioners voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and then 5-0 to remove four individuals from their respective boards and commissions due to lack of attendance. agenda_items.title: Agenda Prep Efficiency and Closed Session on Economic Development

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-05-26 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the May 26, 2015 regular meeting with four commissioners present (Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow had an excused absence). agenda_items.title: Item 5: County Manager's Recommended FY 2015–16 Budget Presentation

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the May 11, 2015 regular meeting, which celebrated the 40th anniversary of Durham County EMS and proclaimed May 17–23 as EMS Week, while approving April 27 minutes (5-0) and selecting five members to the Durham County Hospital Corporation board. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-05-11 7:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Elected-Official Voting Seat on the Restructured Durham Workforce Development Board (Item 15-407)
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-2 over whether to adopt staff-recommended Option 1 (Schedule B1), which replaced elected-official voting representation on the Durham Workforce Development Board with non-voting liaisons, versus Option B2 retaining a voting seat.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Option 1 (Schedule B1) as recommended by staff, making the city and county elected-body appointees non-voting liaisons on a 25-member board.
side_a_arguments: Option 1 follows staff's recommended structure under the transition from WIA to WIOA.
The county already holds appointments on the board including vocational rehabilitation and educational slots such as Durham Technical Community College.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose Option 1 and preserve a voting elected-official voice (Option B2) to advocate directly for jobs and workforce development.
side_b_arguments: Job creation and employment opportunities are a top campaign and policy priority for county commissioners, so the county should not voluntarily give up its voting voice on the Workforce Development Board.
Option B2 would allow a voting board member slot alongside non-voting liaisons.
disagreements.resolution: Option 1 (Schedule B1) passed 3-2 by voice vote (Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. plus one additional commissioner in favor; Michael D. Page and one additional commissioner opposed, with Brenda A. Howerton having queried Option B2 before the vote).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-05-04 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the May 4, 2015 work session, an informational session with no formal votes beyond adjournment. Citizens opened the meeting with urgent testimony regarding conditions at the Durham County Detention Center, alleging 48-hour lockbacks without showers, confiscation of reading materials other than the Bible, and questioning nearly $1 million in jail commissary revenue. Commissioners heard staff introductions from the County Attorney's office, a presentation on the Piedmont Food and Agricultural Processing Center's shared-use kitchen incubator, and the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission's annual report highlighting a 120% six-year rise in bike commuting and Complete Streets priorities. Following a truncated middle section, Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. led a consensus discussion—supported by Chair Page and Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow—directing the County Manager to draft a tailored NACo mental health and jail diversion resolution showcasing Durham's Crisis Access Center and Crisis Intervention Teams ahead of national funding opportunities, alongside an update on senior and veteran homestead tax relief outreach.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Durham County Detention Center Lockbacks and Reading Materials
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Carolyn Adams, Stephanie Gens, and others testified on behalf of inmates at the Durham County Detention Center, criticizing 48-hour lockbacks without showers and the removal of books and reading materials other than the Bible, while questioning jail commissary funds. A separate speaker invited commissioners to a May 20 Golden Toast senior celebration.

agenda_items.title: County Attorney Staff Introductions and Piedmont Food & Agricultural Processing Center Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney introduced assistant attorney Nathan McKinney (child support) and returning attorney Willie Darby. The board then received a briefing on the Piedmont Food and Agricultural Processing Center incubator, which saves food startups over $140,000 in capital upfit costs and helps graduating businesses relocate into Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BPAC presented its annual report with staff liaison Dale McKeel, noting 17 voting members, site plan reviews for UDO compliance, aging 10-year-old bicycle and pedestrian plans needing updates, and a 120% six-year increase in Durham residents commuting by bicycle. The presentation emphasized Complete Streets policies for pedestrian, cyclist, and neighborhood equity and safety.

agenda_items.title: NACo Mental Health and Jail Diversion Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle segment, Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. proposed adopting a tailored NACo resolution on reducing mental illness and substance abuse in county jails to position Durham for federal Bureau of Justice Assistance technical assistance and grant funding. Commissioners Jacobs, Reckhow, and Page agreed, noting over 50% of jail detainees face mental health or substance issues and directing County Manager Wendell Davis to draft a version highlighting Durham's Crisis Access Center and CIT policing.

agenda_items.title: Homestead Property Tax Relief Outreach for Seniors, Disabled Residents, and Veterans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff highlighted strong community demand for property tax relief applications for elderly, disabled, and veteran homeowners (with income thresholds of $29,000 and $43,500), noting that 50 copies distributed through Social Services were claimed quickly.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-27 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 27, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all procedural, consent, and closed-session motions by 5-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. Commissioners granted Ellen W. Reckhow an excused absence for the May 26 meeting, approved draft minutes from the March 2 work session and 2015 budget retreat, approved the consent agenda, and conducted ballot voting for board and commission appointments including two at-large seats on the Adult Care Home Advisory Committee. Ceremonial recognitions included a proclamation for Children's Mental Health Awareness Month and memorial resolutions honoring the late Dr. Joseph F. Han (for his service to Durham Public Schools and Rougemont water resolution efforts) and the late Coach Willie R. Bradshaw (former Hillside High School coach, DPS athletic director, and Stadium Authority member), during which Pastor Frederick Amos Davis formally requested naming Durham County Stadium after Coach Bradshaw and Chair Page referred the request to a future work session. The Board then adjourned into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development business location/expansion matters, returning to open session to report that staff had been given direction before adjourning at 9:05 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence Request, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting with the public charge and Pledge of Allegiance. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested an excused absence for the second regular meeting in May (Tuesday, May 26), which the Board approved unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton. Commissioners also announced the May 2 Aging Well Conference at the Durham County Human Services Building and celebrated Durham native and DPS graduate Loretta Lynch taking the oath of office as U.S. Attorney General.

agenda_items.title: Approval of March 2, 2015 Work Session and 2015 Budget Retreat Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the draft minutes from the March 2, 2015 work session and the 2015 budget retreat. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes were approved unanimously without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation for Children's Mental Health Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a proclamation recognizing Children's Mental Health Awareness Month, presented to a representative for Rob Robinson. Speakers highlighted how community openness and system-of-care leadership help families support loved ones living with mental health needs while retaining employment.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution Honoring Dr. Joseph F. Han
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a memorial resolution honoring the late Dr. Joseph F. Han, noting his education, career in educational measurement, service with Durham Public Schools, and civic engagement. Mark Peeterman of the North Carolina Underground Storage Tank Program and family and community speakers praised Dr. Han's long-standing work to resolve the Rougemont community's water problem, election poll volunteering, and Easter parade organizing before his passing.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution Honoring Coach Willie R. Bradshaw and Stadium Naming Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution paying tribute to the late Coach Willie R. Bradshaw (1928–2015), a Hillside High School graduate, Negro League baseball pitcher, longtime Hillside football and basketball coach, first African American athletic director for Durham Public Schools, and Durham County Stadium Authority member. Pastor Frederick Amos Davis requested that Durham County Stadium be named in honor of Coach Bradshaw, and daughter Natalin Bradshaw Haile Selassie thanked the Board on behalf of the family. Chair Page stated the naming request would be placed on an upcoming work session agenda for review with the County Attorney.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented the consent agenda (referencing items including 15-273, 15-339, 15-352, and 15-362). Without items pulled for separate discussion, the Board approved the consent agenda unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed ballot instructions for board and commission appointments, clarifying with staff that two at-large positions were open on the Adult Care Home Advisory Committee. Ballots were completed and collected, and Chair Page thanked the volunteers selected to serve.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss the location or expansion of a business or industry. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-13 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 13, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all action items by voice vote, with no split votes, though commissioners aired pointed policy and procedural disagreements over Item 15-383 regarding sidewalk maintenance near Forest View Elementary and Solterra Way. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton objected to information being shared with only one commissioner and questioned why Solterra Way did not appear on the priority list, while Chair Page expressed discomfort over equity across communities before the Board unanimously passed a three-item package (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Wendy Jacobs) establishing a comprehensive pedestrian connectivity plan focused on county school facilities and appointing Reckhow and Howerton to a follow-up committee. The Board also approved Item 15-372 (a $26,955 capital financing fund balance appropriation and capital project amendment for an SAP human capital management cloud software upgrade) and Item 15-384 (authorizing NCDMV to distribute Durham County's $7 vehicle registration tax directly to GoTriangle and allowing staff to transfer funds already collected). Earlier in the meeting, the Board approved March 10 Redwood community meeting and March 23 regular session minutes and presented ceremonial items for the Week of the Young Child and the late Dr. Frank Alexander 'Andy' Barrada Jr.

agenda_items.title: Opening Ceremonies, Announcements, and Approval of March 10 and March 23, 2015 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page led the Pledge of Allegiance and announcements, highlighting County Manager Wendell Davis on 'In Touch with Durham County', board recruitment, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs's announcement of an April 21 exporting and Foreign Trade Zone seminar at RTP headquarters. Reviewing the March 10 Redwood community meeting and March 23 regular session minutes, Jacobs requested staff follow-up on Redwood residents' septic, city water hookup, and illegal road dumping concerns, which the County Manager confirmed had been assigned. The minutes passed unanimously on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation for Week of the Young Child
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented a proclamation recognizing the Week of the Young Child to board members Delphine Sellars (Durham's Partnership for Children) and Dan Hodges (Child Care Services Association). Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow praised both organizations' early-childhood readiness work and emphasized recent research supporting prenatal and early-years investments.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution Honoring Dr. Frank Alexander 'Andy' Barrada Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read a memorial resolution honoring Durham rheumatologist Dr. Frank Alexander 'Andy' Barrada Jr., who passed away on February 8, 2015 after more than 30 years of medical service and community volunteerism including Project Access and Senior PharmAssist. Commissioners and guests shared personal reflections before presenting the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-383: Sidewalk Maintenance Policy and School Pedestrian Connectivity Package
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, commissioners debated sidewalk maintenance around Forest View Elementary / Solterra Way and countywide pedestrian equity. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton criticized staff information going to only one commissioner and questioned why Solterra Way was absent from the list, while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs clarified the email chain and noted Item 13 (Randolph Road sidewalk) used a different funding pot, and Chair Page urged making NCDOT funding opportunities visible to all communities. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the three-item package (including a comprehensive pedestrian connectivity plan focused on school facilities), with Chair Page appointing Reckhow and Howerton to a committee and a commissioner stressing the need to fund long-term sidewalk maintenance.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-372: Capital Project and Budget Amendment for SAP Human Capital Management Upgrade
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The IT Director and HR Director presented Item 15-372 to create a new Human Capital Management SAP software upgrade capital project moving on-premise HR systems to the cloud, close out the FY12 HR upgrade and FY12 BW capital projects, and adopt Budget Amendment 15BCC052 appropriating $26,955 from capital financing fund balance. The Board approved the item unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-384: Resolution on $7 Vehicle Registration Tax Distribution to GoTriangle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County legal staff presented a resolution authorizing the North Carolina DMV to distribute Durham County's $7 vehicle registration tax directly to Triangle Transit Authority (GoTriangle) to support the Durham County Bus and Rail Investment Plan and DATA bus service, and requested authority for county finance staff to transfer funds already collected. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the resolution and transfer authorization before adjourning at 9:20 p.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 10, 2015 Redwood Community Meeting and March 23, 2015 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Carried unanimously by voice vote. Confirmed present in digest: Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; Fred Foster Jr. presence not independently confirmed in the truncated digest (no absence announced).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requested staff follow-up on Redwood resident concerns regarding failed septic systems, city water hookups, and road dumping.

votes.item_title: Item 15-383: Sidewalk Maintenance Action Package
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote with no opposition voiced following extended deliberation on board communication and geographic equity.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the three-item package as listed on the agenda, including developing a comprehensive plan for improved pedestrian connectivity focused on school facilities throughout Durham County, after confirming with County Attorney Tyler that the three-item motion posed no legal issue.

votes.item_title: Item 15-372: SAP Human Capital Management Upgrade Capital Project and Budget Amendment 15BCC052 ($26,955)
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Creates the new SAP HR cloud upgrade capital project, transfers unspent funds and closes FY12 HR upgrade and FY12 BW capital projects, and appropriates $26,955 of capital financing fund balance.

votes.item_title: Item 15-384: NCDMV Distribution of $7 Vehicle Registration Tax to GoTriangle and Transfer of Collected Funds
votes.notes: Motion carried unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorizes NCDMV to remit the $7 county vehicle registration tax directly to GoTriangle in support of DATA and the Durham County Bus and Rail Investment Plan, and amends staff recommendation to allow finance staff to transfer previously collected revenues.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-13 7:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Board Communication, Equity Across Communities, and Sidewalk Maintenance Package (Item 15-383)
disagreements.summary: Before voting unanimously to approve Item 15-383, commissioners disagreed over staff information distribution, why Solterra Way / Forest View Elementary was prioritized without appearing on the general list, and how to ensure equitable sidewalk investments and maintenance resources across all Durham communities.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support approving the three-item sidewalk maintenance package (including Forest View / Solterra Way and a countywide school pedestrian connectivity plan), clarifying that separate NCDOT funding pots drove the item.
side_a_arguments: Item 13 on the priority list (Randolph Road sidewalk from Pickett Road to Irwin Road) is funded from a different NCDOT pot than the Solterra Way project.
The three-item package pairs immediate action with a comprehensive plan for improved pedestrian connectivity focused on school facilities throughout Durham County.
disagreements.side_b_position: Express discomfort with one-commissioner staff communications, lack of awareness of NCDOT funding pots in other neighborhoods, and potential unfunded sidewalk maintenance liabilities.
side_b_arguments: Sending staff information to a single commissioner leaves the rest of the Board out of the loop; all materials should be distributed to the entire Board.

While Irwin and Randolph Roads need pedestrian safety measures, Durham County must inform other communities of available DOT funding pots and ensure resources are distributed equitably across the county.
Taking on sidewalk maintenance requires mobilizing dedicated maintenance funding before sidewalks deteriorate.
disagreements.resolution: The Board unanimously passed the three-item Item 15-383 package by voice vote, and Chair Page appointed Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton to a committee to advance the broader policy and resource framework.
