meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-06 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 6, 2015 Work Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners took no substantive formal votes (adjourning at 4:56 p.m.) while conducting lengthy deliberations on a county sidewalk maintenance policy tied to NCDOT's Forest View Elementary / Solterra Way offer and reviewing accountability in the county's $818,000 nonprofit funding pool. During citizen comments, Durham Council of PTAs president Anne Rebek, BPAC representatives, and nearby residents urged accepting NCDOT's offer to build a 170-to-177-foot sidewalk extension and pedestrian signal at Irwin and Randolph Roads, while other speakers opposed renewing the library security contract with G4S and urged living wages and diverse hiring for security workers. On the sidewalk policy, commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow advocated a limited policy accepting long-term maintenance for NCDOT-funded sidewalks serving county school sites outside city limits, whereas Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton sought assurances that other areas such as Cook Road would not be left behind and another commissioner questioned taking on open-ended taxpayer maintenance costs. Because NCDOT needed a county stance by the end of April to spend funds by June, the Board directed staff (Drew Cummings and Mark Ahrendsen) to verify written project details and return on April 13 with a draft resolution and interim policy.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Forest View Elementary Sidewalks and Library Security Contract (G4S)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page capped citizen comments at two minutes per speaker due to a 30-minute limit. PTA Council president Anne Rebek, a BPAC speaker, and neighborhood parents urged the Board to accept NCDOT's offer for a sidewalk extension and traffic/pedestrian signal at Forest View Elementary (Irwin and Randolph Roads) on a case-by-case basis. Additional speakers opposed awarding a new library security contract to G4S over alleged human rights abuses and urged the county to protect existing workers, pay a living wage, and ensure diverse hiring.

agenda_items.title: School Sidewalk Gaps and Draft County Sidewalk Maintenance Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Drew Cummings and transportation planner Mark Ahrendsen presented maps of school sidewalk gaps outside and near city limits (including Forest View Elementary, Oak Grove / Olive Branch Road, and Mangum Elementary) and reviewed BPAC and Board of Health Complete Streets support. Commissioners discussed whether gaps wholly inside city limits should remain the city's responsibility and examined NCDOT's requirement that a local government execute a long-term maintenance encroachment agreement before construction can proceed.

agenda_items.title: Nonprofit Funding Accountability and $818,000 Pool Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, County Manager Wendell Davis and commissioners (including Wendy Jacobs and Fred Foster Jr.) reviewed performance reporting from nonprofit agencies receiving county funds from the $818,000 pool. They noted wide variation in report quality and regional/national organizations' data, calling for sharper staff analysis of Durham County-specific resident impacts, cost per dollar, and potential overlap.

agenda_items.title: NCDOT Forest View / Irwin & Randolph Encroachment Scope and April 13 Direction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported from discussions with the NCDOT District 5 Engineer that NCDOT must spend the funds by the end of June, required a county decision by the end of April, and preferred a local government maintenance signatory (while allowing secondary agreements with an HOA or DPS). Commissioners debated approving only the Forest View / Solterra resolution versus an interim limited school-sidewalk policy while Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton pressed for equity assurances for other communities such as Cook Road. Staff was directed to obtain written scope confirmation (up to 177 feet of sidewalk on both sides of Irwin Road, signal, crosswalk, and pedestrian lighting) and bring a draft policy and resolution to the April 13 regular session before adjourning at 4:56 p.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-04-06 9:00 AM
disagreements.issue: County Sidewalk Maintenance Responsibility and Geographic Equity (Forest View / Solterra vs. Other Communities)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners debated whether Durham County should adopt an interim policy accepting long-term maintenance for NCDOT-funded school sidewalks or act only on the urgent Forest View Elementary / Solterra Way offer while addressing equity concerns across other county corridors.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support a limited interim policy accepting long-term maintenance when NCDOT constructs sidewalks near county schools outside city limits, enabling immediate acceptance of the Forest View / Irwin-Randolph safety project before NCDOT's deadline.
side_a_arguments: NCDOT requires a decision by late April to spend funds by June and will not proceed without a local government maintenance commitment.
A narrow interim policy limited to NCDOT-funded school connections outside city limits addresses urgent student safety while leaving broader policy coordination for DPS and the City of Durham.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question why this specific intersection was prioritized over other underserved areas and warn against taking on open-ended maintenance obligations without assurances for other communities.
side_b_arguments: Other communities such as Cook Road also need pedestrian and safety improvements, and a policy without written assurances could leave them behind.
Approving a standalone resolution for Solterra on April 13 would avoid rushing a broader countywide policy before full multi-jurisdictional review.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken at the work session; staff was directed to get written scope confirmation from NCDOT and bring back both a draft resolution and a minimal draft policy for the April 13, 2015 regular session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 23, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all recorded motions by 5-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. Following a moment of silence for the late Dr. Joseph 'Joe' Han, approval of the March 9 minutes, a Creek Week proclamation, and a resolution honoring the life of civil rights and environmental attorney B.B. Olive, the Board held a public hearing on a downzoning request along North Roxboro Road north of Orange Factory Road. Commissioners unanimously adopted the G.S. 153A-341 consistency statement and approved the UDO rezoning from RS-20 to RR (5-0) to support a conservation subdivision and working farm concept presented by George Stansill and developer Rick Beagle. The Board also conducted ballot voting for boards and commissions, heard comments from Commissioner Wendy Jacobs on JARC transit funding and Project Build youth gang-prevention programming, and met in closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding wastewater property acquisitions along NC Highway 55, T.W. Alexander Drive, and South Alston Avenue before adjourning at 8:28 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Moment of Silence for Dr. Joseph Han, and March 9 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting with announcements regarding 'In Touch with Durham County' guests (CROP Walk coordinator Karen Johanson and Library Director Tammy Baggett), boards and commissions recruitment, and 'Living Healthy'. The Board observed a moment of silence in memory of former DPS Board of Education and Partnership for Children member Dr. Joseph Han, with Chair Page directing the clerk to prepare a future resolution. The March 9, 2015 regular session minutes were approved unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation for Creek Week (March 21–28, 2015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page proclaimed March 21–28, 2015 as Creek Week in Durham County to highlight the importance of local waterways and parks. Presenters noted kickoff events at Durham Central Park, a talk on 'Blue Mind' at the Main Library, and upcoming park improvements.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution Honoring Attorney B.B. Olive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a resolution honoring the late Attorney B.B. Olive (who died December 4, 2014), recognizing his World War II service, Duke engineering degree, founding of the Triangle's first private intellectual property firm, integration of the North Carolina Bar Association, defense of the Crest Street community against NC 147, and New Hope Creek and Eno River conservation work. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Commissioner Jacobs shared personal memories with widow Eve Olive and family members in attendance.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: North Roxboro Road Rezoning (RS-20 to RR)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reported that a rezoning request along North Roxboro Road north of Orange Factory Road (from RS-20 to Residential Rural, RR) was consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and UDO standards and had received a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Presenter George Stansill described the downzoning and accompanying site plan (with developer Rick Beagle) for a conservation subdivision incorporating a working farm. After closing the public hearing with no other speakers, the Board unanimously adopted the G.S. 153A-341 consistency statement and approved the rezoning ordinance by 5-0 voice votes.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments and Consent Agenda Comments (JARC Transit and Project Build)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners cast ballots for board and commission appointments while the County Attorney committed to researching an enabling act question. During vote tabulation, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted two consent agenda topics: welcoming additional Job Access and Reverse Commute (JARC) transit funding for city residents via Transportation Director Linda Thomas, and requesting a future briefing on Michelle Young's Project Build youth gang-prevention program (ages 14–21). The County Attorney reported the ballot appointment results.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Wastewater Property Acquisition (Item 15-314) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding acquisition of real property for wastewater treatment system improvements at 6001 NC Highway 55, 451 T.W. Alexander Road, and 6026 South Alston Avenue owned by 55 Alexander Associates, LLC. Returning at 01:43:43, the Board reported giving direction to staff and adjourned at 8:28 p.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 9, 2015 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Motion carried unanimously by voice vote; full five-member attendance confirmed later by Chair Page's 5-0 vote call at 00:55:34.
votes.discussion_detail: Acceptance of the March 9, 2015 regular session meeting minutes.

votes.notes: Chair Page announced: 'Motion carries unanimously, five to zero.'
votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of consistency statement finding the RS-20 to RR downzoning request consistent with the Durham Comprehensive Plan and adopted policies and ordinances.

votes.item_title: Ordinance Amending UDO to Rezone North Roxboro Road Property from RS-20 to RR
votes.notes: Motion carried unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approves downzoning from Residential Suburban-20 (RS-20) to Residential Rural (RR) for property north of Orange Factory Road at North Roxboro Road.

votes.item_title: Item 15-314: Adjourn to Closed Session Pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) (Wastewater Property Acquisition)
votes.notes: Carried by voice vote; board returned at 01:43:43 after giving direction to staff.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed session concerning acquisition of real property for wastewater treatment system improvements at 6001 NC Hwy 55, 451 T.W. Alexander Rd, and 6026 S. Alston Ave owned by 55 Alexander Associates, LLC.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-03-09 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 9, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. excused (four members present), the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all actions by 4-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. At the County Attorney's request, the Board pulled Consent Item 15-273 (Watts Endowment transfer to Duke University Management Company), approved the remaining consent agenda items, and then separately approved pulled Item 15-276 (modifying Lebanon Fire District boundaries after the state rejected a City of Durham MOU because the city is not a rated rural fire department) and Item 15-286 (authorizing the Planning Director to seek state approval for an administrative interpretation adjusting a Falls Lake Watershed Protection Overlay F/J-A boundary based on survey drainage). The Board also approved prior minutes—with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requesting staff follow-up on board interview notifications and jail inmate hospital cost comparisons—and presented ceremonial recognitions for the 41st annual CROP Hunger Walk, the 50th anniversary of Durham's 1965 triple Black high school basketball state championships (Merrick-Moore, Little River, and Hillside), and Durham County Employee United Way Campaign awards before adjourning at 8:17 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence, Agenda Adjustment (Item 15-273 Pulled), and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page noted that Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. had been excused at the prior work session. At the County Attorney's request, Consent Item 15-273 (terminating Watts Endowment agreements and transferring funds to Duke University Management Company to save $25,000 annually in fees) was pulled from the agenda. Commissioners shared announcements including 'In Touch with Durham County', a March 19 community event, and the 50th anniversary of the Selma march.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Including January 26, 2015 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before voting on the minutes, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested staff follow-up on two prior items: notifying board applicants of interview requirements and providing a comparison of jail inmate hospital medical care costs before and after new state legislation. The minutes were approved 4-0 on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: CROP Walk, 1965 Triple Basketball Championships, and Employee Campaign
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented a proclamation for the 41st annual CROP Hunger Walk to coordinator Karen Johanson, followed by a resolution introduced by Durham City Councilman Eddie Davis honoring the 50th anniversary of the March 1965 triple state basketball championships won by Durham's three Black high schools (Merrick-Moore, Little River, and Hillside). Commissioners also recognized county employees and Rico Horton with United Way and Beating Heart awards.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 15-273, 15-276, and 15-286)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow pulled Item 15-276 and commented on Item 15-289 (noting Seattle's Youth Violence Prevention Initiative was consulting with Durham's Project Build), while Chair Page thanked Duke Energy Progress for its Energy Neighbor Fund donation to Social Services under Item 15-203. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved the remaining consent agenda 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-276: Lebanon Fire District Boundary Changes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow for map clarification, staff explained that the state rejected Durham County's memorandum of understanding with the City of Durham because the city is not a rated rural fire department, requiring boundary adjustments for the Lebanon (and Bahama) fire districts. Following discussion of the maps, the Board approved Item 15-276 unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-286: Administrative Interpretation of Falls Lake Watershed Protection Overlay (F/J-A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented an administrative interpretation based on a property owner's survey showing stormwater runoff drains away from Panther Creek/Falls Lake rather than into the protected watershed. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked what precedent the decision would set for adjacent properties on the same side of the ridgeline, and staff recommended authorizing the Planning Director to seek state approval for the boundary change. On a motion by Commissioner Jacobs seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, the Board approved Item 15-286 unanimously 4-0 before adjourning at 8:17 p.m.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved with request from Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow for follow-up on board interview notifications and jail inmate hospital medical cost comparisons.

votes.notes: Fred Foster Jr. excused and absent (4-0). Seconder acknowledged on microphone ('I have a second back') without stating name.
votes.discussion_detail: Approves fire district boundary adjustments necessitated by state rejection of an MOU with the City of Durham.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-03-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 2, 2015 Work Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners held substantive policy discussions on the joint Pre-K Center and Integral senior housing lease, Parkwood fire/EMS transition staffing, and a proposed county sidewalk maintenance policy, taking two unanimous procedural voice votes to suspend the rules and excuse Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. from the March 9 regular session (with no split votes). During citizen comments, Forest View Elementary parent Charles Armstrong and another parent urged Safe Routes to School sidewalk action, while James Davis and PAC 1 co-facilitator Lavonia Silver requested a contractor job directory and online community job postings. On the Pre-K Center partnership, commissioners questioned 'full control' lease language for Durham Public Schools over the gymnasium and cafeteria so county and community after-hours access would be protected, while Wendy Jacobs backed 50/50 operating cost sharing, walk-zone planning, and sliding-scale tuition students. In a second work session review of county sidewalk maintenance (presented by Drew Cummings and Mark Ahrendsen), Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow argued for a limited policy accepting long-term maintenance for NCDOT-funded sidewalks at school sites outside city limits, while an unidentified commissioner warned of ongoing tax-dollar maintenance costs and cited long-standing citizen requests on Little River Road.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Contractor Job Directories, Online Postings, and Forest View Sidewalks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: James Davis urged County Manager and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick to create a subcontractor project directory for the downtown building modeled on the 2008 Holton Career Center effort, and PAC 1 co-facilitator Lavonia Silver asked the county to post contractor and community job openings on its website alongside follow-up on the disparity study. Two Forest View Elementary parents, including Charles Armstrong, urged the Board to address missing sidewalks and Safe Routes to School access for children living within a quarter mile of the school.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Center and Integral Senior Housing Partnership Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners reviewed the lease and operating structure for the Pre-K Center co-located with Integral's senior housing project (featuring a 40-year loan term, $1/year base rent, and pass-through utilities/maintenance structured as rent for commercial tax deductions). Commissioners sought revisions clarifying county versus Durham Public Schools after-hours community access to the gymnasium and cafeteria so 'full control' language intended to exclude Integral would not block county use, while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs supported 50/50 DPS-county operating cost sharing, a walk zone to trim bus costs, and exploring tuition-paying slots.

agenda_items.title: Parkwood Fire and EMS Transition Staffing Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, staff (Jeff) briefly confirmed that a division chief position remained unhired amid the Parkwood Fire Department transition and that the county's pro rata administrative share remained incorporated in the staffing plan.

agenda_items.title: County Sidewalk Maintenance Policy and Forest View / School Case Studies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Drew Cummings and Mark Ahrendsen returned for a second work session briefing, detailing a 50-year average concrete sidewalk lifespan, ~$40 per linear foot replacement cost, and school site case studies (Irwin and Randolph / Forest View, Hollow Rock access, Oak Grove / Olive Branch Road, and Mangum Elementary). Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow argued for a limited policy accepting maintenance when the state funds school-site sidewalk linkages outside city limits, whereas another commissioner questioned assuming new taxpayer maintenance costs and raised unmet sidewalk requests from residents such as Delma White on Little River Road.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Excusal of Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. for March 9 Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before adjourning for lunch, the Board voted unanimously by voice vote on motions by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton to suspend the rules and excuse Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. from the March 9, 2015 regular session meeting.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Excuse Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. from March 9, 2015 Regular Session
votes.notes: Carried unanimously by voice vote; exact member count at the moment of the work session vote was not read on mic.
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural suspension of board rules to consider excusing Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. from the Monday evening March 9, 2015 meeting.

votes.item_title: Excuse Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. from March 9, 2015 Regular Session
votes.notes: Carried by voice vote with no opposition voiced.
votes.discussion_detail: Excuses Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. from attending the March 9, 2015 regular session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-03-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
disagreements.issue: Whether Durham County Should Accept Long-Term Sidewalk Maintenance Costs for NCDOT-Funded School Sidewalks
disagreements.summary: During the second work session review of sidewalk maintenance policy, commissioners disagreed over whether the county should adopt a limited policy to accept long-term maintenance for state-funded sidewalks near schools outside city limits or avoid taking on new taxpayer-funded maintenance obligations amid competing neighborhood needs.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt a limited policy accepting county maintenance when NCDOT pays to build sidewalks linking school sites to adjacent neighborhoods, aligning with strategic plan health and safety goals.
side_a_arguments: By building sidewalks around schools, Durham County is already in the sidewalk business, and leaving 100 homes across from Forest View Elementary without a safe crossing undermines strategic plan health and safety goals.
Limiting the policy to NCDOT-funded construction at school sites outside city limits caps county exposure while unlocking state construction funds.
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against taking on unbudgeted taxpayer maintenance obligations and highlight unresolved sidewalk needs raised for years in other neighborhoods.
side_b_arguments: Long-term sidewalk maintenance imposes new costs on county taxpayers without dedicated budget funding, mirroring budget pressures faced by the City of Durham.
Residents such as Delma White have petitioned for years for sidewalks along corridors like Little River Road without action, so all communities must be considered fairly.
disagreements.resolution: No vote was taken at the March 2 work session; the policy returned for further work session deliberation on April 6 and formal action on April 13, 2015.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-02-09 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 9, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all agenda, minutes, consent, and financing motions by 5-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. The Board approved the January 5 work session and January 12 regular session minutes, adopted the consent agenda (after which Commissioner Wendy Jacobs praised Item 15-228, a Cooperative Extension and Durham Public Schools contract for the Parent and Family Advocacy and Support Training [PFAS] program), and held a public hearing before approving a resolution supporting the Public Finance Authority's issuance of approximately $13 million in bonds on behalf of the Contemporary Science Center—carrying zero debt or obligation for Durham County taxpayers. Ceremonial recognitions honored Union Baptist Church Boy Scout Troop 411, Hillside High School Assistant Principal Jason Jowers (North Carolina's 2015 Assistant Principal of the Year), and the county project team behind the Durham County Justice Center's 2014 AIA Justice Facilities Review Award (completed early and under budget). Chair Page also announced an upcoming Durham roundtable for the My Brother's Keeper initiative with U.S. Secretary of Labor Thomas Perez before adjourning at 8:11 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Welcome to Boy Scout Troop 411, and Census-Tract Outreach Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and recognized Union Baptist Church Boy Scout Troop 411 attending for their Citizenship in the Community merit badge, alongside announcements of a February 20 event at First Presbyterian Church featuring the NCCU Chancellor. Presenter Ms. Rona briefed commissioners on neighborhood canvassing, postcards, and door hangers for a census-tract-based community outreach program, drawing positive feedback from Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Hillside High School Assistant Principal Jason Jowers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Jason Jowers, Assistant Principal at Hillside High School, on being named North Carolina's 2015 Assistant Principal of the Year. Jowers highlighted Hillside's graduation rate ranking second among large comprehensive high schools in the district and $9.7 million in senior scholarships earned the prior year. Chair Page also noted that Item 15-257 was deferred to the next board meeting.

agenda_items.title: Item 15-258: Recognition of Justice Center 2014 AIA Justice Facilities Review Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored the cross-departmental team that delivered the new Durham County Justice Center, which received the 2014 American Institute of Architects (AIA) Justice Facilities Review Award. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs, and Fred Foster Jr. praised staff for delivering the courthouse on time or early and substantially under budget.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 5 Work Session and January 12 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved the minutes of the January 5, 2015 work session and January 12, 2015 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Item 15-228 Cooperative Extension / DPS PFAS Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled, the Board unanimously approved the consent agenda on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow. Following the vote, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted Item 15-228, a contract between Cooperative Extension and Durham Public Schools for the Parent and Family Advocacy and Support Training (PFAS) program.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Resolution Approving Public Finance Authority Bonds for Contemporary Science Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Drew Cummings presented a resolution required under federal/interstate conduit rules approving the Public Finance Authority's issuance of approximately $13 million in bonds on behalf of the Contemporary Science Center (with Pamela Blizzard present), emphasizing that the bonds create zero debt or financial obligation for Durham County or its taxpayers. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow asked about the size of the new facility, and after opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved the resolution on a motion by Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: My Brother's Keeper Roundtable with U.S. Secretary of Labor Thomas Perez and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced that U.S. Secretary of Labor Thomas Perez would visit Durham that Wednesday from 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. for a My Brother's Keeper (MBK) roundtable with approximately 15 community leaders and youth, and noted that the weather-postponed White House MBK meeting was rescheduled for Thursday (with Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. confirming the updated Wednesday time). The meeting adjourned at 8:11 p.m.

votes.notes: Motion carried unanimously by voice vote; all five commissioners confirmed present in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of minutes from the January 12, 2015 regular session and January 5, 2015 work session.

votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote following public hearing with no speakers.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-01-26 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 26, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all recorded actions by 5-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. After hearing updates on the My Brother's Keeper youth summit and Main Library renovation visioning, the Board celebrated the 125th anniversary of St. Mark A.M.E. Zion Church, national recognition for Southern High School's Bionomic Education and Training Center (BETC), and the Utility Division's second consecutive Collection System of the Year Award. Following a truncated middle section, the Board reviewed the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) and audit compliance summary—debating conservative sales tax projections versus City of Durham forecasts, fund balance growth under 92% expenditure execution maintaining the county's AAA rating, and declining per capita income trends ahead of the budget retreat—and conducted ballot voting for boards and commissions (appointing Patrick Hannah and John Tommy Hunt to the RDU Airport Authority and Fred Mayot to the Transportation Advisory Board). The Board then entered closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privilege and returned to open session to unanimously authorize a $425,000 settlement payment to Durham County from the entity transcribed as 'free line group' before adjourning at 9:40 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and My Brother's Keeper Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened with county television and board recruitment announcements, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs publicized the January 29 public visioning session for the Main Library renovation, and Chair Page delivered an update on Durham's My Brother's Keeper (MBK) initiative, noting four committees, eight co-chairs, and strong youth participation at the weekend summit.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution: 125th Anniversary of St. Mark A.M.E. Zion Church
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution congratulating St. Mark A.M.E. Zion Church on 125 years of ministry and community anchoring in Durham, joined by Pastor Rev. Dr. G. Ray Coleman and church members including Perry Brown. Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. praised the church's historic corner presence and recalled hearing Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. speak inside the sanctuary.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions: Southern High BETC Program (Item 15-219) and Utility Division Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized national honors for Durham's Bionomic Education and Training Center (BETC) stormwater workforce-training program at Southern High School (noting Mr. Leathers and sustainability manager Brian Calloway). At 01:00:54, Utility Division Manager Joe Pierce and Engineering & Environmental Services staff were recognized for winning North Carolina's Collection System of the Year Award for a second consecutive year.

agenda_items.title: CAFR Financial Condition, Audit Findings, and Budget Retreat Fiscal Trends
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated portion of the transcript, commissioners and staff discussed federal/state grant compliance findings in the single-audit schedule, the county's conservative sales tax budgeting compared with City of Durham projections (in light of the prior June's 3-cent property tax increase), and how spending below 92% of budget plus 14-month collections grew fund balance and protected Durham County's AAA credit rating. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and others also flagged declining per capita income trends, delinquent tax collections, and 10-year revenue and rental trends from the Human Services building for deeper review at the budget retreat.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of NCCU Law Interns and Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney introduced two North Carolina Central University School of Law interns, including returning intern Alicia Houston, before the Board completed ballot appointments. After resolving a ballot tie for the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority and clarifying Workforce Development Board slot counts, the clerk announced the appointments of Patrick Hannah and John Tommy Hunt to the RDU Airport Authority and Fred Mayot to the Transportation Advisory Board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Authorization of $425,000 Settlement Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege. Returning to open session at 02:36:25, the Board unanimously approved a motion by Commissioner Jacobs seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow authorizing a claim settlement with the entity transcribed as 'free line group' providing a $425,000 payment to Durham County and authorizing the County Manager to execute the agreement before adjourning at 9:40 p.m.

votes.notes: Carried by voice vote with no opposition; all five commissioners confirmed present during the meeting.

meetings.executive_summary: At the January 12, 2015 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all minutes, consent, and state and federal legislative agenda items by voice vote, with no split or contested votes. Following announcements covering Triangle Transit Authority's FY 2014 Durham County Bus and Rail Investment Progress Report, Affordable Care Act outreach, and the upcoming My Brother's Keeper youth summit, the Board proclaimed National Mentoring Month with local youth-mentoring leaders and tutors. agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation for National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. agenda_items.title: Approval of November 24, December 1, and December 8, 2014 Minutes

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2015-01-05 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 5, 2015 Work Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners held informational briefings and priority-setting discussions with no formal substantive votes or split disagreements recorded (concluding with a voice vote to adjourn). During citizen comments, PAC 1 co-facilitator Lavonia Silver highlighted sharing revaluation imaging project job listings in Community News, while Victoria Peterson urged adding a wing to the Youth Home to house juveniles out of the county jail and address racial disparities, prompting commissioners to discuss staff attendance at PACs and scheduling budget outreach meetings across the community. Staff and partner agencies—including DSS, Meals on Wheels, Durham Center for Senior Life, Senior PharmAssist, Durham Partnership for Seniors, and Durham County ACCESS—presented on aging-in-place needs, warning of a 7% ($85,000) drop in Home and Community Care Block Grant funding, a 49% jump in Adult Protective Services reports, meal waiting lists, and 200–300% diabetes drug price increases creating Senior PharmAssist's first-ever 72-senior waitlist. Following a truncated middle section, Deborah Craig-Ray reviewed draft 2015 state Crime Cabinet items, four NCACC federal legislative priorities (minimum wage, transportation infrastructure, immigration reform, and Medicaid/HUD/veterans/homeless housing), and potential NACo steering committee resolutions ahead of the January 12 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Revaluation Job Outreach, Youth Home Detention, and PAC Budget Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: PAC 1 co-facilitator Lavonia Silver spoke on disseminating job information for the county's revaluation imaging project through Community News at Holton Career & Resource Center. Commissioners followed up by asking about county staff attendance at PAC meetings and directing the manager and clerk to schedule community budget meetings where all five commissioners can participate.

agenda_items.title: Aging in Place Presentation: Senior Services, Waitlists, and Strategic Plan Refresh
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters from DSS, Meals on Wheels, Durham Center for Senior Life, Senior PharmAssist, Durham Partnership for Seniors (including Kathy Stockup), and Durham County ACCESS detailed growing eldercare pressures ahead of the 'silver tsunami' and stressed door-to-door over curb-to-curb transit. Commissioners discussed addressing senior needs during the strategic plan refresh, adding a senior information hub on the county website, and weighing online community giving options.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, Deborah Craig-Ray reviewed state legislative proposals from the Crime Cabinet and Commissioner Ellen W. Commissioners also reviewed four NCACC congressional items (minimum wage, transportation/transit and road/bridge infrastructure, immigration reform, and Medicaid/HUD/veterans and homeless housing funding) and discussed a potential NACo Health & Human Services resolution on federal affordable and homeless housing cuts with Commissioner Fred Foster Jr., requesting copies to review before January 12 prior to adjourning.

Reckhow read a resolution celebrating the 15th anniversary of Kids Voting Durham alongside Cooperative Extension staff, board chair Mike Shiflet, and youth participants. agenda_items.title: Eno River Association Annual Calendar Presentation (Item 7)

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 1, 2014 Worksession presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously suspended its rules and approved a time-sensitive Department of Social Services (DSS) request for 33 full-time equivalent (FTE) positions—converting 15 temporary/provisional caseworkers and adding 18 staff—backed by 75% federal pass-through reimbursement, with no split or contested votes. Earlier in the session, the Board heard public comment supporting public art at the courthouse and climate mitigation measures, and received a UNC School of Government Development Finance Initiative (DFI) briefing on 2013 state legislation authorizing public-private partnership (P3), design-build, and design-build bridging contracting methods. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, commissioners reviewed a proposal to purchase the 18-foot stainless steel sculpture 'Twist of Fate' outside the County Courthouse using remaining courthouse capital project funds ($300,000 remaining). While expressing interest in explanatory signage and a broader countywide public art placement plan across communities, commissioners declined to suspend the rules for immediate approval and placed the required budget amendment on the next Monday's consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Courthouse Public Art and Climate Action
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A retired Downtown Durham Inc. leader spoke in favor of Item 8, urging the Board to invest in the public art piece at the County Courthouse as a hallmark of great cities. A subsequent speaker advocated local climate action including county electric vehicle fleets, telecommuting, energy-efficient smart buildings, and transitioning away from fossil fuels.

agenda_items.title: Briefing on Public-Private Partnership (P3) and Alternative Contracting Legislation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters from the Development Finance Initiative (DFI) at the UNC School of Government reviewed 2013 North Carolina legislation authorizing design-build, design-build bridging, and public-private partnership (P3) contracting for local governments. They detailed statutory steps for P3 development agreements—including adopting a written critical-need finding, defining programming goals, and holding a public hearing after 30 days' published notice of the negotiated agreement—and cited examples in Wilmington and Asheville.

agenda_items.title: Department of Social Services (DSS) Request for 33 Income Maintenance FTEs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the session, DSS staff explained that online benefit applications have increased caseload volume and that 75% federal pass-through reimbursement was now available from the state to fund 33 FTEs (one supervisor and conversion of 15 temporary/provisional caseworkers plus 18 new positions, along with computer equipment) effective January 1. Because a state response was due by Thursday, the Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules and unanimously approved the 33 additional positions.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Purchasing Courthouse Public Art Sculpture ('Twist of Fate') (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the option to purchase 'Twist of Fate,' an 18-foot stainless steel kinetic sculpture temporarily installed at the County Courthouse through April 2015 as part of the Bull City Sculpture Show, noting county staff polling favored purchase and $300,000 remained in the courthouse capital project budget (compared to the $87,000 South Regional Library sculpture). Commissioners asked about adding an explanatory pedestal plaque and developing a strategic public art plan across county communities, and agreed to bring the necessary budget amendment to the next Monday's consent agenda rather than suspending the rules.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend Rules for Time-Sensitive DSS Staffing Request
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously'). Seconder was not clearly identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Board rules to allow immediate action on the DSS staffing request ahead of a Thursday response deadline.

votes.item_title: Approve Department of Social Services Request for 33 Additional FTE Positions
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously'). Seconder was not clearly identified in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 33 FTEs for DSS income maintenance (converting 15 previously temporary/provisional caseworkers and adding 18 new positions) supported by 75% federal pass-through reimbursement, effective January 1 for the remainder of FY 2015.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 24, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved prior meeting minutes and the eight-item consent agenda (Items A through H) by voice votes and appointed residents to multiple county boards and commissions by written ballot, with no split or contested votes. During the session, the Board recognized Commissioner Wendy Jacobs for earning the NCACC Local Elected Leaders Academy Practitioner designation and honored Paramedic Brandon Pittman and fellow first responders for rescuing and resuscitating a 12-year-old boy submerged in water for approximately 15 minutes. After approving the consent agenda, Chair Page and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow directed staff to follow up on Item C regarding news of workforce reductions at an incentivized company to verify whether Durham employment commitments remained intact. Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley and Marqueta Wilson also presented the countywide security strategy initiated in April 2013—covering centralized camera coordination, emergency plans, mass employee notification, and hiring a General Services security manager.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Commissioner Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and announced Affordable Care Act open enrollment events on December 6 and December 13, county board vacancies, Wednesday chair office hours, and the December 1–31 pre-application window for FY 2015–16 nonprofit funding. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted Durham Public Schools Career and Technical Education programs including robotics, welding, early childhood, business finance, and Project Lead the Way engineering across several schools.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (October 27 and November 10, 2014 Regular Sessions) (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the Board unanimously approved the minutes from the October 27 and November 10, 2014 Regular Sessions. Chair Page also displayed Downtown Durham Inc.'s 2013–2014 Outstanding Downtown Development Project plaque awarded for the Durham County Human Services Complex.

agenda_items.title: NCACC Recognition for Commissioner Jacobs and Heroism Recognition for Paramedic Brandon Pittman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Commissioner Wendy Jacobs for achieving the Practitioner level in the NCACC Local Elected Leaders Academy, joining Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. (Practitioner) and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton (Mentor). The Board then honored seven-year Durham Paramedic Brandon Pittman and responding crews for jumping into the water to rescue and successfully resuscitate a 12-year-old boy who had been submerged for roughly 15 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through H) and Economic Development Incentive Follow-Up (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled by citizens or commissioners, the Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A through H on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton. Immediately following the vote, Chair Page and Commissioner Reckhow instructed staff to loop back with the company referenced in Item C after news reports of workforce cuts to confirm whether its Durham facility would still satisfy job targets tied to its county economic development incentive.

agenda_items.title: Board Update on Countywide Security Strategy (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis, Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley, and Marqueta Wilson presented recommendations stemming from vulnerability assessments launched in April 2013. Key needs included standardizing building emergency plans, centralizing disparate camera systems, completing an employee mass notification system, creating an organizational security management team with Sheriff's Office participation, and immediately advertising the budgeted General Services security manager position.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment and Board and Commission Appointments (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief truncated segment featuring public remarks regarding human rights concerns and endorsement of staff recommendations, commissioners cast paper ballots for multiple advisory boards and commissions. The Clerk tabulated and read the results appointing Mildred Mays and Deidre Thornlow (prior board), Cynthia Fisher Richardson (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission), Daniel Colbarr (Boxing and Wrestling Commission), Michael Miller (City-County Appearance Commission), Angela Holmes (Homeless Services Advisory Committee), Deidre Thornlow (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee), Art Ferguson (Public Health Board), Dorin Johnson (Transportation Advisory Board), and Amy Aspaw, Doreen L. Johnson, Gina Dillon, and Davida Major (Women's Commission).

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of the October 27, 2014 and November 10, 2014 regular sessions without amendment.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 10, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items B through I, pulled and subsequently approved Consent Items A and J, and authorized Cooperative Extension to submit a federal Promise Zone designation application, with no split or contested votes. During consent review, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted $300,000 remained in the courthouse capital budget for potential public art, while Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. urged returning surplus project funds from tax-supported capital projects back to taxpayers rather than reallocating them. Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers presented the proposed 'Durham–Fayetteville Assault on Poverty' Promise Zone application seeking $5 million or more in federal resources with a shared $300,000 local match between Durham and Cumberland counties, which the Board approved unanimously while requesting collaboration with the City of Durham. The Board also approved pulled Consent Item A—a $266,413.33 Tyler Technologies contract amendment for 2016 property revaluation work—and pulled Consent Item J authorizing an electronic surplus vehicle auction after Commissioner Wendy Jacobs urged updating fleet replacement standards for fuel efficiency and green emissions.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Citizen Comments, and My Brother's Keeper Launch
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced the November 14 deadline for Durham Open Space and Trails Commission matching grants, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs promoted the November 15–February 15 Affordable Care Act enrollment window with ten local outreach events. A citizen speaker raised concerns about 15-to-18-year-old youths being held in the Durham County Jail, and Chair Page announced the county's 'My Brother's Keeper' community stakeholders meeting for young men of color at the Human Services Building.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National Adoption Awareness Month (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation declaring November 2014 as Adoption Awareness Month in Durham County, joined by Department of Social Services staff Janice Williams and Jovetta Whitfield. The proclamation highlighted the ten children in Durham County foster care awaiting adoptive families and thanked DSS staff for their work.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items B through I approved; Items A and J pulled) (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled Items A and J for separate questions and discussed Item D's transfer of unspent courthouse capital funds ($2.45 million to $2.7 million), with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow confirming $300,000 remained if the Board later pursued public art and Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. arguing surplus tax-backed project funds should be returned to citizens rather than redirected. The Board then unanimously approved Consent Items B through I on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Cooperative Extension Federal Promise Zone Designation Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript covering Item 7, Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers sought approval to apply for round two of the federal Promise Zone competition under a joint 'Durham–Fayetteville Assault on Poverty' proposal with Cumberland County, targeting census tracts above 33% poverty with a $300,000 shared local match to leverage at least $5 million plus VISTA staff. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr.—who urged the County Manager to seek City of Durham collaboration and a letter of support—the Board unanimously authorized the application, MOA authority, and contingent match allocation.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item A: Tyler Technologies 2016 Revaluation Contract Amendment ($266,413.33)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After discussing Item A's $266,413.33 contract amendment with Tyler Technologies for field-based addressing, street-level residential photography, CAMA sketch validation, and workflow software ahead of the 2016 property revaluation, the Board approved the item unanimously. The motion was made by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton and seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item J: Surplus Vehicle Electronic Public Auction Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned staff about Section 5.0 vehicle age and mileage replacement criteria and urged updating county fleet policy to prioritize green emissions and fuel efficiency. The Board then unanimously approved the resolution authorizing electronic public auction disposal of surplus vehicles on a motion by Commissioner Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 27, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved prior meeting minutes, a new Durham Convention Center interlocal agreement, a small capital upgrades request for the Convention Center, and a closed session on personnel matters, while making board and commission appointments by ballot, with no split or contested votes. Early in the meeting, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow relayed citizen concerns over parking and long early-voting lines, the Board honored the late Dr. John Thomas Daniel Jr. for his medical and Board of Public Health service, and County Manager Wendell Davis introduced new Budget and Management Services Director Claudia Odom Hager. agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Early Voting Concerns

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 22, October 6, and October 13, 2014) (Item 4)

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Dr. John Thomas Daniel Jr. and Welcome of Budget Director Claudia Odom Hager

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention Center Joint Venture Interlocal Agreement

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 13, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A through G, pulled and subsequently approved Consent Item H, rezoned a 9.7-acre parcel on Rhododendron Drive (Case Z140010), and renamed unbuilt Darcy Court to Elmfoot Street (Case 140001), with no split or contested votes. The Board also issued proclamations recognizing October 2014 as Dysautonomia Awareness Month and November 1, 2014 as Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Culture of Health and Take a Loved One to the Doctor Day, and held a public hearing on the 100% state-funded FY 2014–15 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) transit grant. On Rezoning Case Z140010 (159 Rhododendron Drive), the Board unanimously adopted both a Comprehensive Plan consistency statement and a UDO amendment changing the parcel from Science Research Park (SRP) to Residential Suburban 20 (RS-20) to allow up to nine single-family homes. Before approving pulled Consent Item H—a $57,876 contract amendment for DSS child care document imaging—Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned the cumulative $2.085 million scanning contract and exit strategy, receiving staff assurance that child care represents the final phase of the multi-year records imaging project.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Proclamations (Items 4 & 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page opened the meeting with announcements regarding the November 1 Culture of Health event, DOST matching grants, Living Healthy broadcasts, and an American Tobacco Trail film. The Board proclaimed October 2014 as Dysautonomia Awareness Month with Connie Prue and her son Noah sharing his experience with POTS, and proclaimed November 1, 2014 as RWJF Culture of Health and Take a Loved One to the Doctor Day with Public Health Director Gayle Harris.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through G approved; Item H pulled) (Item 6/7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested to pull Item H for separate discussion, while another commissioner commended Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers under Item F for partnering with the Detention Center to provide a teacher. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A through G.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2014–15 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) Grant (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County ACCESS Program Manager Linda Thomas-Wallace and Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers presented the state-required public hearing on the annual formula-based ROAP grant. They noted the program is 100% state-funded with no county match required and supports demand-response transportation for residents age 60+ and disabled citizens as well as employment transportation (further discussion/disposition fell within the subsequent truncated segment).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z140010 (159 Rhododendron Drive, SRP to RS-20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Patrick Young presented Case Z140010 to rezone ~9.7 acres at 159 Rhododendron Drive near Treyburn from Science Research Park (SRP) to Residential Suburban 20 (RS-20) for up to nine single-family homes, noting consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. After Commissioner Reckhow asked about adjacent SRP-zoned edge parcels and the public hearing closed with no speakers, the Board unanimously adopted the required GS 153A-341 consistency statement and the rezoning ordinance in two separate votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Renaming 140001 (Darcy Court to Elmfoot Street) (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Patrick Young presented Street Renaming Request 140001 to rename unbuilt platted Darcy Court (off Mineral Springs Road adjacent to Delmar Drive and Ashton Hall Phase 2) to Elmfoot Street for consistent public safety addressing, reporting no opposition from the August 14 community meeting. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved the renaming resolution on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item H: DSS Child Care Records Document Imaging Contract Amendment ($57,876)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned the $57,876 amendment raising the overall DSS scanning contract from $2,027,422 to roughly $2,085,000 and asked whether internal staff could handle active records going forward. DSS staff explained that child care represents the tail end of a multi-year imaging project that has cleared overcrowded office space, after which the Board unanimously approved Item H on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 6, 2014 Worksession presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously voted to enter closed session regarding Shane v. County of Durham et al. (12 CVS 1634) and, upon returning to open session, unanimously suspended its rules and approved a third modification of an air lease and authorized Chair Page to sign a settlement agreement in the Shane lawsuit, with no split or contested votes. Earlier in the worksession, citizens Victoria Peterson and James Chavis urged expanded educational programming for 16-to-18-year-old detainees at the Durham County Jail, and District Attorney Roger Echols, Criminal Justice Resource Center staff, Sheriff's officials, and Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley briefed the Board on pretrial release outcomes (75% completion rate), Superior Court felony disposition rates (2,998 dispositions vs. 2,598 filings), and plans for crime lab contracting and a future jail annex lab. Following a truncated middle section, commissioners reviewed the proposed $36,000 courthouse sculpture purchase—noting it remained on display for free until April 2015 while at least one commissioner questioned the $36,000 cost—and discussed creating a Durham County Community Giving Fund via the Triangle Community Foundation or CitizenVestor crowdfunding app. Before entering closed session, the County Manager also reported the South Regional Library sculpture cost just over $87,000 and nearly $2 million remained in the courthouse project budget.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Detention Center Youth Education (Item 1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Victoria Peterson and James Chavis addressed the Board regarding minors aged 16–18 housed in the Durham County Jail lacking adequate schooling beyond limited IEP hours and called for oversight of funds. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs clarified that county and school officials were actively working on solutions.

agenda_items.title: Courts, Detention Center, and Pretrial Services Briefing (Item 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District Attorney Roger Echols, Criminal Justice Resource Center staff, Sheriff's Office representatives, and Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley presented data on pretrial release compliance (75% court appearance/completion), Superior Court felony case management (2,598 felony filings in 2013–14, median pending age 158 days ranking 7th of 44 districts, and 2,998 cases disposed), and educational planning for 16–18-year-old detainees. Staff also confirmed plans to explore interim external lab contracting and incorporate a local lab into the future jail annex design.

agenda_items.title: Courthouse Public Art Sculpture Discussion ($36,000 Proposal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, commissioners discussed the proposed $36,000 purchase of the temporary courthouse sculpture, noting it would remain on site at no cost until the end of April 2015 and was liked by courthouse staff. At least one commissioner expressed support for public art generally while criticizing the $36,000 price tag given community economic needs and asking staff to return with additional options.

agenda_items.title: Creation of a Durham County Community Giving Fund and Job Placement Update (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented two charitable giving concepts to fund community-supported public projects such as trail improvements or public art: an investment fund through Triangle Community Foundation (1% administrative fee, modeled on Orange County) and the CitizenVestor civic crowdfunding app. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs supported exploring both options, and staff subsequently provided an update on placing participants into identified county jobs within 30 days.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Settlement / Air Lease Modification in Shane v. County of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the County Manager reported that the South Regional Library sculpture cost just over $87,000 and nearly $2 million remained in the courthouse project budget, the Board unanimously voted to enter closed session under GS 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Shane v. County of Durham et al. (12 CVS 1634). Returning to open session at 03:31:05, the Board unanimously suspended its rules and approved the third modification of the air lease and authorized Chair Page to sign the Shane lawsuit settlement agreement.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session pursuant to GS 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege regarding Shane v. County of Durham et al. (12 CVS 1634).

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Board rules to act immediately on closed-session items and closed-session minutes.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the third modification of the air lease and authorized Chair Michael D. Page to execute the settlement agreement in the Shane lawsuit.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 22, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow excused out of town at a conference, the three present members (Chair Page, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs) unanimously approved prior minutes, Consent Agenda Items A–F and H–I, and pulled Consent Item G by 3-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. Consent Item G—approving continued funding for Planned Parenthood Health Systems following its January 1, 2015 merger with Planned Parenthood of Central North Carolina—was pulled by citizen speaker Victoria Peterson, who objected to tax dollars going to an organization providing abortions, before passing 3-0 on a motion by Vice Chair Howerton seconded by Commissioner Jacobs. The Board also issued proclamations honoring Durham native and Hillside High School alumna Dr. Elmira Mangum upon her inauguration as the 11th (and first female) President of Florida A&M University, recognizing Durham Reads Together around Congressman John Lewis's 'March: Book One,' and declaring October 6–10 as Minority Enterprise Development Week. Additionally, Tobin Freid presented proposed county comments warning that draft North Carolina hydraulic fracturing rules inadequately protect public health, the environment, and local government authority, and the Board conducted ballot appointments to advisory committees.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Member Excusals, and Approval of Minutes (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page announced that Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow were excused while attending an out-of-town conference, leaving a three-member quorum. Following announcements and a reminder from Vice Chair Howerton about 'Durham Women, Your Voices Matter,' the Board approved the September 2 and September 8, 2014 minutes unanimously (3-0) on a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Dr. Elmira Mangum Day, Durham Reads Together, and MED Week (Items 5–7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page proclaimed October 3, 2014 as Dr. Elmira Mangum Day honoring the Durham native and Hillside High graduate on becoming the first female president of Florida A&M University, with her sister accepting the proclamation. The Board also presented a resolution honoring Congressman John Lewis for Durham Reads Together (featuring 'March: Book One' and an October 4 unity march) to Library Director Tammy Baggett, and proclaimed October 6–10 as Minority Enterprise Development (MED) Week with remarks from citizen Victoria Peterson and county MWBE staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–F and H–I approved; Item G pulled) (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson requested to pull Item G for public comment. With no other items pulled, the Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A through F and H through I (3-0) on a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Comments on Proposed North Carolina Hydraulic Fracturing Rules (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presenter Tobin Freid outlined proposed comments on North Carolina's draft hydraulic fracturing regulations, warning that the rules did not adequately protect human health or the environment and failed to allow local government participation in siting, regulation, and emergency management. Commissioners asked whether the proposed rules addressed health and safety impacts on fracking workers.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners completed paper ballots for advisory board vacancies while addressing Item 10. Following the Item G vote, the Clerk announced the tabulated results beginning with the selection of Jenna Mints and Jessica M. Walker for the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (remainder truncated before adjournment).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item G: Planned Parenthood Funding Following Merger
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Addressing pulled Consent Item G—funding of Planned Parenthood Health Systems after its January 1, 2015 merger with Planned Parenthood of Central North Carolina—citizen Victoria Peterson objected to taxpayer funding for an organization that offers abortions. Following her remarks, the Board voted 3-0 on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs to approve Item G.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 8, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton after the Board voted to excuse Chair Michael D. Page, the four present commissioners (Vice Chair Howerton, Fred Foster Jr., Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs) unanimously approved prior minutes, Consent Agenda Items A through G, and up to $10.5 million in tax-exempt conduit revenue bonds for Voyager Foundation, Inc. by 4-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. Prior to formal votes, the Board honored the legacy of pioneering Durham librarian Mrs. Selena Warren Wheeler (read by Commissioner Jacobs), memorialized longtime Juvenile Crime Prevention Council member Karen King Thompson, and issued proclamations for September 2014 National Recovery Month (read by Commissioner Reckhow) and the 2014 Bull City Stand Down for homeless veterans (read by Commissioner Foster). Under Item 10, following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board approved the Voyager Foundation Series 2014 charter school revenue bonds—issued through Wisconsin's Public Finance Authority solely to refinance existing middle school debt over roughly 30 years with no financial liability to Durham County. The Board concluded by meeting in closed session under GS 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Roy Tisdale v. J.R. Berman and giving direction to staff upon returning to open session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Chair Excusal, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Chair Michael D. Page absent, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided and the Board voted to excuse Chair Page. Announcements highlighted DOST matching grants, DSS's 4th Annual Grandparents and Caregivers Conference, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's appointment as chair of the NCACC Environment Steering Committee and Board of Directors member, after which the Board approved the August 11 and August 25, 2014 minutes 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolutions and Proclamations: Selena Warren Wheeler, Karen King Thompson, Recovery Month, and Bull City Stand Down
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a memorial resolution honoring Mrs. Selena Warren Wheeler, Durham County's first African American professional librarian, accepted by Library Director Tammy Baggett and Stanford L. Warren branch manager Myrtle Darden alongside an announcement of the October 4 Durham Reads Together march with Congressman John Lewis. The Board also presented a memorial resolution for JCPC leader Karen King Thompson to her family, proclaimed September 2014 as National Recovery Month (read by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow), and proclaimed the 2014 Bull City Stand Down for homeless veterans (read by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr.).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled, a commissioner briefly commented on Item A—urging future local food sourcing in collaboration with the Soil and Water and Farmland boards—and Item E. The Board then approved Consent Agenda Items A through G unanimously by a 4-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Private Activity Revenue Bonds for Voyager Foundation, Inc. (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney presented a TEFRA public hearing under IRS Code Section 147(f) for up to $10,500,000 in Series 2014 charter school revenue bonds issued by the Wisconsin-based Public Finance Authority for Voyager Foundation, Inc., emphasizing that the County carries zero debt liability. Voyager counsel Brandon Lofton confirmed the ~30-year bonds would refinance existing middle school debt rather than construct new buildings, and after the public hearing closed with no speakers, the Board approved the bond resolution 4-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to GS 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Roy Tisdale v. J.R. Berman, Durham County Deputy Sheriff in his official and individual capacity. Returning to open session at 01:42:37, the Board noted direction was given to staff and adjourned.
