meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 2, 2014 Worksession presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously suspended its rules and voted to remove Chris Conimiro from the Durham City-County Appearance Commission due to poor attendance, with no split or contested votes. Public Affairs Director Deborah Craig-Ray led a review of potential 2015 NCACC statewide legislative goals—including Sheriff's Office proposals on stolen firearms penalties and shortening holding times for unclaimed livestock, as well as potential state childcare subsidy impacts—which the Board agreed to place on the consent agenda. Soil and Water Conservation Director Eddie Culberson also presented on the Bionomic Educational Training Center (BETC) at Southern High School, highlighting youth agricultural workforce training, 13 installed rain gardens, and $9,537 in program revenue. Following a truncated middle segment, commissioners scrutinized utility, HVAC, and security costs under the county's after-hours and weekend facility-use policy (agreeing to advance the policy to the next Monday's consent agenda) and viewed a demonstration of a new digital portal for logging and tracking commissioner and constituent requests.

agenda_items.title: Removal of Durham City-County Appearance Commission Member for Poor Attendance (Item 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no citizens signed up for comment, Chair Page introduced Item 2 to remove Chris Conimiro from the Durham City-County Appearance Commission due to poor attendance. The Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules (moved by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton) and then voted unanimously to remove him (moved by Vice Chair Howerton, seconded by Commissioner Reckhow).

agenda_items.title: Discussion of 2015 NCACC Statewide Legislative Goals (Item 3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deborah Craig-Ray led a discussion of county proposals for the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners' 2015 legislative goals process, focusing on Sheriff's Office requests regarding penalties/72-month minimum enhancements for stolen firearms (GS 14-72 / 15A-1340.16A) and shortening unclaimed livestock holding times by 10 days, alongside concerns over restrictive state childcare assistance legislation. Commissioners agreed to place the legislative goals package on the upcoming consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Bionomic Educational Training Center (BETC) Presentation at Southern High School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Soil and Water Conservation Director Eddie Culberson presented the BETC program developed at Southern High School to prepare students for high-demand, entry-level agricultural and plant science jobs that do not require a four-year degree. He reported that participating students installed 13 rain gardens—including at Moorhead Montessori Elementary and Stirrup Iron Creek—and grossed $9,537 through plant sales and installations.

agenda_items.title: County Facility After-Hours and Weekend Fee Policy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, commissioners questioned General Services and staff regarding uncaptured HVAC chiller, utility, and security overtime costs when opening buildings like the Human Services Complex on weekends for departmental outreach events (citing $960 room and $561 security charges for an upcoming Public Health Saturday event). Commissioners cautioned against unfunded subsidies and weighed departmental budgeting versus weekday evening access before agreeing to place the policy on next Monday's consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Constituent Inquiry Portal Demo and Closing Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff demonstrated a new centralized tracking portal allowing commissioners and staff to submit constituent inquiries, assign them to department heads, monitor workload, and maintain a searchable archive; Chair Page noted IT would schedule brief one-on-one walkthroughs with each commissioner. Staff also noted receipt of a letter from the Sheriff's legal counsel regarding the jail and deferred Item 7 because the Board was 30 minutes late for a joint school and city leadership meeting.

votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Board rules to allow immediate action on removing a member from the Durham City-County Appearance Commission for poor attendance.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 25, 2014 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved the August 4, 2014 work session minutes (5-0), passed the consent agenda Items A–J and L–M after pulling Item K at the County Attorney's request (5-0), and unanimously adjusted the Sheriff's salary to the peer-county median of $137,262 plus a 3% increase following his annual evaluation (5-0). The Board recognized Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton on her election as Second Vice President of the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners and Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. on his appointment as Vice Chair of NACo's Human Services and Education Steering Committee, and the County Attorney introduced legal intern Alicia Houston. Commissioners also discussed Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) confusion and diversity outreach for the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) before making ballot appointments to BPAC, the Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, and the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council. The Board then adjourned into closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) (5-0) before finally adjourning at 8:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Closed Session Report, and Commissioner Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page reported that the Board had met in closed session and provided direction to staff, then led the Pledge of Allegiance and standard county broadcast, boards and commissions, and office-hours announcements. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs announced a free fall lawn care clinic on September 13 hosted by the Durham County Soil and Water Conservation District and the Sierra Club to help reduce nutrient runoff into local lakes, and thanked Pearsontown Elementary School third graders for their letters.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 4, 2014 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the August 4, 2014 work session with no corrections noted. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions of NCACC and NACo Appointments and Legal Intern Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton on her election as Second Vice President of the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners (the first Durham County commissioner to serve as an NCACC officer) and Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. on his appointment as Vice Chair of the National Association of Counties Human Services and Education Steering Committee. Later in the session, the County Attorney introduced third-year NCCU School of Law intern Alicia Houston.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–J and L–M; Item K Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page noted that the County Attorney requested pulling Item K to return at a later date. Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. moved approval of Items A–J and L–M, seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted facility renovations and partnership improvements at the Animal Protection Society shelter under Item L.

agenda_items.title: Sheriff Annual Performance Review and Salary Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a favorable annual evaluation of the Sheriff's accomplishments, a motion was made and seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs to set the Sheriff's salary at the peer-county median of $137,262 and apply a 3% increase.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and JCCPC/BPAC Outreach Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners paused briefly to clarify confusion from the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) regarding Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) vacancies after the City appointed an earlier JCCPC nominee, and noted the need for broader diversity outreach for BPAC and the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission. The Board then voted by ballot, appointing Jennifer McDuffie and Malcolm White to BPAC, Clarence Mayner and Lao Reuber to the Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, and Patricia Evans to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton moved, seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, to adjourn to closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) to prevent disclosure of privileged or confidential information not considered a public record under Chapter 132. The Board later returned and adjourned the meeting at 8:30 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: During its August 4, 2014 worksession, the Durham Board of County Commissioners pulled Item 4 (Healing with Care funding request) for a future session pending staff information and voted unanimously to suspend the rules to extend the 30-minute public comment period (5-0) for 26 registered speakers. Public commenters debated Durham County's ~$1 million annual contract with security firm G4S over alleged human rights abuses in Israel and occupied Palestine alongside a G4S employee defending the company's local charitable record, as well as detention center education, oral health, and Healing with Care. The Board reviewed proposed amendments to its Rules of Procedure for board governance and citizen appointments, and voted unanimously to suspend the rules (5-0) and approve an assignment of the South Parking Deck lease from American Campus LLC to American General Life Insurance Company and American Home Insurance Company (5-0). Commissioners also reviewed board directives, with the County Manager announcing a new single-portal tracking system and staff confirming the Sheriff's August 28 evaluation.

agenda_items.title: Opening and Pull of Item 4 (Healing with Care Funding Request)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page called the worksession to order at 9:10 a.m. and announced that Item 4, a funding request from Healing with Care, was pulled so staff could assemble additional information for a future worksession. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs thanked community supporters, emailers, and petition signers in attendance for Healing with Care.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments and Extension of Public Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With 26 speakers signed up, Chair Michael D. Page initially allotted one minute per speaker to fit within the 30-minute rule. Multiple residents and members of Jewish Voice for Peace urged the County to cancel its $1 million annual security contract with G4S over human rights allegations in Israel and Palestine, while a 25-year G4S employee defended the company's local service and charitable giving; other speakers addressed oral health, jail education programs, sheriff accountability, and Healing with Care. When time expired with four to five speakers remaining, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to suspend the rules and extend public comment, which passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Rules of Procedure for the Board of County Commissioners and Citizen Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney and Clerk to the Board reviewed proposed amendments to the Board's Rules of Procedure, including meeting questioning procedures and potentially expanding membership on a commission to improve diversity and activity. Staff agreed to check relevant state statutes and place the Rules of Procedure updates on the August 11 consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: American Campus South Parking Deck Lease Assignment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director George Quick presented a request to approve the assignment of a May 22, 2014 lease with American Campus LLC for the South Parking Deck to American General Life Insurance Company and American Home Insurance Company. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. seconded motions both to suspend the rules for immediate action and to approve the lease assignment.

agenda_items.title: Review of Board of County Commissioners Directives and Work Session Follow-Ups
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the directives report with staff. In response to Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow's question on tracking budget-deliberation requests such as total security costs, the County Manager announced that IT staff and high school interns were building a unified tracking portal for presentation in September. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs verified the rollover of prior-year funds for a newly hired youth coordinator position, and the Board confirmed August 28 for the Sheriff's annual evaluation.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 28, 2014 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners celebrated Durham County winning the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation 2014 Culture of Health Prize, approved an economic development incentive grant for Argos Therapeutics (5-0), and passed the consent agenda including pulled Item J extending the Probation and Parole office lease for three years (5-0). Following a closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), the Board took three votes on appointed officials' compensation: approving a 3% increase for the County Attorney, Tax Assessor, Clerk to the Board, and Register of Deeds by a 4-1 split voice vote (confirmed Ayes included mover Brenda A. Howerton and seconder Wendy Jacobs; the single Nay and remaining two Ayes among Michael D. Page, Fred Foster Jr., and Ellen W. Reckhow were not identified by name in the voice vote), approving a market-value salary of $120,500 plus two years of insurance credit for the Tax Administrator by a 3-2 split voice vote (confirmed Ayes included mover Ellen W. Reckhow and seconder Wendy Jacobs; the two Nays and third Aye among Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, and Fred Foster Jr. were not named in the voice vote, though one dissenter objected on employee fairness grounds), and unanimously rolling a $1,500 annual vehicle allowance into the Clerk to the Board's salary (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Recognition: Robert Wood Johnson Foundation 2014 Culture of Health Prize
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Gayle Harris, staff, and community partners were recognized for Durham County receiving the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation 2014 Culture of Health Prize. Remarks highlighted collaborative health, trails, East Durham Children's Initiative, Lincoln Community Health Center, and poverty-reduction work, followed by a prize video and presentation of the Culture of Health flag.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–S; Item J Pulled for Separate Discussion)

At 00:51:15, the Board discussed Item J, a three-year lease extension for Probation and Parole, emphasizing the goal of relocating leased offices (currently costing over $500,000 countywide, nearly half for Probation and Parole) into renovated county-owned space once Board of Elections, Juvenile Justice, and EMS transition to the judicial building; Item J then passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Investment Funds for Argos Therapeutics
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton presented an economic development incentive recommendation for Argos Therapeutics. Commissioners praised workforce partnerships with Durham Tech, NCCU's BRITE program, and Duke University to retain local graduates, and company executive Randall Gallo spoke briefly. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded.

Sharp (Convention Center Authority), Adam Clayton and Gayle Harris (Criminal Justice Advisory Committee), and Carnetta Reed and Sharon Brinson (Women's Commission).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adjourned to closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to review appointed officials. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session (Audio Only)
meetings.executive_summary: At its storm-impacted audio-only June 23, 2014 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved the June 2 and May 27, 2014 minutes with a wording correction (5-0) and heard County Manager Wendell Davis present the FY 2014–2015 Budget Ordinance featuring a 79.31-cent property tax rate (a 1.87-cent increase, lowered from the original 2.73-cent proposal due to higher property valuations) and $60.5 million in debt service, along with funding for the employee compensation study, farmland protection, and clerk staffing. The Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A–V excluding pulled Item K (5-0) and later approved Item K unanimously after public discussion on detention, job training, and mental health (5-0). Commissioners also unanimously approved an amendment to the 2011 Scattered Site Housing Grant shifting reconstruction funds to general rehabilitation after two households exited the program (5-0), and made ballot appointments to several county boards before adjourning for summer recess.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 9, 2014 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners issued a resolution honoring the life and legacy of former North Carolina Commerce Secretary J. Keith Crisco, proclaimed June 2014 as National Home Ownership Month with the Durham Regional Financial Center, and honored Durham Children's Choir founder Scott Hill. During the public hearing on the proposed FY 2014–2015 budget, speakers urged the Board to restore the zeroed-out $77,000 Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) matching grant program and raised concerns about record expungement and the G4S security contract. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Chair Michael D. Page clarified that the proposed cuts were staff-identified options to reduce the 2.73-cent tax increase proposal rather than final board decisions, with Reckhow urging preservation of the DOST matching grants and requesting a status report on the G4S contract before renewal. The Board then entered closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (5-0) with no substantive legislative votes taken in open session.

agenda_items.title: Opening and Commissioner Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page welcomed attendees to the FY 2014–2015 budget public hearing session and scratched Item 4 (minutes) as minutes were scheduled for distribution on June 23. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs announced the Durham County Library Summer Reading program (June 14–August 9), and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton announced the June 11 child protection webinar, the June 30 gun safety and free gun-lock distribution event, honored writer Maya Angelou, and offered Father's Day wishes.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Former Commerce Secretary J. Keith Crisco
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a Board resolution honoring the late J. Keith Crisco, North Carolina Secretary of Commerce from 2009 to 2013, crediting his leadership in recruiting nearly 120,000 jobs and over $27 billion in investment and supporting Durham County's entrepreneurial startups.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: June 2014 as National Home Ownership Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a proclamation requested by Durham Regional Financial Center officials (Chairman Daryl Grant, Secretary Diane Pledger/Plej, and President Glendola Massenberg-Beasley) declaring June 2014 as National Home Ownership Month and encouraging residents to seek housing counseling and affordable mortgage options.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Durham Children's Choir Director Scott Hill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page introduced a resolution honoring retired educator Scott Hill, founder and director of the Durham Children's Choir, following her final concert at Duke University.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2014–2015 Budget (DOST Matching Grants, Tax Rate, and G4S)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the budget public hearing, speakers including the Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association president urged the Board not to eliminate the $77,000 Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) matching grant program or cut open space protection by 20%, highlighting its role in leveraging outside funds and protecting ~3,000 acres of farmland; speakers also raised criminal record expungement and G4S. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Chair Page, and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton clarified that the proposed cuts were staff-generated options to lower the 2.73-cent tax increase request rather than final board decisions, while Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow called for preserving the DOST matching grants and requested a staff report on the G4S contract before any renewal.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 2, 2014 worksession, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard public comments from Durham Community Enrichment Organization representative James Chavis requesting $50,000 for detention center education teachers and security officers, and from residents on criminal justice issues. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned the value of funding a vacant Assistant District Attorney position while the county jail population was at a decade low (512–520), prompting the County Manager to schedule an August worksession with the Sheriff, DA, and Criminal Justice Partnership. Staff also presented proposed revisions to the Durham County Living Wage Policy (slated for the consent agenda), reviewed quarterly budget reports and OPEB/fund-balance compliance ahead of consent action, and fielded commissioner requests on the Community Health Trust Fund, swap funds, Affordable Care Act impacts, and fire tax district insurance rates before entering closed session and adjourning at 11:36 a.m. (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Detention Center Education and Pre-Trial Justice
agenda_items.discussion_summary: James Chavis of the Durham Community Enrichment Organization urged the Board to budget $50,000 for two part-time teachers and two part-time security officers so all detainees at the Durham County Detention Center can access educational programming beyond START, IEP, and upcoming GED offerings. Following additional comments on pre-trial detention, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noted that the jail population had dropped to a decade low (~512–520) without an Assistant DA position filled and requested performance benchmarks; the County Manager scheduled a comprehensive August worksession with the Sheriff, DA, and Gudrun Palmer of Criminal Justice Partnership, including state misdemeanor confinement impacts.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Revisions to Durham County Living Wage Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Drew Cummings and HR Director Cora Wilson presented proposed revisions to the Durham County Living Wage Policy, noting outreach to City of Durham finance staff on contractor living wage applicability (noting state legislation applied to counties rather than cities) and clarifying federal FLSA hour schedules for law enforcement, firefighters, and EMS. Commissioners raised market salary discrepancies and directed the policy revision to the next consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Quarterly Budget Reporting, Fund Balance / OPEB Compliance, and Directives Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, staff reviewed quarterly budget reporting, fund-balance policy percentages, and an OPEB (Other Post-Employment Benefits) adjustment arising from credit-rating agency meetings, placing the item on the upcoming Monday consent agenda. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs requested multi-year projections for the Community Health Trust Fund (noting proposed draws doubled from the prior year), swap fund accrual details, ACA/Medicaid impacts on Social Services, and fire-tax-district-level impacts on homeowner insurance ISO ratings, while the Manager noted work on a unified tracking portal for board directives.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With the first part of Item 7 deleted, the Board voted (seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs) to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel. Upon reconvening at 02:29:22, Chair Michael D. Page reported the Board provided direction to staff, and the Board adjourned at 11:36 a.m. on a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Fred Foster Jr.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 27, 2014 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved the May 5 work session and May 12 regular session minutes (5-0) and read a resolution supporting congressional legislation (H.R. 3118 / S. 567) to increase Social Security benefits, which Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs asked to forward to the federal delegation. The Board accepted the Gold Greater Triangle Stewardship Development Award for the Durham County Justice Center and parking deck and recognized Deputy Andre Hinton and Paramedic Taylor Kennedy for receiving Civitan Club community honors. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously adopted Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) changes (5-0), distributed ballots for board and commission appointments, and resolved Commissioner Jacobs's concerns on pulled Consent Item O (opposing state preemption of local tree and fertilizer ordinances) by agreeing to append the Environmental Affairs Board and Keep Durham Beautiful resolutions for delivery to the Durham legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Announcements, and Approval of May 5 and May 12 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the Pledge of Allegiance and standard announcements, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded approval of the May 5, 2014 work session minutes and May 12, 2014 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Increase of Social Security Benefits
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a citizen-requested resolution urging Congress to increase Social Security benefits, citing low cost-of-living adjustments and high retiree medical costs. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow connected the issue to fixed-income residents and stagnant state employee pay ahead of budget deliberations, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked to forward the resolution to Durham's federal congressional delegation, and a volunteer with the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare thanked the Board for endorsing H.R. 3118 and S. 567.

agenda_items.title: Gold Greater Triangle Stewardship Development Award and Civitan Club Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board accepted the Gold Greater Triangle Stewardship Development Award for environmental stewardship at the Durham County Justice Center and parking deck. Under Item 7, the Sheriff and EMS Director recognized Deputy Andre Hinton and Paramedic Taylor Kennedy for receiving community honors from the Durham Civitan Club.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the meeting, Planning staff presented Comprehensive Plan text updates derived from the Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR), noting the Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0 on April 8, 2014. meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Michael D. Page absent and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presiding as Madam Chair, the four-member Durham Board of County Commissioners (Howerton, Fred Foster Jr., Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs) approved prior minutes (4-0), issued proclamations for EMS Week and the 100th anniversary of North Carolina Cooperative Extension, and approved the unpulled Consent Agenda items (4-0). Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously adopted targeted City-County Inspections Department permit fee adjustments (4-0). Commissioners also unanimously approved a 50/50 City-County public-private development agreement for the downtown Jack Tar and Austin Lawrence Partners City Center mixed-use project (4-0), and approved pulled Consent Items A, C, D, F, and G (4-0) after questioning funding reductions for El Futuro, Juvenile Justice Project funding, and requesting clearer future explanations when lower procurement bids are deemed non-responsive.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided, offered belated Mother's Day wishes, and delivered standard announcements, while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs announced Durham Bike Month activities. The Board approved the late-April regular session minutes by a 4-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: EMS Week and NC Cooperative Extension 100th Anniversary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read a proclamation designating May 18–24, 2014 as Emergency Medical Services Week in Durham County. The Board also presented a proclamation honoring 100 years of North Carolina Cooperative Extension service (May 19) and its support for local food access, followed by remarks from the Department of Social Services Director.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Unpulled Items B, H–N, P–Q)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Items E and O already removed, commissioners pulled Items C, D, F, and G for discussion and Item A for questions. The Board approved the remaining consent items (B, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, P, Q) by a 4-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: City-County Inspections Department Permit Fee Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Inspections Director Gene Bradham presented targeted trade permit fee adjustments (leaving new single-family and commercial permit fees unchanged) along with new fees for incomplete plan resubmittals and first HVAC replacement reinspections to improve efficiency and cost recovery, noting prior City Council approval. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, the Board approved the ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Public-Private Development Agreement: Jack Tar / City Center Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a community development agreement establishing a 50/50 City-County public support share for the Jack Tar redevelopment (14,000 sq ft retail and rooftop bar/lounge) paired with Austin Lawrence Partners' 25-story City Center mixed-use tower (subgrade parking, retail, office space, and 133 apartments) in the Downtown Durham National Historic District, following City Council approval on April 24. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow thanked staff and developers for compromise language, and the Board approved the agreement 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items A, C, D, F, and G (Nonprofit Funding & Procurement Bids)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On Item A, a commissioner questioned why El Futuro's recommended funding dropped from $46,100 to $35,485 and noted the Juvenile Justice Project's $70,000 countywide school reach before Item A passed 4-0. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 5, 2014 worksession, the Durham Board of County Commissioners—with Fred Foster Jr. granted an excused absence due to illness (4-0)—suspended its rules (4-0) and unanimously authorized $500,000 from the Community Health Trust Fund to support Lincoln Community Health Center's adoption of Duke University Health System's Epic electronic health record system (4-0), urging Duke to help cover the remaining $500,000 needed. The Board reviewed Comprehensive Plan trends and issues, with Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs emphasizing mixed-income affordable housing near transit stations, land banking, transit-corridor rezoning, and green infrastructure. Commissioners also reviewed a revised Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO Memorandum of Understanding and courthouse parking lease rates for the consent agenda, briefly discussed a stalled $15 fast-food worker wage resolution under board directives without a vote, and entered closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4) (4-0) before adjourning at 1:05 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Lincoln Community Health Center and Duke Health System Epic EHR Collaboration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff, Lincoln Community Health Center CEO Phillip Harewood, CMO Dr. Howard Eisenson, DCHC trustee Craig Savage, and Duke Regional Hospital President Katie Galbraith discussed Lincoln's integration onto Duke's Epic electronic health record system. Finance Director George Quick recommended $500,000 (half of the $1 million request) from the ~$7 million unrestricted Community Health Trust Fund balance, with Lincoln absorbing ~$250,000 in annual maintenance and commissioners urging Duke Health System to cover the other half. The Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and 4-0 to authorize the $500,000 allocation.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Fred Foster Jr. and Afternoon Board Retreat
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded excusing Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. due to illness (4-0). Because entering the budget cycle would make rescheduling with a contracted facilitator difficult, the Board decided to proceed with its 1:00–5:00 p.m. retreat.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Trends & Issues: Transit-Oriented Affordable Housing and Land Use
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated presentation segment, Planning staff reviewed long-term 25-year land supply trends, suburban development patterns, and post-WWII structures entering the 50-year historic preservation window in 2014. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow emphasized prioritizing mixed-income affordable housing around transit stops per recent Board resolution, while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs highlighted land banking, transit-corridor rezoning incentives, green building, and green infrastructure.

agenda_items.title: DCHC MPO Revised MOU and Courthouse Parking Lease Rates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ellen Beckman and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow (MPO TCC representative) presented technical corrections to the Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO Memorandum of Understanding. Staff also reviewed 20-year courthouse parking space lease escalations, which were directed to the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Review: Fast-Food Worker Wage Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under directives review, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs inquired about the status of a September request for a resolution supporting a $15/hour wage for fast-food workers. Discussion indicated the Board was not advancing a $15/hour resolution (with a commissioner stating opposition to $15 while suggesting pushing toward a $10.10-level compromise), and no formal action was taken.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded entering closed session to discuss business/industry location or expansion and consult with legal counsel under attorney-client privilege (4-0). After reconvening at 03:58:43 and reporting further direction to staff, the Board adjourned at 1:05 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 28, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the April 7 and April 14 minutes, consent agenda items A, D, G, and H (after the County Manager pulled items B, C, E, and F and Item 11 was removed), and an excused absence for Chair Page for the May 12 meeting, with no split or contested votes. The Board issued proclamations for Workforce Development Professionals Month (highlighting the year-round Durham YouthWork Internship Program) and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month, adopted a memorial resolution honoring late banking and civil rights leader Ferdinand Vincent 'Pete' Allison Jr., and directed that a copy of an environmental protection resolution with a cover letter be sent to the Governor and the Secretary of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. In its sole substantive budget action, the Board unanimously approved Capital Project Amendment No. 14CPA0008—presented by EMS Director Skip Kirkwood—reducing EMS Station No. 1 renovation funds by $365,000 to procure station-location analysis software, hire engineering/architectural reviewers for existing co-located stations, and engage a planner ahead of the fall Capital Improvement Plan update. The Board also completed ballot appointments to the Durham County Hospital Corporation, Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, and Open Space and Trails Commission, then entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) on real property acquisition for the Rougemont critical water infrastructure project before adjourning at 9:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the session and recognized the County Manager, who pulled consent agenda items B, C, E, and F to return at the next meeting. Page delivered county television, board/commission recruitment, and Chair office-hour announcements, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs announced a May 6 memorial plaque and tree dedication for former Commissioner Becky Heron at Durham County Stadium and a May 3 Durham Public Schools event.

agenda_items.title: Item 4: Approval of April 7, 2014 Work Session and April 14, 2014 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the April 7, 2014 Work Session and April 14, 2014 Regular Session. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the minutes were approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Resolutions (Workforce Development, Children's Mental Health, Pete Allison Jr., and Environment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented proclamations for May 2014 as Workforce Development Professionals Month (with workforce board officials highlighting the year-round Durham YouthWork Internship Program) and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow, Fred Foster Jr., and Brenda A. Howerton offered tributes to late banking and civil rights leader Ferdinand Vincent 'Pete' Allison Jr. in presenting a memorial resolution to Dr. Lavonia Allison and family, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read an environmental protection resolution with a request to send copies and a cover letter to the Governor and DENR Secretary.

agenda_items.title: Item 10: Consent Agenda (Items A, D, G, and H) and Removal of Item 11
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With items B, C, E, and F previously pulled by the County Manager and no public speakers signed up, the Board approved consent agenda items A, D, G, and H unanimously by voice vote (seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton). Chair Page also recognized the Public Health Department's 100-year celebration and announced that Item 11 was removed from the agenda to be taken up at a later date.

agenda_items.title: Item 12: Capital Project Amendment No. 14CPA0008 (EMS Station No. 1 Renovations & Facilities Study)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: EMS Director Skip Kirkwood requested pausing EMS Station No. 1 renovations and shifting $365,000 in county contribution funds to purchase location-analysis software (citing a Lee County, Florida case study), hire an architectural/engineering firm to evaluate four co-located fire/EMS stations, and engage a planner for a comprehensive EMS facilities plan for the fall CIP update. Kirkwood noted that co-locating ambulances with fire trucks forfeits the 'first responder advantage' and that community paramedicine staff need dedicated vehicle parking; Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. confirmed the $2,603,499 project funding source before the Board unanimously approved the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 13: Board and Commission Appointments and Chair Excused Absence Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners cast written ballots for multiple boards and commissions, during which Chair Michael D. Page requested and received unanimous approval to be excused from the May 12, 2014 meeting. The Clerk announced selections for the Durham County Hospital Corporation (Philip Harwood, Gail Belvett, Robert Newman, Katrina Avery, Charles Cooperburg), Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (Robert Gaddy), Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee (LaSalle Wepley Jr.), and Open Space and Trails Commission (Charles Welch, LaDonna Summers).

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Closed Session (Real Property Acquisition for Critical Water Infrastructure) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to instruct staff regarding price and material terms for acquiring real property for the Rougemont critical water infrastructure project. Upon returning to open session, the Board adjourned unanimously at 9:00 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Motion carries'); all five seated commissioners were present and active during the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes from the April 7, 2014 Work Session and April 14, 2014 Regular Session without amendment.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Decreased $365,000 in county contribution funding from EMS Station No. 1 renovations to fund location-analysis software, engineering/architectural assessment of existing stations, and a comprehensive EMS facilities plan for the CIP.

votes.item_title: Excuse Chair Michael D. Page from May 12, 2014 Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimous').
votes.discussion_detail: Granted Chair Michael D. Page an excused absence for the May 12, 2014 meeting.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to instruct staff on real property acquisition terms for the critical water infrastructure project.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 14, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs absent on an excused absence previously granted April 7), the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened by swearing in new County Manager Wendell M. Davis, administered by Judge Wilts. Davis reflected on his earlier tenure as Deputy County Manager under former Manager David Thompson, highlighted county facilities built over the prior 14 years, and pledged a strong focus on human capital and education, while Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. welcomed him—with Foster acknowledging the board's earlier divisions and protracted transition. The Board unanimously approved the March 24, 2014 Regular Session minutes and Consent Agenda Items A through N (with a meeting-time correction on Item K), with no split or contested votes. Commissioners also observed National County Government Month, discussed child abuse prevention and the Triple P positive parenting grant, recognized Ernie Mills' appointment to the Governor's Task Force on Homelessness, and met in closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on business location or expansion before adjourning at 3:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In Ceremony and Remarks of County Manager Wendell M. Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Judge Wilts administered the oath of office to new County Manager Wendell M. Davis alongside his family. Davis recalled returning to Durham County 14 years after serving as Deputy County Manager under David Thompson (present in the audience), citing major capital facilities like the Human Services Complex, Judicial Center, and regional libraries while emphasizing human capital and educational opportunity as his central priorities. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Fred Foster Jr. welcomed Davis, with Foster noting the protracted transition amid a divided board and staffing gaps.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Approval of March 24, 2014 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following brief announcements, the Board considered the minutes from the March 24, 2014 Regular Session. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Items 6 & 7: National County Government Month Proclamation, Child Abuse Prevention Remarks, and Homelessness Task Force Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented a proclamation recognizing April as National County Government Month (noting staff member Deborah Craig-Gray's absence due to family illness). Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow highlighted data from a child-welfare resolution showing high abuse rates among girls ages 0 to 6 and urged community participation in the Triple P (Positive Parenting Program) grant initiative; Page also recognized Ernie Mills on his swearing-in to the Governor's Task Force on Homelessness.

agenda_items.title: Item 8: Consent Agenda (Items A through N as Corrected)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no public speakers signed up, a commissioner requested a technical correction to Item K's resolution time (reflecting the daytime meeting time rather than 7:00 p.m.). On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved Items A through N as corrected.

agenda_items.title: Item 10: Closed Session (Economic Development) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss matters relating to the location or expansion of a business or industry. Upon returning at 01:30:32, Chair Page announced the Board provided direction to staff, and the meeting adjourned unanimously at 3:30 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 7, 2014 Worksession presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard citizen comments—including Threshold Clubhouse volunteer interpreter Stephanie Gans urging the Durham County Jail to accept consular IDs for family visitation—and unanimously suspended its rules to adopt a proclamation supporting Durham TRY's (Together for Resilient Youth) April 12 youth substance-abuse prevention conference, with no split or contested votes. The Durham County Women's Commission presented on food insecurity among local women and families, citing a ~65% free/reduced-price lunch rate in Durham Public Schools, decentralized food pantries, and urban farming initiatives. Following an omitted middle portion of the transcript digest covering Convention Center marketing, parking deck space turnover, and facility revenues, the Board reviewed county facility fee schedules (including a $50/hour utility recovery rate for courthouse use after judicial feedback and liability waivers for the courthouse gym) and debated state short-session legislative priorities—including full funding for the Justice Reinvestment Act, charter school transparency/diversity, and statutory limits on local rent control. After meeting in closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and (a)(3), the Board unanimously granted Commissioner Wendy Jacobs an excused absence for the April 14 meeting and adjourned at 4:55 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments (Jail Visitation Foreign ID Policy and Additional Speaker)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stephanie Gans of Threshold Clubhouse spoke on behalf of Spanish-speaking residents unable to visit family members in the Durham County Jail because foreign IDs other than passports (such as Mexican consular IDs) were not accepted, noting outreach to the Mexican Consulate and Durham Police Chief Lopez. Chair Page asked the County Attorney's Office to follow up and look into options, and a second speaker (Tarantino) also addressed the Board.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Proclamation for Durham TRY Prevention Conference
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To adopt a proclamation ahead of Durham TRY's (Together for Resilient Youth) April 12 conference at the Carolina Theatre, the Board unanimously suspended its rules (moved by Wendy Jacobs, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton) and approved the 'Talk It Up, Lock It Up, Drop It Month 2014' proclamation (moved by Brenda A. Howerton, seconded by Wendy Jacobs). Chair Page read statistics on youth prescription painkiller access, Director Wanda Boone accepted the proclamation, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow thanked TRY for its substance-abuse prevention work.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Women's Commission Presentation on Food Insecurity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Women's Commission Chair Gina Dillon, Rosa Anderson, and Bobby Gallagher presented on food insecurity affecting women and families in Durham County, aligning their work with the County's health and well-being strategic goal. Discussion highlighted Durham Public Schools' ~65% free/reduced lunch eligibility and pilot nutrition programs, decentralized pantries (Durham Tech, Senior Center, Rougemont Ruritan Club), the food hub, and urban farming.

agenda_items.title: Convention Center Operations, Parking Deck Turnover, and Revenue Ideas
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a six-hour middle portion truncated in the digest, transcript fragments captured discussion of Convention Center consumer and trade shows with Downtown Durham Inc. and the Chamber, flipping reserved parking spaces on the lower levels of the parking deck to high-turnover event parking, and potentially operating a cafe for additional revenue.

agenda_items.title: County Facilities Fee Policy, Courthouse Utility Fee, and Liability Waivers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed public and nonprofit use fees across County facilities, noting a $50/hour courthouse utility recovery fee after judges objected to a $50-per-courtroom charge. Commissioners and staff discussed phasing implementation around May 1 while awaiting July 1 budget appropriations for Human Services and excluding the under-construction CJRC, as well as governmental immunity and liability waivers for public use of the courthouse gym.

agenda_items.title: State Short-Session Legislative Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed draft legislative priorities for the General Assembly's short session, emphasizing full funding for the Justice Reinvestment Act (unanimously backed by a Crime Cabinet ad hoc committee including Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton) to deliver promised community reinvestment. Discussion also addressed parental/grandparent custody clarification, charter school diversity and enforcement of existing open-meetings and minutes laws, and state statutory preemption barring local rent control.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Excused Absence Request, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(1) (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Wendy Jacobs) and returned at 07:46:46 having provided direction to staff. Before adjourning at 4:55 p.m., the Board unanimously granted Commissioner Wendy Jacobs' request for an excused absence from the April 14, 2014 meeting.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously'). Individual attendance of all five commissioners could not be fully verified because a six-hour middle portion of the transcript was truncated; Page, Howerton, Reckhow, and Jacobs are confirmed active in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Board rules so the proclamation for Durham TRY's upcoming April 12 prevention conference could be voted on during the worksession.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the proclamation recognizing Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) and its April 12, 2014 prevention conference at the Carolina Theatre.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(1))
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to preserve attorney-client privilege and protect privileged/confidential records under Chapter 132.

votes.item_title: Excuse Commissioner Wendy Jacobs from April 14, 2014 Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Granted Commissioner Wendy Jacobs an excused absence for the April 14, 2014 Regular Session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 24, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners presented proclamations honoring new North Carolina Central University Chancellor Dr. Debra Saunders-White and NCCU's MEAC-champion men's basketball team, followed by Chair Page's State of the County address highlighting Board leadership, late former Commissioner Becky Heron, the Human Services Complex, and Public Health and DSS achievements. Following a truncated middle segment, the Board voted 5-0 after public hearings to approve an economic development incentive for a $10 million historic downtown building rehabilitation creating 90 new jobs and to adopt a FY 2014 order extending the obligation period for remaining 2007 General Obligation school bond funds. The meeting's sole contested vote occurred on pulled Consent Agenda Item G—a joint Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) among Durham County, the City of Durham, and Durham Public Schools for a coordinated youth initiative—which passed 4-1 with Chair Michael D. Page, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs voting Aye and Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. voting Nay due to objections to the process and the organization given oversight. The Board also completed ballot appointments to four advisory boards and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) before adjourning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations Honoring NCCU Chancellor Debra Saunders-White and NCCU Men's Basketball Team
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read proclamations welcoming North Carolina Central University's 11th Chancellor and first permanent female leader, Dr. Debra Saunders-White, for Installation Week 2014, and saluting the NCCU men's basketball team for its 28-6 season, undefeated home record, MEAC championship, and NCAA Tournament appearance.

agenda_items.title: State of the County Message
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page delivered the State of the County address, recognizing Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton (running for NCACC Second Vice President), former Chair Fred Foster Jr., Wendy Jacobs, veteran Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, and the 29-year legacy of late former Commissioner Becky Heron. Page also commended Interim County Manager Lee Worsley, Public Health Director Gayle Harris, DSS Director Michael Becketts, and the $9 million Human Services Complex expansion.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive for Historic Downtown Building Rehabilitation ($10M / 90 Jobs)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle portion truncated in the digest, the Board concluded review of an economic development incentive supporting a company's $10 million investment to rehabilitate a historic downtown building and create 90 new jobs (Managing Director Daniel Robinson representing the company). Chair Page opened and closed the public hearing with no speakers, and the Board approved the incentive 5-0 on a motion by Wendy Jacobs seconded by Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Public Hearing on FY 2014 General Obligation Bond Extension Order (2007 Referendum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Financial Officer George Quick presented a statutory request to extend the period to obligate and spend remaining funds from the 2007 General Obligation bond referendum, noting the re-appropriated balance would fund renovations at multiple schools. With no public speakers signed up, Chair Page opened and closed the public hearing, and the Board unanimously approved the extension order.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed communication from the Library Board of Trustees chair referenced by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and submitted written ballots. At 03:23:34, the Clerk announced selections to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (Anita Daniels), Library Board of Trustees (Rosemary Kitchen), Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee (Dorothy Justice and Joyce Nettles), and Workforce Development Board (Henry McCoy Jr.).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Agenda Item G: Joint Youth Initiative MOU with DPS and City of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. pulled Consent Agenda Item G to state on the record that he opposed the MOU because he did not support the process or the organization given oversight of the youth initiative. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Chair Michael D. Page agreed to seek a community-input update and place the broader coordination process on the upcoming Board retreat agenda, while staff clarified how unspent May–June funds would fall to fund balance ahead of FY15 budgeting; Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval (seconded by Reckhow), and the item passed 4-1 with Foster dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Item 19: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege. Upon returning at 03:36:25 with direction given to staff, the Board adjourned unanimously.

votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote ('This motion carries five to zero').

votes.notes: Passed 4-1 by voice vote ('All opposed. No. One. Okay. So this item passes four to one'). Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. stated on the record at 03:05:11 that he would not support the item.

disagreements.issue: Process and Oversight Organization for Joint County-City-DPS Youth Initiative MOU (Consent Item G)
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. pulled Consent Item G to oppose the interlocal MOU establishing oversight for a joint youth initiative with the City of Durham and Durham Public Schools, whereas Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and the majority urged moving forward after lengthy interlocal negotiations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the negotiated MOU among Durham County, the City, and DPS to coordinate disconnected youth services while scheduling follow-up on community input and future budget structure.
side_a_arguments: Both the IBM and MDC studies identified disconnected youth services in Durham needing stronger coordination.
Negotiating the MOU among Durham Public Schools, the City, and the County took a long time and should not be stalled.
Broader process concerns and community input can be reviewed at the upcoming Board retreat and during the upcoming FY15 budget cycle.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the MOU because the selection process and oversight organization are unsatisfactory.
side_b_arguments: Did not support the process used to develop the oversight structure.
Did not support the specific organization designated to have oversight over the youth initiative.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve Consent Item G passed 4-1 (Ayes: Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: Fred Foster Jr.), with Chair Page adding the broader coordination process to the Board retreat agenda.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 10, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the February 24, 2014 minutes, Consent Agenda Items A and C through G (after pulling Item B for discussion), pulled Item B on surplus county vehicles, and a personnel closed session, with no split or contested votes. During announcements and proclamations, Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton requested scheduling budget hearings with Partners Against Crime (PACs), commissioners recognized County Attorney Lowell Siler and Women's History Month, and the Board proclaimed March 2014 as National Professional Social Work Month while praising DSS for high-performing childcare subsidy management and navigating state NC FAST food-assistance delays. During the FY 2014-15 pre-budget public comment period introduced by Interim Budget Director Keith Lane, residents and InterNeighborhood Council/HOA advocates urged funding in the Planning Department budget to complete the stalled UDO cell tower ordinance ahead of the Board's budget retreat. On pulled Consent Item B, Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. and commissioners questioned vehicle-disposal practices so departments would not surplus usable vehicles and seek replacements in the budget, before approving the surplus list unanimously upon staff confirmation of the County's 85%-repair-cost replacement policy.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, PAC Budget Hearings Request, and Tribute to County Attorney Lowell Siler
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the session from recess and delivered standard county announcements. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton asked staff to schedule budget hearings with Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts (with Page noting mixed turnout in past quadrant sessions and suggesting central locations), and commissioners recognized Women's History Month and praised County Attorney Lowell Siler and his 10-attorney office.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments (Durham County Jail Concerns)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Tarantino and Peterson addressed the Board regarding individuals held in the Durham County Jail who they stated were innocent of alleged offenses, offering to provide names to the County during the week. Chair Page asked the County Manager to record the request and follow up.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Approval of February 24, 2014 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes of the February 24, 2014 Regular Session. Moved by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Proclamation for National Professional Social Work Month (March 2014)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation honoring March 2014 as National Professional Social Work Month to Department of Social Services staff. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs, and Brenda A. Howerton praised DSS leadership (including Michael Becketts, Javetta, and Rhonda) for securing additional state childcare subsidy reallocations and supporting residents through state NC FAST food-assistance backlogs, with Jacobs calling for a broader staff celebration the following month.

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Consent Agenda (Items A, C, D, E, F, and G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After pulling Item B at the request of Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Michael D. Page for separate discussion, the Board approved Consent Agenda Items A, C, D, E, F, and G on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: FY 2014-15 Pre-Budget Public Comment (UDO Cell Tower Ordinance Funding)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Budget Director Keith Lane introduced the annual pre-budget public hearing ahead of the Board's March 13 budget retreat. Following a truncated middle segment, speakers Hamner and Donna Rudolph (Eagles Point HOA, citing the InterNeighborhood Council's two years of work) urged the Board to fund Planning Department staff or a temporary consultant in FY 2014-15 so the cell tower ordinance text amendment for residential zones would not be stalled as a low priority.

agenda_items.title: Item 9 (Pulled Consent Item B): Surplus County Vehicles Disposition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. questioned why departments were surplusing vehicles and cautioned he would scrutinize FY15 budget requests for new vehicles, while Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton asked about vehicle donations and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs questioned auctioning vehicles listed in 'good condition.' Purchasing staff and CFO George Quick explained that the County's vehicle replacement policy triggers disposal based on mileage, age, or repair costs exceeding 85% of value and noted serviceable vehicles are offered to other departments first, after which the Board approved Item B unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications/employment. Returning at 01:29:02 with direction given to staff, the Board adjourned unanimously at 8:33 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Approval of February 24, 2014 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously'); all five seated commissioners were present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the February 24, 2014 Regular Session minutes as presented.

votes.item_title: Item 9 (Pulled Consent Item B): Approval of Surplus County Vehicles Disposition
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved disposal/auction of surplus county vehicles after staff explained the County's vehicle replacement policy (mileage, age, and 85% repair-cost threshold) and interdepartmental transfer screening.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; Board returned at 01:29:02 and reported direction given to staff.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to consider personnel qualifications, performance, or employment conditions.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 24, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners honored late longtime Commissioner Becky M. Heron (1982–2011; first female Board chair 1994–1996) in a memorial resolution presented to her husband Duncan Heron and family, and recognized retiring Budget Director Pam Meyer for 13 years of service and 10 GFOA budget awards. All formal actions passed unanimously (5-0), with no split or contested votes: the Board approved the prior work session and February 10 regular session minutes, adopted the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Item K and updating an outdated signature block), and authorized staff to negotiate a contract for the downtown City Center / Jack Tar community development project. On pulled Consent Item K, Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. clarified for the public record that the $12,935 matching-grant total comprised $12,400 for the Eno River Association and $535 for the Museum of Durham History before the Board approved it 5-0. Following a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(5), the Board unanimously approved a settlement agreement with New Atlantic Contracting and authorized staff to obtain conservation easement options on farm properties at 2132 Infinity Road and 4103 Adcock Road.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of Work Session and February 10, 2014 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page delivered standard county announcements and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton announced a March 13 NCCU public administration event honoring Tyrone Baines and Howard Clement. On a motion by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs (seconded on voice vote), the Board unanimously approved the minutes of the recent work session and February 10, 2014 Regular Session.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Memorial Resolution Honoring Former Commissioner Becky M. Heron
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read a resolution honoring former Commissioner Becky M. Heron (elected 1982, retired 2011, passed away January 23, 2014), Durham's first female BOCC Chair (1994–1996) and 1995 NCACC Outstanding County Commissioner, highlighting her advocacy for environmental protection, Little River Park, the Center for Senior Life, animal control, and transportation. Commissioners presented the resolution to her husband Duncan Heron and family.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Retiring Budget Director Pam Meyer
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution honoring retiring Budget Director Pam Meyer, who served since January 2001, led 13 annual budgets and six 10-year Capital Improvement Plans, and earned 10 GFOA Distinguished Budget Presentation Awards. (The middle section immediately following this tribute was truncated in the transcript digest.)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item K, with Signature-Block Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Consent Item K pulled by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr., commissioners noticed an outdated signature block on a consent resolution listing former Chair MaryAnn Black and former Clerk Garry Umstead. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved the consent agenda with the necessary signature-block updates.

agenda_items.title: City Center / Jack Tar Community Development Project Negotiation Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed the downtown City Center / Jack Tar community development project—noting it would be a signature downtown building exceeding the SunTrust building's height—and commended CFO George Quick, Drew, and the County Attorney's Office for carrying extra workload during the manager transition. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the Board voted unanimously to move forward with negotiating a contract for the project.

agenda_items.title: Item 10: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During ballot distribution, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked the Clerk's Office to provide hard-copy applicant summary sheets at future meetings. At 01:11:04, the Clerk began announcing ballot results (starting with the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee before remaining lines were omitted in the digest).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item K: Budget Matching Grants (Eno River Association and Museum of Durham History)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. explained he pulled Item K to clarify on the public record that the $12,935 allocation was the combined total—$12,400 to the Eno River Association and $535 to the Museum of Durham History—rather than $12,935 to each organization. Foster then moved approval (seconded on voice vote), and the item passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Closed-Session Actions (New Atlantic Contracting Settlement & Conservation Easements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) (including Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser) and (a)(5) (conservation easements on 2132 Infinity Road and 4103 Adcock Road, and Rougemont critical water infrastructure). Adcock Jr. and Paul S. Adcock), reported staff direction on Rougemont water infrastructure, noted an update without action on Robinson v. Bowser, and adjourned at 9:10 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 10, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A–J (excluding Item H), a $600,000 economic development incentive for Argos Therapeutics (matching a $600,000 City incentive), and Interim County Manager Lee Worsley's amended Fire Study recommendations (after debate over modifying consultant items and engaging the New Hope Fire District). Two items passed on 4-1 split voice votes in which the lone dissenting commissioner was not identified by name on microphone: first, UDO Text Amendment TC1200012 (Article 6 density revisions requested by Horvath Associates) passed 4-1 on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, with one unnamed commissioner among Michael D. Page, Fred Foster Jr., and Wendy Jacobs voting Nay; second, following a personnel closed session, the Board voted 4-1 to appoint Wendell M. Davis as County Manager effective April 14, 2014 at a $198,800 salary and approve his employment contract on a motion by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton, with one unnamed commissioner among Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report, Announcements, and PAC Budget Hearing Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page reported the Board had met in closed session prior to 7:00 p.m. and provided direction to staff. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton urged scheduling budget hearings with Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts (with Page recommending one or two central sessions given low turnout at past quadrant meetings), and commissioners discussed preparing a memorial resolution for late former Commissioner Becky Heron.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Consent Agenda (Items A–G, I, and J)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item H moved to the regular agenda, the Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A through J (excluding Item H) on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Public Hearing — Economic Development Investment Funds for Argos Therapeutics ($600,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Manager Marqueta Welton presented a $600,000 economic development incentive for Durham-headquartered biopharmaceutical firm Argos Therapeutics (matching a $600,000 City of Durham incentive for a $1.2 million local commitment) to support personalized cancer and HIV immunotherapies, job retention, and job creation alongside Durham Tech and NCCU's BRITE training programs. Company Facilities Director Randall Guller attended, Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. asked about the company's initial public offering, and the Board approved the incentive 5-0 after the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Public Hearing — UDO Text Amendment Density Revisions to Article 6 (TC1200012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Michael Stock introduced UDO Text Amendment TC1200012, initiated by Horvath Associates regarding suburban-tier roadway density standards (noting staff had found the original proposal unsupportable; middle discussion was truncated in the digest). Applicant Ron Horvath spoke at public hearing citing tree coverage (20–24%), stormwater (20%), and impervious surface constraints; on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the amendment passed 4-1 by voice vote with one unnamed commissioner opposed.

agenda_items.title: Item 8 (Moved from Consent Item H): Fire Study Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Lee Worsley presented revised Fire Study recommendations modified after meeting with fire chiefs (adjusting item 52 on volunteer policy and deferring action on items 58–61 pending finer-grained analysis). Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. questioned why staff modified or declined recommendations from a paid consultant study, while Worsley and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted the New Hope Fire District had not been fully included in earlier chief talks and parcel-level hydrant/tanker details required staff vetting; Bahama Fire Chief Lynn Needham spoke at the public hearing before the Board unanimously approved the amended recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Appointment of County Manager Wendell M. Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to discuss personnel qualifications and initial employment conditions. Returning at 01:24:35, the Board voted 4-1 on a motion by Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. seconded by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton to appoint Wendell M. Davis as County Manager effective April 14, 2014 at a salary of $198,800 and approve his employment contract (one unnamed commissioner voted Nay), then adjourned at 8:50 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Economic Development Investment Funds for Argos Therapeutics ($600,000)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Motion carries unanimously').
