meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 3, 2014 Worksession—presided over by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton because Chair Michael D. Page was absent under a doctor's care—the Durham Board of County Commissioners took no formal substantive votes and had no split votes, devoting the session to citizen comments, policy work, and financial briefings. During citizen comments, speakers raised safety concerns at Durham Public Schools' Holton Career Center, disputed Crime Cabinet meeting procedures, voiced Bahama Fire Department opposition to several Fire Study recommendations (including staffing mandates, tax-district consolidation, and board-composition limits), and urged immediate adoption of a resolution setting a 15% affordable-housing goal within a half-mile of transit stations for households under 60% AMI. Following a lengthy middle portion truncated in the digest, commissioners discussed issuing two separate wage resolutions—one backing local food workers (for February 10) and another endorsing the federal Fair Minimum Wage Act (for February 24). Chief Financial Officer George Quick and Debt Manager Jessica Brown-Linton also briefed the Board on remaining 2007 General Obligation bond funds ($52 million of $91 million outstanding, primarily for schools), the County's 0.65% variable-rate Bank of America BANs line, and $5.9 million earmarked for Durham Tech ahead of a February 24 financing resolution, before the Board rescheduled its closed session to Wednesday afternoon to accommodate Chair Page and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Citizen Comments (Holton Career Center, Crime Cabinet, Fire Study, Transit Affordable Housing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the worksession while awaiting/excusing Chair Michael D. Page, who was under a doctor's care. Four citizens spoke: James Chavis raised mower safety concerns at Holton Career Center; Ms. Peterson disputed Crime Cabinet public-question procedures; Bahama Fire Chief Lynn Needham opposed Fire Study Recommendations #9 (citing $600,000–$700,000 in added staffing costs), #59 (tax-district consolidation), and #67 (assistant chiefs on the board); and Larissa Seiber urged rapid adoption of Item 3 setting a 15% affordable-housing goal within a half-mile of transit centers for households under 60% AMI, UDO developer incentives, and a joint citizens advisory committee.

agenda_items.title: Item 2: Advisory Board Member Attendance / Removal Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board briefly took up an item concerning potential removal of an advisory board member who had contacted staff explaining her absences were due to a medical issue. (The subsequent four-and-a-half-hour portion of the worksession was truncated in the transcript digest.)

agenda_items.title: Separate Resolutions on Local Food Workers and Federal Fair Minimum Wage Act
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Fred Foster Jr., Wendy Jacobs, and Ellen W. Reckhow discussed distinguishing a community-submitted resolution supporting local food workers from a broader BOCC resolution endorsing the federal Fair Minimum Wage Act. Jacobs noted Durham County already pays its own employees a livable wage despite state General Assembly limits on contractor wage mandates, and the Board agreed to review the revised food-workers resolution with its sponsors for February 10 and prepare the Fair Minimum Wage Act resolution for February 24.

agenda_items.title: Item 8: Proposed 2014 Bond Financing and 2007 GO Bond Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO George Quick and Debt Manager Jessica Brown-Linton briefed the Board on the 2007 $207 million GO bond referendum ($52 million of $91 million outstanding, leaving ~$39 million mostly for schools), explaining how a $60 million Bank of America variable-rate BANs line at 0.65% saved substantially compared to 3–3.5% fixed debt ahead of upcoming refunding bonds. Commissioners asked staff to obtain written confirmation from Durham Tech regarding its planned use of ~$5.9 million in remaining bond funds and its northern campus plan before returning with a financing resolution on February 24.

agenda_items.title: Old Social Services Building Update, Rescheduling of Closed Session, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly referenced an upcoming worksession update on options for the old Social Services building and proposed plaza. To accommodate Chair Michael D. Page's schedule, the Board agreed to reschedule its postponed closed session to Wednesday from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. and adjourned.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 27, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton—with Chair Michael D. Page excused absent and the remaining four commissioners (Howerton, Fred Foster Jr., Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs) present—the Durham Board of County Commissioners held a moment of silence for late former Commissioner Becky Heron and honored Southern High School's 2013 state champion football team and retiring County Manager Mike Ruffin (retiring January 31 after 13 years in Durham and 36 years in local government). In unanimous 4-0 votes, the Board approved the January 6 and January 13 minutes, Consent Agenda Items A–O (excluding pulled Items H, J, and K), pulled Item H (New Hope Preserve trails and bridges), pulled Item K (following an NCDOT secondary-road and maintenance funding briefing by Division 5 Maintenance Engineer Brandon Jones), and pulled Item 7J after closed session. After a closed session on personnel and legal matters, two split 3-1 votes occurred on the interim leadership transition: the Board voted 3-1 to appoint Lee Worsley as Interim County Manager effective February 1, 2014 until a full-time manager begins employment, and voted 3-1 to approve Worsley's employment agreement; on both voice/show-of-hands votes, the transcript recorded three Ayes and one Nay among the four present commissioners (Brenda A. Howerton, Fred Foster Jr., Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs) without naming individual Ayes, Nays, movers, or seconders on microphone.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence for former Commissioner Becky Heron, who passed away the prior week. The Board unanimously voted to excuse Chair Michael D. Page from the meeting and heard announcements on county programming, Twitter Q&A (#AskDCO), and free NCSU/Durham County farmer food-safety workshops.

agenda_items.title: Item 4: Approval of January 6 Work Session and January 13, 2014 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a commissioner confirmed with the Clerk that morning corrections had been incorporated, the Board unanimously approved the minutes of the January 6 Work Session and January 13 Regular Session.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Resolutions Honoring Southern High School Football Champions and Retiring County Manager Mike Ruffin
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adopted ceremonial resolutions honoring Southern High School's Spartans football team and Coach Adrian Jones for their 38-31 comeback win for the 2013 NCHSAA 3AA state championship, and honoring County Manager Mike Ruffin on his January 31, 2014 retirement after leading Durham County since November 2000 (maintaining AAA bond ratings and passing three bond referenda and two sales tax referenda). Ruffin and commissioners exchanged farewell remarks.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–O, Excluding Pulled Items H, J, and K)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item J pulled for consideration after closed session and Items H and K pulled for separate discussion, the Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A–G, I, and L–O.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item H: New Hope Preserve Trails and Pedestrian Bridges
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners took up pulled Consent Item H immediately rather than waiting until after closed session. Following remarks praising the New Hope Preserve parking area, trails, five pedestrian bridges, and use by Forest View Elementary School and Orange and Durham county residents (noting late Commissioner Becky Heron's support), the Board approved Item H unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item K: NCDOT Secondary Road Construction and Maintenance Funding Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NCDOT Division 5 Maintenance Engineer Brandon Jones explained state legislative changes under House Bill 817 that cut statewide secondary road paving construction funds to $12 million and moved remaining dirt roads into a statewide prioritization system, while noting Durham County's primary maintenance budget rose from $728,000 in 2011 to $1.4 million and secondary maintenance rose from $2.3 million to $2.5 million. Following questions, the Board approved Item K unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointment (Public Health Board), Closed Session, Item 7J, and Interim County Manager Votes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk announced James Miller's selection to the Public Health Board, and the Board entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3). Returning at 02:25:26, the Board unanimously approved pulled Consent Item 7J, then voted 3-1 in separate motions to appoint Lee Worsley as Interim County Manager effective February 1, 2014 until a full-time manager begins and to approve Worsley's employment agreement before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its brief January 13, 2014 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened by reporting direction given to staff in an earlier closed session and delivered announcements including the January 15 Martin Luther King Jr. observance program. All formal actions passed unanimously (5-0), with no split or contested votes: the Board approved the December 2 and December 9, 2013 minutes and Consent Agenda Items A, C, D, E, F, G, H, and J (after County Manager Mike Ruffin removed Item B, Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. pulled Item I, and staff answered questions on Item J regarding wastewater industrial inspections and groundwater contamination remediation timelines). Following a public hearing, the Board unanimously approved a 1.84-acre zoning map change at 7460 Wake Forest Highway (Triangle Paintball) downzoning frontage from RS-20 to Rural Residential (RR) in the watershed overlay district to match the remainder of the parcel, while advising a resident concerned about a nearby interstate gas pipeline to bring that unrelated topic to the monthly worksession. On pulled Consent Item I—Budget Ordinance Amendment No. 14BCC000038 regarding accrued compensatory time payouts—Commissioners Foster and Ellen W. Reckhow questioned large accrued leave liabilities and requested a future agenda review of both comp time and management leave policies before approving the amendment 5-0 and adjourning at 7:22 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Closed Session Report, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting by reporting the Board had met in closed session and provided direction to staff. Announcements covered county television shows, board/commission vacancies, and the 9th Annual Durham City-County Martin Luther King Jr. Observance Program scheduled for January 15 at First Presbyterian Church.

agenda_items.title: Item 4: Approval of December 2 Work Session and December 9, 2013 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the December 2, 2013 Work Session and December 9, 2013 Regular Session. On a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Consent Agenda (Items A, C, D, E, F, G, H, and J)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin removed Item B from the agenda and Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. pulled Item I for separate discussion. Before voting, commissioners questioned staff on Item J regarding periodic industrial wastewater inspections and groundwater remediation timelines (referencing West Virginia and Wake County contamination sites) and urged 'time is of the essence' contract language; on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, Items A, C, D, E, F, G, H, and J passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Public Hearing — Zoning Map Change for Triangle Paintball (Z1300027, 7460 Wake Forest Highway)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a rezoning request for a 1.84-acre portion of 7460 Wake Forest Highway (Highway 98) from RS-20 to Rural Residential (RR) within the F/J-A watershed overlay district so the entire property would carry a consistent rural zoning designation ahead of a minor special use permit application to expand paintball operations (recommended 14-0 by the Planning Commission). The applicant's attorney spoke in favor of the downzoning; resident Ms. Crump sought to raise safety concerns about an interstate gas line 20 feet from her home, and Chair Page explained public-hearing rules limited testimony to the paintball rezoning while inviting her to the next first-Monday worksession before the Board approved the rezoning 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 7 (Pulled Consent Item I): Budget Ordinance Amendment No. 14BCC000038 (Accrued Compensatory Time)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. pulled Item I to question how many employees were accruing large compensatory-time balances and what controls could limit mounting county leave liabilities. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted she had asked staff to bring both non-managerial comp time (suggesting annual payouts) and managerial leave policies back for a comprehensive future review; on a motion by Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Reckhow, the Board approved Budget Ordinance Amendment No. 14BCC000038 unanimously and adjourned at 7:22 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 6, 2014 work session, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (4-0) suspended the rules and excused absent Commissioner Wendy Jacobs before observing a moment of silence in memory of her mother. Commissioners heard public comment on the Hill Forest Road bridge and Rougemont water system boundary, received a Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau three-year marketing update, and evaluated options to address the six-month State Bureau of Investigation (SBI) crime lab backlog despite restrictive local lab grant terms. Staff also briefed the Board on the Rougemont water system plan, proposed Village of Rougemont commercial zoning and impervious surface updates, pending November and December board directives, and a potential $300,000–$400,000 mid-year budget impact from Social Services temporary staffing requests. In formal action, the Board unanimously (4-0) suspended the rules and approved the 2014 Federal Legislative Agenda as amended, and unanimously (4-0) entered closed session for attorney-client consultations regarding Jodine Robinson v. Joe Bowser and IBM, providing direction to staff before adjourning with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the work session, apologized for a delayed start, and noted that Commissioner Wendy Jacobs was traveling following the passing of her mother during the holidays. The Board suspended its rules and formally excused Commissioner Jacobs from the meeting, then observed a moment of silence in memory of her mother.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Rougemont Bridge and Water System Boundary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Rougemont resident John Minigurr thanked the Board for rebuilding the bridge on Hill Forest Road. He also expressed satisfaction with the Rougemont water system map and asked for confirmation that the drawn boundary represents 250 feet from the center of contamination, which staff confirmed they were verifying with GIS staff as accurate.

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau (DCVB) Annual Report and Three-Year Marketing Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A DCVB presenter (Shelley) reviewed the organization's statutory origin under 1986 enabling legislation and interlocal agreements, emphasizing that DCVB is funded by one-third of hotel occupancy tax revenues rather than property taxes. She reported that Durham visitors spent roughly $842 million and generated $44 million in local government tax revenue under the prior day-trip strategy, and outlined a new three-year marketing plan targeting four leisure segments while noting Durham's marketing budget lags behind Raleigh, Greensboro, Cabarrus County, and Currituck County.

agenda_items.title: SBI Crime Lab Backlog and Local Toxicology/Drug Lab Grant Evaluation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff discussed the North Carolina SBI crime lab turnaround backlog exceeding six months, which prolongs jail stays and pulls analysts away from lab work for court travel from Raleigh to Durham. Staff explained that a proposed grant to host a local lab would only cover blood alcohol testing equipment and one year of personnel costs—excluding blood drug testing and drug identification—leaving the County to absorb ongoing personnel costs in year two, while commissioners also queried potential FBI agreement terms and termination options.

agenda_items.title: Rougemont Water System Plan and Village of Rougemont Plan Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined a simple system plan covering policies for the Rougemont water system and previewed Village of Rougemont Plan Updates slated for February Planning Commission review. The plan amendment shifts commercial zoning eligibility along Red Mountain Road toward major crossroads along US 15-501 so property owners can request rezoning, and increases allowable impervious surface limits within the Village of Rougemont boundary in the Falls Lake five-mile watershed zone.

agenda_items.title: 2014 Federal Legislative Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to suspend the rules in order to act on the 2014 Federal Legislative Agenda during the work session. Commissioners then voted to approve moving ahead with the 2014 Federal Legislative Agenda as amended and thanked staff member Deborah for her work.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-0 (suspend rules); Passed 4-0 (approve agenda as amended)

agenda_items.title: Review of November and December Board Directives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Dionne Hines reviewed the November and December Board of County Commissioners directives. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested follow-up on a peer-county contingency best-practices item regarding lowering contingency from 10 to 6 percent that was marked complete without her seeing the email, and commissioners checked on pending items involving an adjacent building inquiry and Northern Durham park-and-ride lot expansion.

agenda_items.title: Budget Retreat Scheduling and County Manager Transition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed scheduling the annual February budget retreat, with the County Manager noting that timing is complicated by the Board's ongoing selection of a new manager. Chair Michael D. Page noted upcoming committee adjustments and asked for two weeks following the holidays to review schedules and prepare budget background.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Privilege Consultations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Jodine Robinson v. Joe Bowser, an additional privileged legal matter, and the matter of IBM. Upon returning to open session at 03:23:12, the Chair reported that the Board had provided direction to staff.

agenda_items.title: Social Services Temporary Staffing Request and Special Meeting Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed scheduling a special meeting with Social Services leadership, weighing mid-January dates versus January 27 to ensure staff can compile detailed cost data first. Staff cautioned that Social Services is expected to request approximately 30 to 35 eight-month temporary positions, which could impose a $300,000–$400,000 county share mid-year and carry directly into the next fiscal year's baseline budget.

votes.notes: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs was absent/excused; unanimous 4-0 voice vote among seated members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Michael D. Page requested a motion to suspend the rules prior to voting on excusing Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, who was absent on travel.

votes.notes: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs was absent; unanimous 4-0 voice vote among present members.

votes.notes: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs was absent; unanimous 4-0 voice vote among present members.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to proceed with the 2014 Federal Legislative Agenda as amended, seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 9, 2013 regular session—his first regular meeting presiding as Chair—Chair Michael D. Page welcomed an added presentation from the Eno River Association, recognized Durham County Librarian Lynn Richardson, Hillside High School Principal Dr. William Logan, and the Durham County Engineering and Environmental Services Department Utility Division, and oversaw routine minutes and consent approvals (5-0). On two consent items pulled for separate discussion, the Board split 4-1 twice: budget amendment 14 BCC 0031 appropriating $1,000 from a Walmart Foundation grant for the Sheriff's Project Lifesaver program passed 4-1 with Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye and Fred Foster Jr. voting Nay, and budget amendment 14 BCC 0032 appropriating $50,859 from the Bahama Fire Tax special revenue fund balance for a 2004 Bahama Volunteer Fire Department brush truck chassis replacement passed 4-1 with Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye and Fred Foster Jr. voting Nay. Foster argued against continuing to repair an aging 2004 fire truck rather than purchasing a new vehicle based on a life-expectancy study, while Reckhow urged developing a unified capital improvement plan across all volunteer fire departments. The Board also completed ballot appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee and unanimously (5-0) entered closed session for economic development and personnel matters before returning to report staff direction and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Eno River Association Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page called the meeting to order, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and added an annual December presentation from the Eno River Association. Executive Director Robin Jacobs introduced newly elected board president Barbara Driscoll, thanked the Board for supporting land protection and the Eno festival, and distributed the association's 2014 geocaching calendar.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of Minutes (Nov. 4 & Nov. 11, 2013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County announcements highlighted Durham County TV programming, the FY 2014-15 nonprofit funding pre-application deadline of December 19, 2013, and health initiatives. The Board unanimously approved the minutes from the November 4, 2013 work session and November 11, 2013 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Lynn Richardson (Historical Society of North Carolina)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored Durham County Library North Carolina Collection head Lynn Richardson upon her induction into the Historical Society of North Carolina. The Board highlighted her leadership since 2001, including chairing the Durham Civil Rights Heritage Project and curating exhibits for the County Administration Building and Courthouse.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Engineering & Environmental Services Utility Division
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Taken out of order prior to item 6, the Board recognized County Engineer Glenn Whisler, Utility Division Manager Joe Pearce, and staff for winning the 2013 NC AWWA-WEA Collection System of the Year award for systems of its size.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Dr. William Logan (Wells Fargo Principal of the Year)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Hillside High School Principal Dr. William Logan for being named Durham Public Schools Wells Fargo Principal of the Year, praising his career progression from English teacher to school leader alongside Superintendent Dr. Eric Becoats/Keys.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–O and R–U) and Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow pulled consent items P and Q for separate discussion, and the Board unanimously approved items A through O and R through U. Commissioners then voted by paper ballot to appoint Krista Gatson, Harvey Kirby, and Dolores McNair to three seats on the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (Consent A–O, R–U); Ballot appointments completed

agenda_items.title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 14 BCC 0031: Walmart Foundation Grant for Project Lifesaver
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed budget amendment 14 BCC 0031 appropriating $1,000 in Walmart Foundation grant funds for the Sheriff's Office Project Lifesaver program with Sheriff's PIO Paul Sherwin and Finance Officer Kim Franklin. After discussion and confirming program information was posted on the Sheriff's Office website, the Board approved the amendment 4-1 over Commissioner Fred Foster Jr.'s opposition.

agenda_items.title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 14 BCC 0032: Bahama VFD Brush Truck Chassis Replacement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered a $50,859 budget amendment from the Bahama Fire Tax special revenue fund balance to replace the chassis on a 2004 Bahama Volunteer Fire Department brush truck. Commissioner Fred Foster Jr. objected to spending over $50,000 repairing an older vehicle instead of buying a new ~$100,000 truck based on a long-range cost study, while staff explained the truck body lasts 20–25 years across two chassis and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow urged a unified VFD capital improvement plan; the item passed 4-1.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development & Personnel) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following introduction of Interim Fire Marshal Mark, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for business location/expansion and 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel matters. Upon returning to open session at 02:51:37, the Chair reported that staff had been given direction, and the Board adjourned unanimously.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Bahama Volunteer Fire Department $50,859 Brush Truck Chassis Replacement (Item Q)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over spending $50,859 from the Bahama Fire Tax fund balance to replace the chassis on a 2004 brush truck rather than purchasing a new vehicle.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $50,859 chassis replacement while pursuing a unified VFD capital improvement plan.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners should defer to fire department fleet expertise on apparatus maintenance.
Fire staff testified the truck body lasts 20–25 years while a chassis lasts 9–12 years, making a two-chassis lifecycle cost-effective compared to ~$100,000 for a new brush truck.

disagreements.side_b_position: Buy a new vehicle instead of repairing a 2004 brush truck.
side_b_arguments: Fred Foster Jr. argued the 2004 truck had passed its expected service life and spending $50,859 on a chassis without a long-range cost-comparison study risked 'buying more trouble' for taxpayers.
disagreements.resolution: Budget ordinance amendment 14 BCC 0032 passed 4-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 2, 2013 work session, the Board held its annual leadership reorganization under N.C.G.S. 153A-39, electing Michael D. Page as Chair in a 4-1 voice vote on a nomination by Wendy Jacobs (the individual nay voter was not identified by name in the audio transcript) and unanimously (5-0) electing Brenda A. Howerton as Vice Chair on a nomination by Ellen W. Reckhow. The Board suspended its rules and voted unanimously (5-0) to approve public official bonds, recognize NC DHHS Public Health Education funding via budget ordinance amendment 14 BCC 000029, and adopt capital project amendment 14 CPA 0006 for Durham Public Schools 2007 General Obligation Bond projects. Commissioners also received an annual bus and rail update from Triangle Transit's David King on the Durham-Orange light rail NEPA environmental timeline, and suspended the rules to unanimously (5-0) adopt a resolution for the Institutional Commute Trip Reduction (CTR) program and approve Durham County's local priority project list for NCDOT Prioritization 3.0 (FY 2016–2022 TIP). Finally, the Board unanimously (5-0) entered closed session for attorney-client consultations on pending litigation—including Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser and Orbitz LLC v. Gray—and reported back in open session that it had agreed with counsel to settle the Orbitz matter before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Annual Election of Chair and Vice Chair and Approval of Public Official Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 153A-39, the County Attorney presided over the nomination for Chair; Wendy Jacobs nominated Michael D. Page, who was elected 4-1 by voice vote. Chair Page then presided over the unanimous 5-0 election of Brenda A. Howerton as Vice Chair (nominated by Ellen W. Reckhow), and the Board suspended the rules and unanimously approved public official bonds.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Chair Passed 4-1; Vice Chair Passed 5-0; Bonds Passed 5-0

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments (Transit Connections and Social Services)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three speakers addressed the Board, including comments urging regional transit connections linking Pittsboro and a proposed research technology park to Research Triangle Park, remarks from Scott Harmon on innovative approaches, and comedic commentary from John Tarantino. Staff and Social Services representatives also thanked the Board for support benefiting clients.

agenda_items.title: Budget Ordinance Amendment 14 BCC 000029: NC DHHS Public Health Funds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Public Health Director Gayle Harris present, the Board waived discussion and unanimously suspended the rules to act during a work session. Commissioners then unanimously approved budget ordinance amendment 14 BCC 000029 recognizing state Division of Public Health funds for the Health Education Division.

agenda_items.title: Capital Project Amendment 14 CPA 0006: DPS 2007 General Obligation Bond Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting the item was straightforward, the Board unanimously suspended the rules and approved capital project amendment 14 CPA 0006 adjusting project budgets under the Durham Public Schools 2007 General Obligation Bond.

agenda_items.title: Annual Bus and Rail Transit Update (Triangle Transit)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Taken ahead of items 6 and 7 to accommodate scheduling, Triangle Transit General Manager David King provided the annual update required under the half-cent sales tax transit plan. He detailed expanded bus service linking Durham and Chapel Hill and outlined plans to submit a request to the FTA within 30 days to enter formal two-year project development and NEPA environmental review for light rail along 15-501, Irwin Road, and the NCRR corridor.

agenda_items.title: Institutional Commute Trip Reduction (CTR) Program Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a presentation on simplifying employer reporting for the Commute Trip Reduction program and outreach to volunteer employers, the Board suspended the rules unanimously. Commissioners then approved the resolution supporting the Institutional Commute Trip Reduction program 5-0 while requesting staff follow-up on commissioner comments.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Local Priority List for NCDOT Prioritization 3.0 (FY 2016–2022 TIP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation planner Ellen presented the county's local priority project list for submission to the MPO and NCDOT under the Strategic Transportation Investments Prioritization 3.0 process. She explained a proposed swap removing three fiscally unconstrained projects not in the 2040 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (including a Briggs Avenue extension from Riddle Road to So-Hi Drive) in favor of higher-priority corridor projects; the Board suspended the rules and approved the priority list unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege: Robinson v. Bowser & Orbitz LLC v. Gray)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultations regarding Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser, an additional privileged matter, and Orbitz LLC v. Gray (COA No. 13-918). Upon returning to open session at 03:59:05, Chair Page announced that the Board agreed with legal counsel to settle the Orbitz matter, and the Board adjourned unanimously.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 11, 2013 regular session, Chair Fred Foster Jr. led a Veterans Day tribute honoring Durham County's nearly 17,000 veterans and read the Board's Veterans Day 2013 proclamation. The Board unanimously (5-0) approved prior minutes, adopted the unpulled Consent Agenda items (8A, 8B, 8D, 8E, and 8G), and approved Major Site Plan D1300230 (Project Joshua) for a 27,000-square-foot data center in Treyburn Corporate Park. Commissioners also unanimously (5-0) adopted Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment TC1100007 removing discretionary administrative regulations in favor of objective standards or quasi-judicial review after Planning staff and the InterNeighborhood Council agreed on a future technical-amendment follow-up schedule, approved the 2014 meeting calendar (Item 8C), and approved Item 8F after amending its construction contingency down from 10% to 6% and directing staff to gather peer-county benchmarks. No split or contested votes occurred, and the Board also voted 5-0 to excuse Michael D. Page from the November 25 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance with Veterans, Announcements, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Veterans joined the Board to lead the Pledge of Allegiance, followed by announcements regarding Time Warner Cable channel DTV8/97.5 transition, board/commission vacancies, and diabetes programming. Commissioners unanimously approved the October 7 work session and October 28 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Veterans Day 2013 Proclamation and Staff Honors
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. read the Veterans Day 2013 proclamation honoring the nearly 17,000 veterans residing in Durham County. Remarks also highlighted morning Veterans Day ceremonies, a Durham County EMS/tactical team's first-place competition finish, and an upcoming November 23 family celebration at the Human Services complex.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 8A, 8B, 8D, 8E, and 8G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled items 8C and 8F for separate discussion and unanimously approved the remaining consent items (8A, 8B, 8D, 8E, and 8G).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Major Site Plan D1300230 (Project Joshua Data Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Patrick Young presented Major Site Plan D1300230 requested by Kimley-Horn & Associates on behalf of Treyburn Corporate Park for an approximately 27,000-square-foot data center on International Drive zoned Industrial Light (IL) within the Falls Lake watershed. Noting the Development Review Board recommended approval 7-0 on September 6, 2013, the Board held and closed the public hearing with no speakers and unanimously approved the site plan.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1100007 (Removal of Discretionary Regulations)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC1100007 to replace discretionary administrative site-plan provisions in the Unified Development Ordinance with objective standards or quasi-judicial review per state statute, noting City Council adopted it in March 2013 and the BOCC had deferred it in April 2013 following InterNeighborhood Council (INC) and BPAC feedback. Tom Miller spoke on behalf of INC in support after reaching agreement with staff on post-January technical adjustments, and Wendy Jacobs confirmed advisory boards (DOST/BPAC) would continue submitting review comments included in staff reports before the Board voted 5-0 to approve.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 8C: Proposed 2014 Board of County Commissioners Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noted that the proposed April 14, 2014 regular session falls during Durham Public Schools spring break and Easter Monday, making her unavailable. After brief discussion, the Board unanimously approved the calendar.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 8F: Capital Project Contingency Reduction (10% to 6%) & Elevator Vendor Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned using a 10% construction contingency factor and raised concerns about avoiding sole-source lock-in on elevator maintenance contracts, noting the County works with three elevator firms. The County Manager concurred with reducing the contingency to 6% and agreed to survey peer counties and report back; the Board approved the item as amended 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Commissioner Page (Nov. 25), Plaza Public Meeting Reminder, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 5-0 to excuse Commissioner Michael D. Page from the November 25 meeting. Commissioners also reminded the public of a November 12, 6:00 p.m. meeting at the Human Services auditorium regarding plaza plans before adjourning unanimously.

votes.notes: Carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Routine minutes approval.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 4, 2013 work session, the Board heard extensive citizen comments on open data initiatives (Code for America / GovLoop), foreclosure and criminal record expungement clinics (including Legal Aid requests and 'Ban-the-Box' hiring practices), and fast-food workers' advocacy for a $15/hour wage and unionization resolution—which commissioners tabled for staff review in light of North Carolina General Assembly restrictions on local contractor living-wage mandates. The Board unanimously (5-0) suspended the rules and approved prior minutes, temporarily tabled the removal of an appointee (Wayne Allbrook) for legal research, and conducted a detailed work-session review of the Board's Rules of Procedure and advisory board appointment policies. In formal action at the end of the session, commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) on two separate motions to enter closed session for attorney-client privilege regarding online travel company tax litigation (Orbitz, Travelocity, Hotels.com, Priceline) and Pennex/Pin-ex v. Durham County, returning with no action taken and adjourning with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Open Data, Reentry/Expungement Clinics, and $15 Fast-Food Wage Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Andrew Krzmarzick (GovLoop / Code for America Brigade) advocated for open public data sets, while reentry and Legal Aid advocates urged support for mobile expungement clinics and 'Ban-the-Box' employment policies. Fast-food worker organizer Keith Bullard requested a Board resolution supporting $15/hour wages and union rights; Michael D. Page noted the County's ~$12 living wage and recent state legislation barring contractor wage mandates, Wendy Jacobs voiced support for worker advocacy, and the Board tabled the resolution request for staff legal review.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously suspended its rules to take action during the work session and unanimously approved the minutes listed under the agenda item.

agenda_items.title: Removal of Board Member Due to Poor Attendance (Wayne Allbrook)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney reported that new information regarding Wayne Allbrook's attendance had just become available and requested time for quick research. The Board agreed to temporarily table the item.

agenda_items.title: Review of Board Rules of Procedure and Advisory Board Appointment Policies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following mid-session items omitted in transcript truncation, commissioners reviewed draft updates to the Board's Rules of Procedure and appointment rules. Discussions covered defining 'timely request' for agenda items (proposed 2 working days), creating an alert sheet for late agenda additions/deletions after Wednesday iPad uploads, limiting individual commissioner board assignments (Reckhow noted serving on eight boards), targeting a 7-day appointment packet turnaround and shortening 90-day re-advertising periods, clarifying the statutory duty to vote under which non-votes count as affirmative, and rules for staff attendance in closed session.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege: Online Travel Companies & Pin-ex v. Durham County)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board passed two unanimous 5-0 motions under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Orbitz/Travelocity/Hotels.com/Priceline litigation (v. David Hore et al.) and Pin-ex v. Durham County. Upon returning to open session at 07:52:57, the Board reported no action was taken and adjourned unanimously.

votes.notes: Carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural motion to approve minutes at work session.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (Item 7 / 1-8)
votes.notes: Carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Routine approval of minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Online Travel Companies / Orbitz et al. Litigation)
votes.notes: Carried unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding Travelocity.com LP, Hotels.com LP, Priceline/Orbitz litigation.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Pin-ex v. Durham County)
votes.notes: Carried 5-0; no action taken upon return.
votes.discussion_detail: Second closed-session motion under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with counsel regarding Pin-ex v. Durham County.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 28, 2013 regular session, the Board unanimously (5-0) approved the October 14 regular session minutes and Consent Agenda items 6A through 6I, and recognized Library Director Tammy Baggett for receiving the 2013 Roadbuilders Award from the North Carolina Library Association Roundtable for Ethnic Minority Concerns. Commissioners held two required public hearings: one on a $600,000 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) infrastructure application to build a community well and water distribution system for groundwater-contaminated homes in Rougemont, and a second on allocating $900,000 in economic development investment funds to AW North Carolina. Following strong support from the Chamber of Commerce and commissioners praising AW North Carolina's $112 million Treyburn Corporate Park expansion and 56 new machine-operator jobs, the Board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the $900,000 incentive. Finally, commissioners elected Sandra Chambers and Henry Felder by ballot to the Library Board of Trustees before adjourning unanimously with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of October 14, 2013 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. called the meeting to order, followed by announcements on Time Warner Cable channel DTV8/97.5 free digital adapter boxes (available through December), board/commission recruitment, and Living Healthy programming. The Board unanimously approved the October 14, 2013 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Tammy Baggett (2013 NCLA Roadbuilders Award)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton introduced Library Director Tammy Baggett, who received the 2013 Roadbuilders Award from the NCLA Roundtable for Ethnic Minority Concerns at the 60th NCLA biennial conference. Commissioners Reckhow, Jacobs, and Howerton praised Baggett's leadership and library staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A–6I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the consent agenda, and the Board unanimously approved items 6A through 6I.

agenda_items.title: Required Public Hearing: CDBG Funds Application for Rougemont Community Water System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Drew Cummings briefed the Board on the $600,000 CDBG infrastructure grant application to help build a community well and distribution system addressing groundwater pollution in Rougemont in northern Durham County, noting an engineering/design RFQ and system policies were forthcoming. The public hearing opened and closed with no speakers, and staff confirmed standard legal notice had been provided.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $900,000 Economic Development Investment Funds for AW North Carolina
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton presented a proposed $900,000 economic development incentive for AW North Carolina (an Aisin AW subsidiary established in Durham in 1998) to support a $112 million capital investment and 56 new full-time machine operator jobs at its 820,000-square-foot Treyburn Corporate Park plant amid competition from sites in NC, Georgia, Tennessee, and Mexico. Chamber of Commerce VP Ted Connor and supporters highlighted the company's 2,000 employees and $612 million cumulative investment; commissioners praised AW North Carolina's partnership with Durham Tech and Holton Career Center and approved the incentive 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments (Library Board of Trustees) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voted by written ballot to fill two seats on the Library Board of Trustees, electing Sandra Chambers and Henry Felder. With no further business, the Board adjourned 5-0.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (October 14, 2013 Regular Session)
votes.notes: Carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Routine minutes approval.

votes.item_title: Allocation of $900,000 Economic Development Investment Funds to AW North Carolina
votes.notes: Carried 5-0 after public hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: Supports AW North Carolina's $112 million manufacturing expansion and 56 new jobs in Treyburn Corporate Park.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 14, 2013 regular session, the Board emerged from closed session with no action taken, approved the September 23 regular session minutes (5-0), and celebrated the openings of the southern segment of the American Tobacco Trail and the downtown History Hub. Commissioners recognized Public Health Nurse Shirley Stock as Employee of the Year at the Refugee Health Conference and adopted ceremonial resolutions honoring Catherine Spearman Farrell on her 101st birthday and the Extension and Community Association on its centennial. On Item 11, commissioners unanimously (5-0)—with Ellen W. Reckhow 'reluctantly' seconding—amended the County's living wage policy as compelled by a new North Carolina General Assembly prohibition on local contractor wage mandates, while maintaining the policy for direct County employees and directing staff to survey and encourage voluntary subcontractor compliance. Finally, following a briefing from Social Services Director Michael Becketts on severe risks to childcare subsidies, Work First, and food assistance during the federal government shutdown, the Board voted 5-0 to authorize up to $235,000 in budget amendment authority if needed to sustain County operations.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements (ATT & History Hub Openings), and Sept. 23 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. reported no action from closed session and opened the meeting; Wendy Jacobs announced free screenings of the Alzheimer's documentary 'Alive Inside,' and Ellen W. Reckhow highlighted the Saturday openings of the final southern segment of the American Tobacco Trail and the History Hub. Commissioners approved the September 23, 2013 regular session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions and Resolutions: Shirley Stock, Catherine Spearman Farrell (101st Birthday), and ECA Centennial
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Gail Harris presented Immunization Clinic Nurse Shirley Stock, named Public Health Employee of the Year for serving Durham's growing refugee population. The Board also read resolutions honoring civic leader Catherine Spearman Farrell on her 101st birthday and celebrating the 100th anniversary of the North Carolina Extension and Community Association (ECA).

agenda_items.title: Living Wage Policy Revision Following State Preemption Statute
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following mid-meeting items omitted in transcript truncation, commissioners expressed dismay at a new General Assembly law prohibiting local governments from enforcing living wage requirements on service contractors. Staff confirmed existing County employees (including part-time workers) would remain covered without losing pay, and commissioners directed staff to notify subcontractors that the change was state-mandated, encourage voluntary compliance, and survey practices before voting 5-0 (reluctantly seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow) to approve the required revision.

agenda_items.title: Impact of Federal Government Shutdown on DSS Programs (Budget Authority up to $235,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS Director Michael Becketts and County Manager Mike Ruffin briefed the Board on federal shutdown impacts threatening childcare subsidies (~$55,000/day or >$1 million/month, affecting working families, Durham Tech students, and at least 25 DSS employees), Work First cash benefits, and food stamps alongside the NC FAST transition. Commissioners discussed engaging major employers, foundations, and HR support for county staff, and voted 5-0 to authorize a budget amendment up to $235,000 if operating budgets could not absorb emergency needs.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (September 23, 2013 Regular Session)
votes.notes: Carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Routine minutes approval.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Living Wage Policy Compliance Revision (Rescinding Contractor Mandate per State Law)
votes.notes: Ellen W. Reckhow stated 'I'll reluctantly second it' in protest of the state mandate; carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioners objected to the General Assembly's preemption of local contractor living-wage rules, retained the policy for County employees, and directed staff to notify subcontractors and survey compliance.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Authorization for Up to $235,000 Budget Amendment for Federal Shutdown DSS Impacts
votes.notes: Carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorizes Manager to bring forward a budget amendment up to $235,000 if needed to address federal shutdown disruptions to DSS programs.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 7, 2013 work session, the Board heard public comments proposing an alternative middle-corridor alignment for the Durham-Orange Light Rail NEPA study, advocating SBIRT substance-abuse screening, urging an early affordable-housing anti-displacement inventory around transit stations, and addressing Office on Youth staffing. Commissioners received an NCACC introductory video and a progress report from Made in Durham on connecting all Durham youth to post-secondary credentials and living-wage careers by age 25, while deferring the nonprofit funding process review to the November work session. In formal action, the Board suspended the rules and voted unanimously (5-0) to approve a 96-gallon curbside recycling roll-out cart pilot covering approximately 759 households in the 27514 and 27714 zip codes within existing solid waste funds, suspended the rules (5-0) to conduct a ballot board reappointment, and entered closed session (5-0) under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel matters before adjourning with no action taken and no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Light Rail Alignment, Affordable Housing Inventory, SBIRT, and Office on Youth
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Five speakers addressed the Board: a transportation engineer proposed an alternative Durham-Orange light rail alignment claiming $300–$400 million in savings and fewer grade crossings/eminent domain takings; another speaker urged an early affordable-housing inventory to prevent resident displacement near light rail stations; other speakers addressed SBIRT treatment screening, Salvation Army holiday aid (noting 500 of 700 applications from Latino families), and staffing for the Office on Youth.

agenda_items.title: NCACC President Introductory Video and Risk Management Pools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board viewed an introductory video from Person County Vice Chair Ray Jeffers, incoming President of the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners, highlighting NCACC advocacy and county workers' compensation, liability, and property insurance pools.

agenda_items.title: Made in Durham Progress Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: David Dotson, Julie Mooney, and Kay Stratton briefed commissioners on Made in Durham, a community partnership engaging major employers, Durham Public Schools, Durham Tech, County officials, and Alliance Behavioral Health to ensure all Durham youth obtain a post-secondary credential and living-wage career connection by age 25, including ongoing fiscal mapping.

agenda_items.title: Curbside Recycling 96-Gallon Roll-Out Cart Pilot Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following mid-session items omitted in transcript truncation, solid waste staff presented a pilot to replace 18-gallon bins with 96-gallon wheeled roll-out carts for roughly 759 unincorporated households in the 27514/27714 zip codes (Massey Chapel/Herndon Road area) using existing budget funds, aiming to evaluate participation and contamination before any FY15 expansion to all 9,000 subscribers. Commissioners clarified GIS boundary anomalies and prior $17,672 recycling revenue, then suspended the rules and approved the pilot 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Nonprofit Funding Process Deferral and Board Reappointment Ballot
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff postponed the nonprofit funding process review to the November work session due to time constraints, opting to gather initial feedback in individual briefings. The Board then suspended the rules 5-0 to distribute a ballot for a board reappointment.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a 15-minute recess, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications/employment. Commissioners returned at 07:45:33 with no action taken and adjourned 5-0.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton excused absent, the four present commissioners—Chair Fred Foster Jr., Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs—approved all actions unanimously (4-0) at the September 23, 2013 regular session. The Board voted 4-0 to add Item 11 on Ellen W. Reckhow's request, later voting 4-0 to direct the County Manager to write to Governor Pat McCrory, the DENR Secretary, and the local legislative delegation protesting North Carolina's rejection of an EPA baseline surface-water monitoring grant ahead of potential fracking. Commissioners also voted 4-0 to approve prior minutes, adopt Consent Agenda items 6A–6G, authorize submission of the $242,000 FY14 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) transit grant application, and transfer a federal Section 179D energy-efficiency tax deduction for Administration Building chiller and lighting upgrades to Sud Associates (while urging front-end negotiation of such credits in future contracts). In board appointments, Sean Miller and Tamara Hayward won seats on the Library Board of Trustees while ties for the remaining two seats were carried over, and the Board entered closed session (4-0) for legal consultations including Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser before adjourning with no action taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment (Fracking Baseline Water Testing), and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. opened the meeting, and the Board voted 4-0 to add Ellen W. Reckhow's requested discussion on baseline surface-water testing ahead of fracking as Item 11. Announcements covered Durham Open Space and Trails FY13-14 matching grants (due November 4) and Michael D. Page's report on the Bull City Stand Down veterans event.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Aug. 26 & Sept. 9, 2013 Regular Sessions) and American Cancer Society Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 4-0 to approve the August 26 and September 9, 2013 regular session minutes. Eric Hayden of the American Cancer Society then briefed commissioners on Cancer Prevention Study-3 (targeting 350 enrollments across Durham and Orange counties) and Relay for Life of Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A–6G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled and Chair Foster noting Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's excused absence for the record, the Board unanimously (4-0) approved Consent Agenda items 6A through 6G.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY14 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) Grant Application ($242,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Program Manager Margaret Skelly and Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers presented the annual $242,000 NCDOT ROAP grant application, comprising $130,000 for elderly and disabled transportation (no local match), $31,000 for employment transportation (no local match), and rural general public transit (10% local match funded by fares). With no public speakers, the Board approved submitting the grant application 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Allocation of Federal 179D Energy-Efficient Commercial Building Tax Deduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested approval to allocate the federal Section 179D tax deduction for the Administration Building chiller and lighting efficiency upgrades to engineering designer Sud Associates, noting the tax-exempt County cannot use the deduction and incurs no administrative cost. Commissioners expressed concern that tax-paying design firms benefit from taxpayer-funded upgrades without sharing savings, urged staff to factor 179D credits into future contract negotiations up front, and approved the transfer 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Letter Regarding State Rejection of EPA Baseline Water Quality Monitoring Grant Ahead of Fracking
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ellen W. Reckhow reported that North Carolina declined an EPA research grant that would have funded DENR baseline surface-water monitoring in the shale basin south of Durham ahead of fracking, contrary to recommendations in DENR's 2012 report. The Board voted 4-0 directing the County Manager to send a letter to the Governor, copied to the DENR Secretary and local delegation, expressing concern and urging reconsideration.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Board Appointments (Library Board of Trustees & Industrial Facilities Discussion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners raised questions about incumbent designations on the Industrial Facilities board and discussed Library Board of Trustees recommendations for incumbent reappointments. Ballot voting selected Sean Miller and Tamara Hayward for two of the four open Library Board seats, while repeated ties for the remaining two seats were carried over.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 9, 2013 regular session, the Board heard public comments on jail death reporting and food stamp access, recognized the Department of Public Health's 100th anniversary and Minority Enterprise Development Week, and signed a joint resolution urging Governor Pat McCrory and the North Carolina General Assembly to expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act (noting roughly 18% of Durham County residents were uninsured). Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved Consent Agenda items 11A–11C (after removing 11D) and, following a public hearing, voted 5-0 to allocate up to $1 million over seven years in economic development investment funds to Purdue Pharma Manufacturing LP for a $59 million, 100-job pharmaceutical facility in Treyburn Corporate Park. After a closed session for personnel and legal consultations including Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser, the Board returned to open session and voted unanimously (5-0) to grant a 4.25% raise to the Register of Deeds and excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from the September 23 regular session before adjourning with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements (DSS Relocation & Matching Grants), and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. opened the meeting; announcements noted Open Space and Trails matching grants and the upcoming relocation of all Social Services offices to the new Human Services building at 415 E. Main St., while Item 4 (Minutes) was removed until September 23. During citizen comments, activist Victoria Peterson sought Sheriff's Office/jail death reporting and staffing, and another speaker raised food-stamp delays affecting diabetic residents.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Department of Public Health Centennial Anniversary (1913–2013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read a proclamation honoring the 100th anniversary of the Durham Department of Public Health, originally formed in 1913 after a 1912 smallpox epidemic. Health Director Gail Harris thanked the Board for sustained county investment above state minimums.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Urging North Carolina General Assembly and Governor to Expand Medicaid
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a resolution signed by all five commissioners urging Governor Pat McCrory, House Speaker Thom Tillis, Senate President Pro Tem Phil Berger, and the Durham delegation to accept federal ACA funds to expand Medicaid below 138% FPL, citing 18% county uninsurance, 500,000+ eligible North Carolinians, and $65 million in projected 10-year state savings. Health Director Gail Harris, DSS Director Michael Becketts, and Project Access Executive Director Sally Wilson discussed October–March ACA outreach plans, and Ellen W. Reckhow suggested copying the NC DHHS Secretary.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Minority Enterprise Development (MED) Week (Oct. 7–11, 2013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. proclaimed October 7–11, 2013 as Minority Enterprise Development Week in Durham County, highlighting county support for minority- and women-owned small businesses alongside Ms. Gales.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 11A–11C)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item 11D removed, the Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda items 11A, 11B, and 11C.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $1 Million Economic Development Incentive for Purdue Pharma Manufacturing LP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton presented a seven-year performance incentive of up to $1 million for Purdue Pharma Manufacturing LP's proposed $59 million, 120,000-square-foot oral solid dosage facility creating 100 jobs in Treyburn Corporate Park, competing against two other NC sites and Virginia. Ted Connor (Chamber of Commerce) and Casey Steinbacher spoke in support alongside Purdue representatives and Durham Tech/NCCU BRITE Center partners; commissioners emphasized local workforce hiring and approved the incentive 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Register of Deeds 4.25% Raise, and Excusal of Commissioner Howerton
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) for personnel matters and legal consultation regarding Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser et al. Upon returning to open session at 02:50:03, the Board voted 5-0 to grant the Register of Deeds a 4.25% salary raise and voted 5-0 to excuse Brenda A. Howerton from the September 23 regular session before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 26, 2013 regular session, the Board opened by voting unanimously (5-0) to approve 4.25% raises for appointed officials and department heads—including Clerk to the Board Michelle Parker-Evans, Tax Administrator Kim Simpson, and County Attorney Lowell Siler—before approving prior minutes (5-0) and presenting honors for WWII veteran Jerry M. Smith's 100th birthday, Mary D. Holderness's 25 years leading Project Graduation, and the Department of Public Health's state accreditation. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved Consent Agenda items 11A–Q (excluding pulled items C, L, and R) and, after scrutinizing why a proposed Evergreen Solutions classification and compensation study carried a $200,000 not-to-exceed figure above the $88,500 bid, voted 5-0 to approve the study capped at the $88,500 baseline while committing to implement its findings for employees. After discussing and unanimously (5-0) approving pulled items 11C, 11L (Human Services Complex elevators), and 11R (Northern Durham farmland preservation easements for the Douglas Day and George Tilly farms) and completing ballot appointments to five citizen boards, the Board entered closed session (5-0) and returned to vote 5-0 authorizing a $55,000 expert witness contract for Health and Human Services construction litigation before adjourning with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: 4.25% Raises for Appointed Officials, Call to Order, Announcements, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emerging from a pre-meeting closed session, the Board voted 5-0 to approve 4.25% salary raises for appointed officials/department heads including Clerk to the Board Michelle Parker-Evans, Tax Administrator Kim Simpson, and County Attorney Lowell Siler. Following announcements on the American Cancer Society study enrollment at the Main Library, the Board approved the July 29 and August 5, 2013 minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolutions & Recognitions: Jerry M. Smith (100th Birthday), Mary D. Holderness, and Public Health Accreditation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored World War II Navy Seabees veteran Jerry M. Smith on his 100th birthday, recognized Mary D. Holderness for 25 years leading alcohol- and drug-free Project Graduation celebrations, and received a North Carolina Public Health Accreditation plaque for the Department of Public Health. Subsequent announcements recognized Durham Tech partners and promoted the Bull City Stand Down veterans event.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Unpulled Items 11A–B, 11D–K, 11M–Q)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled consent items 11C, 11L, and 11R for separate review (with a follow-up noted for item 11E). The Board unanimously approved the remaining consent agenda items 5-0.

agenda_items.title: County Classification and Compensation Study (Evergreen Solutions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Human Resources Director Cora Wilson presented the classification and compensation study contract with Evergreen Solutions. Commissioners questioned the gap between Evergreen's $88,500 proposal and the $200,000 not-to-exceed agenda cap, insisted any cost increase return to the Board for approval, and urged commitment to implementing the resulting pay adjustments for employees; the Board voted 5-0 to approve the study capped at the $88,500 baseline.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Board Appointments (Ballot Results)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners completed written ballots and the Clerk announced selections: Jermaine Brewington (Adult Services Oversight Committee), Randall Best (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission), David Lowe (Board of Adjustment), Kimberly Cameron (Women's Commission), and Casey Steinbacher (Workforce Development Board).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 11C, 11L (Human Services Elevators), and 11R (Farmland Easements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Wendy Jacobs noted an outdated September 2 application deadline typo in item 11C, questioned vendor selection for Gen 2 elevators in the Human Services complex (11L), and joined commissioners in questioning appraisal-based pricing for perpetual farmland preservation easements on the 100-year-old Douglas Day and George Tilly farms in Northern Durham funded 50% by federal grants (11R). Satisfied with staff's explanations, the Board approved items 11C, 11L, and 11R 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Closed Session $55,000 Expert Witness Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) for personnel and attorney-client consultations including Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser et al. Returning to open session at 02:26:25, the Board voted 5-0 to authorize the County Attorney to enter into a $55,000 expert witness contract for the Health and Human Services construction project before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 5, 2013 work session (with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs previously excused on June 24), the Durham County Board of Commissioners heard citizen comments from Victoria Peterson regarding natural gas deregulation contacts and a request for Sheriff's Department records on the death of James D. Devon/DeBon on Red Mountain Road. The Board voted unanimously by voice vote (4-0 among the four seated members present: Fred Foster Jr., Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, and Ellen W. Reckhow) to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation, returning with no action taken. Triangle Transit Authority CEO David King then delivered an extended update on the Durham County Transit Plan, detailing bus service expansion plans for FY15 (including the US 15-501 corridor and Northern Durham/Durham Tech campus), commuter rail, and the 17-mile Durham-Orange light rail corridor, along with route alignment trade-offs, federal funding competitiveness, and affordable housing near transit stations. Following a truncated middle portion, staff updated the Board on Year 2 (FY13-14) Strategic Plan initiatives—including tree planting, Leadership Academy, school CPR/AED partnerships, and a joint City-County economic development strategic plan—while commissioners requested timelines for ongoing items, stronger substance abuse prevention focus, and inline answers on the board directives tracker. No split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Natural Gas Deregulation and Sheriff's Investigation Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson asked to be connected with the county staff member handling natural gas purchasing in light of commercial and municipal gas deregulation in North Carolina. She also asked commissioners for assistance obtaining Sheriff's Department records regarding the death of James D. Devon/DeBon on Red Mountain Road, noting a discrepancy between a coroner ruling and an ongoing homicide investigation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Privilege Consultation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the County Attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege. Upon returning to open session at 00:40:07, the Chair reported that no action was taken.

agenda_items.title: Triangle Transit Authority Bus and Rail Investment Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Triangle Transit Authority CEO and General Manager David King updated commissioners on regional transit plan implementation following Orange County's half-cent sales tax referendum approval. Discussion covered FY15 bus planning for the 15-501 corridor, Northern Durham/Durham Tech campus, and AW North Carolina's 1,500-plus workforce, as well as the 17-mile light rail corridor (14 miles in Durham County), route alignment alternatives (Meadowmont/Woodmont and Patterson Place to MLK across New Hope Creek), federal funding cost competitiveness, and statutory and ridership reasons to align affordable housing near stations.

agenda_items.title: FY 2013-14 Strategic Plan Implementation Update (Year 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the work session, staff presented Year 2 (FY13-14) Strategic Plan updates covering website development, tree planting and nutrient-reduction environmental campaigns, the Leadership Academy, hands-only CPR/AED training with Durham Public Schools, and a joint City-County economic development strategic plan involving County Manager Michael Ruffin, Deputy Manager Marqueta Welton, and Durham City Manager Tom Bonfield. Commissioners urged adding substance abuse prevention initiatives, replacing 'ongoing' labels with concrete timelines, including North Carolina Central University in collaborative partnerships, and maintaining focus on workforce and economic development.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Tracking Format and Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner asked staff to place concise one-line factual answers (such as TTA T-Links paratransit trip counts of 5,752 in FY12 or unincorporated household totals) directly in the final column of the directives tracker rather than only noting 'completed answers emailed.' Staff agreed to incorporate that improvement in future updates.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 29, 2013 regular session (with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs previously excused on June 24), the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (4-0) approved meeting minutes and the consent agenda (excluding four pulled items: 5A, 5B, 5L, and 5P). County Manager Michael M. Ruffin formally submitted his retirement letter after 13 years of service, highlighting capital projects and growth in the General Fund balance from $50.5 million to $133.2 million, before the Board voted 4-0 to enter closed session for economic development discussions and later adjourned with no split or contested votes.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) Matching Grants ($41,370) vs. Revenue-Generating and Basic-Needs Priorities
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over approving $41,370 in DOST matching grants for four community park and trail projects (including Horton Grove, Sandy Creek Park, and Briggs Avenue community garden gazebo).
disagreements.side_a_position: Honor the prior fiscal year's budget allocation and citizen committee process by approving the four vetted DOST matching grants totaling $41,370.
side_a_arguments: The County previously budgeted roughly $77,000 for the program and invited citizens and nonprofits to submit elaborate proposals in good faith after a two-year suspension.
Projects like Sandy Creek Park and the Briggs Avenue gazebo reclaim unsafe spaces, make parks handicap-accessible, and support physical fitness and obesity prevention.
Citizens waited until after 10:00 PM to advocate for wholesome, safe community amenities.
disagreements.side_b_position: Questioned dedicating additional funds to open space and trails rather than revenue-producing events or basic food and housing needs.
side_b_arguments: The County had already spent $65,000 on open space and trails earlier in the year (on a voice vote where one commissioner noted not having given a yes voice vote).
Funds could instead support revenue-producing sports tourism such as recruiting an AAU track and field meet (generating $10M+ annually in Greensboro) or addressing food and housing needs.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1 by voice vote; the transcript digest does not explicitly name the four Aye voters or the single Nay voter.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 3, 2013 work session (and combined budget work session), the Board of County Commissioners heard citizen comments from James Chavis criticizing Durham Public Schools' central administration spending relative to classroom teachers, an Appearance Commission representative proposing a unified alphabetical plaque on the 1921 courthouse World War I monument listing all 48 Black and White war heroes together, and Philip Azor urging caution on the Youth Opportunity Initiative while prioritizing mental health access. Long-Term Care Ombudsman Carmelita Karhoff requested increasing the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee from 13 to 15 volunteer positions per state statutory formula, and representatives from the Senior Tar Heel Legislature and Triangle J Council of Governments began a briefing on Community Resource Connections.
