Staff also introduced summer intern Katie Martin and new Assistant to the County Manager Sam Williford and reviewed updated trust fund pages and fund balance trends, with no formal votes taken in the digest.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: DPS Budget, WWI Monument Plaque, and Youth Opportunity Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: James Chavis urged the Board not to accept Durham Public Schools' budget without scrutiny, opposing a central chief administrator hire and single-gender school surplus while teachers split campuses. An Appearance Commission representative presented a May 15 resolution recommending adding a unified alphabetical plaque of all 48 WWI heroes to the 1921 courthouse monument (which commissioners asked staff to bring back at a future work session), and Philip Azor urged waiting on the MDC juvenile justice task force before proceeding with the Youth Opportunity Initiative.

agenda_items.title: Request to Expand Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee Volunteer Positions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Long-Term Care Ombudsman Carmelita Karhoff (Triangle J Area Agency on Aging) requested expanding the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee from 13 to 15 members per state statutory formula based on Durham's 13 adult care homes and ~32 family care homes. Commissioners noted prior difficulty filling vacancies, praised Wendy Jacobs for agreeing to serve as liaison and Ellen W. Reckhow's ongoing support, and suggested adding direct website links on the county and senior center pages.

agenda_items.title: Community Resource Connections (CRCs) Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Tar Heel Legislature delegate Rosalyn Petty Ford and Triangle J Council of Governments representative Joan Pelletier opened a briefing on Community Resource Connections (CRCs) prior to the truncated middle section of the digest.

agenda_items.title: FY 2013-14 Budget Work Session: Durham Technical Community College and Fund Balance Review

Howerton shared a report from a recent benchmarking trip. The Board then approved the April 22, April 11 CIP, April 13 PAC 4, and April 1 work session/nonprofit hearing minutes by voice vote.

Reckhow. Commissioners also asked why Item K board appointments skipped standard ballot voting and requested cost data for joining the City's youth initiative.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 6, 2013 work session, the Board of County Commissioners opened with citizen comments covering long-term care advocacy, Concord Hospitality's proposed downtown hotel at the historic McPherson building, and transit funding transparency. Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee Chair Jeff Goll requested a board liaison—for which Commissioner Wendy Jacobs volunteered—and Trinity Park Neighborhood Association representatives and another speaker discussed Concord Hospitality's proposed $2 million City-County hotel partnership, while James Chavis and another resident urged clearer public education and website reporting on Durham's transit tax revenues. Following a truncated middle segment, Budget Director Pamela Meyer and Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson presented revised FY 2013-14 property tax base estimates ($30.64 billion) and a blended 98.8% collection rate amid delayed implementation of North Carolina's 'Tax and Tag Together' vehicle tax system. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned whether recent real-property base underestimates of roughly $400 million warranted less conservative revenue projections, while staff and another commissioner emphasized caution given $9 million in pending Property Tax Commission appeals and auto-collection uncertainty. Commissioners also reviewed the board directives tracker and adjourned with no formal policy votes or split votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Adult Care Home Liaison, Downtown Hotel Proposal, and Transit Tax Transparency
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Adult Care Home CAC Chair Jeff Goll reported on quarterly facility visits, a donor-funded screening of 'Alive Inside' at the Carolina Theatre, and requested a commissioner liaison (Wendy Jacobs volunteered). Trinity Park Neighborhood Association representatives John Swansea and Julia Borbely-Brown and a subsequent speaker addressed Concord Hospitality's proposed $2 million public-private partnership at the McPherson building, while James Chavis and another speaker debated transit priorities and urged joint City-County public meetings and website clarity on how sales tax and vehicle fee revenues are spent (with commissioners clarifying transit funds cannot legally fund job training).

agenda_items.title: FY 2013-14 Property Tax Base and Revenue Projections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson and Budget Director Pamela Meyer presented a final FY13-14 property tax base estimate of $30,641,144,478 and a blended 98.8% collection rate projection under the Fiscal Control Act during North Carolina's delayed September 1 'Tax and Tag Together' rollout. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted the real property tax base had exceeded adopted estimates by roughly $400 million (~$3 million in revenue or 1 cent on the tax rate) and urged realistic forecasting, while staff and another commissioner defended conservative assumptions to hedge against $9 million in pending Property Tax Commission appeals and vehicle-tax transition uncertainty.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Tracker Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the directives status report, commended staff for clearing completed items, and requested an emailed list of any still-pending directives from the past year before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 22, 2013 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved prior minutes from February 25 and April 8, recognized the General Services Solid Waste Division for winning the Carolina Recycling Association's Spotlight Award for its Recycling Ambassadors Program, and issued proclamations honoring retiring Downtown Durham, Inc. President Bill Kalkhof ('Bill Kalkhof Week') and proclaiming May 6–12, 2013 as Children's Mental Health Awareness Week. Following a truncated middle segment, the Board held a public hearing on a Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendment expanding allowable locations for farmers markets and enabling urban agriculture (previously recommended 12-1 by the Planning Commission and approved by Durham City Council on March 18). After supportive remarks from speakers Kevin Hammock, Peter Schubert, and Kevin McDonough—who urged follow-up work on aquaponics, compost sales, crafts, and parking—and supportive comments from commissioners about using public school lots for weekend markets, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the UDO amendment. Commissioners also approved Item 9 by unanimous voice vote and completed appointments across five boards and commissions, including the Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees, Farmland Protection Advisory Board, and EMS Council, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of Minutes (April 8 and February 25, 2013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Announcements highlighted DSS operating hours changing June 24, the 'Living Healthy' diabetes television series, and an April 23 Coordinated Transportation Program workshop. The Board unanimously approved minutes for the April 8, 2013 and February 25, 2013 regular sessions.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Solid Waste Division Recycling Ambassadors Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Director Motiryo Keambiroiro, supervisor Brian Haynesworth, Chrissy Korb, and Rougemont volunteer Bruce Davis presented the Carolina Recycling Association Spotlight Award earned for the 2012 Recycling Ambassadors community outreach program.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Honoring Retiring Downtown Durham, Inc. President Bill Kalkhof
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. read a proclamation declaring the last week of April 2013 'Bill Kalkhof Week' in recognition of Kalkhof's 20 years leading Downtown Durham, Inc. and over $1.3 billion in downtown revitalization, including American Tobacco, DPAC, and county government investments.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Children's Mental Health Awareness Week (May 6–12, 2013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Michael D. Page read a proclamation designating May 6–12, 2013 as Children's Mental Health Awareness Week, received by Alliance Behavioral Healthcare Executive Director Ellen Hollerman and staff member Tika.

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment: Urban Agriculture and Farmers Markets
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Mike Stock) presented a UDO text amendment expanding farmers market locations and allowing urban agriculture and related food sales by right, noting 12-1 Planning Commission support and March 18 City Council approval while flagging future stakeholder requests on crafts, aquaponics, compost sales, and parking. Speakers Kevin Hammock, Peter Schubert, and Kevin McDonough endorsed the amendment and urged prioritizing follow-up updates, and commissioners praised the grassroots effort and suggested school campuses for weekend farmers markets before adopting the amendment 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 9 Approval and Citizen Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved Item 9 by unanimous voice vote and recognized retiring clerk/staff member Ellen on her final meeting night. The Clerk then announced board and commission appointments for the City-County Appearance Commission, Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees (five seats), EMS Council, Farmland Protection Advisory Board, and Industrial Facilities & Pollution Control Financing Authority.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 1, 2013 Worksession presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard citizen comments opposing UDO text amendment TC1100007's removal of the Durham Review Board for freestanding concealed cell towers (specifically citing a proposed Southpoint/NC 751 tower near high-pressure gas lines) and supporting remediation of MTBE petroleum groundwater contamination affecting roughly 50 properties in Rougemont. In formal action, the Board voted unanimously (5-0) by voice vote to suspend the rules to act on Item 2 regarding the removal of Lisa Panero from the Durham Workforce Development Board for exceeding the 50% annual absence limit; a motion to remove her was moved and seconded before the middle portion of the transcript truncated. Later in the session, commissioners heard FY 2013-2014 funding presentations from nonprofit agencies—including arts, youth workforce, TROSA, Operation Breakthrough, Museum of Durham History, Eno River Association, and after-school programs—and raised concerns about regional cost-sharing, Durham Public Schools (DPS) partnerships, and the City of Durham phasing out smaller nonprofit contracts before scheduling a follow-up budget discussion.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments: Cell Tower Ordinance (TC1100007) and Rougemont Groundwater Contamination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two speakers representing the Good Neighbors of 751 Durham and the Inter-Neighborhood Council opposed UDO Section 5.3.3 and pending amendment TC1100007, arguing that eliminating the 10-member Durham Review Board shifts cell tower siting authority solely to the Planning Director without resident notice or legislative review—highlighting a proposed tower near two high-pressure gas lines along NC 751. A Rougemont resident also spoke in strong support of moving forward to resolve a 25-year-old petroleum/MTBE groundwater contamination issue affecting about 50 properties, noting residents canvassed the area and found unanimous backing. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, Chair of the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC), invited speakers to share their UDO cell tower concerns at Wednesday's JCCPC meeting.

agenda_items.title: Removal of Lisa Panero from Durham Workforce Development Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that Lisa Panero, appointed March 23, 2009 to the Durham Workforce Development Board, had absences exceeding 50% of meetings in a calendar year in violation of the Board's appointment attendance policy and had not resigned following a written request. The Board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules to act on the item during the work session, and a motion to remove Ms. Panero was moved and seconded immediately prior to transcript truncation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (suspend rules); removal motion moved and seconded before transcript truncation

agenda_items.title: Nonprofit Agency FY 2013-2014 Funding Presentations and Commissioner Follow-up Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners heard budget requests and program updates from local nonprofits including a creative arts organization, a youth Summer Career Academy and school-year internship program, TROSA, Operation Breakthrough (Troy Dixon), the Museum of Durham History (Katie Spencer), the Eno River Association ($15,000 request matched by a $38,000 City of Raleigh grant), and an after-school program partnering with Githens Middle School. Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and colleagues pressed TROSA on why Wake County provided no funding despite 35 Wake residents being served, questioned why agencies already receiving DPS or mental health funds sought supplemental county grants, and noted that roughly 20 requesting agencies did not appear before scheduling a follow-up 11:30 AM budget discussion prior to their 1:00-4:00 PM CIP session.

votes.item_title: Suspension of Rules to Act on Item 2 (Workforce Development Board Removal)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote; the subsequent substantive removal motion was moved and seconded at [00:21:42]-[00:22:03] immediately before middle transcript truncation.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved to suspend the rules so the Board could take action during the work session on removing Lisa Panero from the Durham Workforce Development Board for excessive absences.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 11, 2013 Regular Session presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners passed all formal items unanimously (5-0) with no split or contested votes. Chair Foster read a North Carolina Department of Commerce letter awarding Durham County a $600,000 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) contingency grant for Rougemont water system infrastructure, and County Manager Mike Ruffin presented the Anchor Award to County Engineer Glenn Whisler for 16 years of leadership and delivering the new Durham County Courthouse $24 million under expected budget. Following a public hearing, the Board voted 5-0 to levy a $7 motor vehicle registration tax in Durham County and voted 5-0 to approve the accompanying interlocal and implementation agreements directing the revenue to Triangle Transit Authority (TTA) to support the Bus and Rail Investment Plan. The Board also approved Consent Agenda items 6A-N (excluding 6G) 5-0 and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and $600,000 CDBG Grant for Rougemont Water System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. opened the meeting, announced board vacancies, upcoming Department of Social Services operating hour changes effective June 24, 2013 (7:30 AM-5:30 PM), and the Durham Diabetes Coalition television program. He also read an official letter from Governor Pat McCrory and NC Department of Commerce Secretary Sharon Decker awarding $600,000 in CDBG contingency infrastructure funds, which staff clarified is designated specifically for the Rougemont water system.

agenda_items.title: Minutes Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. announced that approval of the meeting minutes would be deferred and submitted on April 8, 2013.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of Anchor Award to County Engineer Glenn Whisler
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented the Anchor Award to County Engineer Glenn Whisler, crediting his 16 years of Capital Improvement Program oversight—most recently delivering the newly dedicated Durham County Courthouse $24 million under expected budget alongside Senior Project Manager Adeel Shobande and engineering staff—with saving the County hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. Whisler accepted the award on behalf of his staff and thanked the Board for its 2000 master facilities vision and commitment to sustainable design.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A-N, excluding 6G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved Consent Agenda items 6A through 6N, with Item 6G removed, by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution Levying $7 Motor Vehicle Registration Tax
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Attorney Carol Hammond introduced the public hearing and resolution to levy a $7 vehicle registration tax on motor vehicles registered in Durham County to support transit. One speaker, Mike Shiflet, spoke in support of creating a dedicated transit revenue source, after which the Board unanimously adopted the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Interlocal and Implementation Agreements for $7 Vehicle Registration Tax (Bus and Rail Investment Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carol Hammond outlined the interlocal agreement among TTA, Durham, Raleigh, and Chapel Hill directing 100% of Durham County's $7 registration tax to TTA, along with the implementation agreement among the County, TTA, and the MPO allowing up to 50% for increased costs of existing DATA service with annual reporting and four-year reviews. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requested a future update on how the agreements impact the Bus and Rail Investment Plan, and TTA General Manager David King noted City of Durham transit budget pressures stemming from expiring CMAQ funds for the Bull City Connector and $250,000 in state operating assistance.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Economic Development and Personnel Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location/expansion and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider public officer or employee qualifications and performance. The Board reconvened in open session at 02:19:57 and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Resolution Levying $7 Motor Vehicle Registration Tax in Durham County
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a public hearing with one supportive speaker (Mike Shiflet), the Board adopted the resolution levying the $7 vehicle registration tax on motor vehicles registered in Durham County.

votes.item_title: Interlocal and Implementation Agreements for $7 Vehicle Registration Tax Transit Proceeds
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: The Board approved the interlocal agreement with TTA and partner municipalities and the implementation agreement with TTA and the MPO governing distribution and reporting of the $7 vehicle registration tax for the Bus and Rail Investment Plan.

votes.item_title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: The Board voted to enter closed session to discuss business/industry location or expansion and personnel qualifications/employment matters.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 25, 2013 Regular Session presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners recognized Public Health Director Gayle Harris for receiving the 2013 Sam Stevens Award, approved Consent Agenda items A-I (excluding F) 5-0, held an advance public comment period on the FY 2013-2014 budget, and conducted a public hearing on UDO text amendment TC12009 removing the five-year cap on public school modular classrooms prior to a truncated middle segment. Following closed session and written-ballot board appointments, the Board divided 3-2 on authorizing an offer to purchase 264+ acres at 1003 Santee Road from Capital Bank for $950,000 for East Durham open space: Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs voted Aye, while Brenda A. Howerton and Fred Foster Jr. voted Nay. Howerton and Foster cited a projected $19 million budget gap and potential property tax burdens on residents, whereas Reckhow, Jacobs, and Page emphasized that the purchase used previously designated open space funds, leveraged a one-third City of Raleigh grant, and protected critical Falls Lake watershed land in underserved East Durham.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Recognition of Public Health Director Gayle Harris
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. announced the March 10, 2013 grand opening and dedication ceremony for the new Durham County Courthouse at 510 South Dillard Street and referenced the February 11 minutes. Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton then recognized Public Health Director Gayle Harris for earning the NC Association of Local Health Directors' Sam Stevens Award, and Harris thanked the Board while reflecting on her 41 years of public health service.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-I, excluding Item F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved Consent Agenda items A through I, with Item F removed, on a unanimous 5-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Advance Public Comments on FY 2013-2014 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted the annual non-statutory advance budget public comment period ahead of May budget preparation. No members of the public signed up to speak, and commissioners reminded the public that written comments could be emailed to commissioners@dconc.gov.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC12009 (Temporary Uses: School Modular Classrooms)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Steve Medlin presented TC12009, recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission, which permits annual temporary use renewals for public school modular classrooms without a site plan and removes the five-year maximum limit subject to parking and stormwater analysis. Commissioner Michael D. Page expressed concern over heavy reliance on classroom trailers at schools like Eastway and urged DPS to focus on permanent classrooms, while Commissioner Wendy Jacobs queried document versions; a motion to approve was made after closing the public hearing before the transcript truncated.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Motion made; vote omitted due to transcript truncation

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following fragmented ballot counting on board appointments, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding open space acquisition at 1003 Santee Road and (a)(6) for personnel matters. Upon returning to open session at 02:30:41, the County Attorney announced written-ballot selections to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (4 appointees), Durham City-County Appearance Commission (Wayne Alesbrook), Community Child Protection / Child Fatality Prevention Team (Dorothy Brown and Harriet Sander), and township/at-large positions (Brian Busby, Riddle Smith, and Lindsey Smart).

agenda_items.title: Offer to Purchase 1003 Santee Road for Open Space ($950,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, Commissioner Michael D. Page moved and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded authorizing the County Manager to submit an offer to purchase 1003 Santee Road from Capital Bank for $950,000 and close by March 27, 2013. The motion passed on a 3-2 split vote with Page, Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye, and Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Chair Fred Foster Jr. voting Nay over budget-gap and tax-impact concerns.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 3-2 (Ayes: Page, Reckhow, Jacobs; Nays: Howerton, Foster)

votes.item_title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(6)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Michael D. Page moved and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs seconded entering closed session to instruct staff on acquiring 1003 Santee Road from Capital Bank and to consider personnel matters.

votes.item_title: Authorize Offer to Purchase 1003 Santee Road from Capital Bank ($950,000)
votes.notes: Split 3-2 voice vote following closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioners Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Wendy Jacobs supported purchasing the 264+ acre Santee Road parcel using designated open space funds and a City of Raleigh grant, while Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Chair Fred Foster Jr. dissented due to a projected $19 million budget gap and potential tax pressures.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Acquisition of 1003 Santee Road Open Space Property ($950,000)
disagreements.summary: The Board split 3-2 over purchasing 264+ acres at 1003 Santee Road in East Durham for $950,000, weighing pre-designated open space funding, Falls Lake watershed protection, and equity for East Durham against a projected $19 million FY 2013-2014 budget gap and possible tax increases.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $950,000 acquisition using previously set-aside open space funds
side_a_arguments: Funds were already designated in prior budgets for open space and farmland protection, avoiding direct impact on the upcoming operating budget.

One-third of the purchase price is covered by a City of Raleigh grant, and 93% of the 264+ acre site lies within 300 feet of water with Falls Lake frontage, potentially generating Falls Lake nutrient reduction credits.
Represents Durham County's first Eastern Open Space land purchase in a rapidly growing East Durham community near Neal Middle School.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose discretionary land acquisition during a severe projected budget shortfall
side_b_arguments: County Manager projections indicate a potential $19 million budget gap and possible property tax increases in the upcoming budget cycle.
Residents consulted in Southeast Durham weighed discretionary spending against tax burdens and urgent household needs.
Fiscal conservatism warrants deferring discretionary capital purchases under current budget constraints.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 3-2, authorizing the County Manager to enter an offer to purchase 1003 Santee Road for $950,000 and close by March 27, 2013.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 11, 2013 Regular Session presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened by voting 4-0 to excuse Commissioner Wendy Jacobs due to a family emergency, and every subsequent vote passed unanimously (4-0) among the four seated commissioners present with no split or contested votes. The Board approved the January 14 and January 28 Regular Session minutes and Consent Agenda items A-I (excluding Item E, pulled to Item 10), then held a public hearing and voted 4-0 to allocate $400,000 in economic development investment funds to bioMérieux, Inc. to support its Treyburn manufacturing expansion. Commissioners also held an early public hearing on the FY 2013-2014 HUD HOME Consortium Annual Action Plan (approximately $652,712 consortium total, $32,636 county pro-rata share) and later voted 4-0 to adopt both three Federal Legislative Agenda priorities (opposing unfunded mandates, supporting gun safety and mental health funding aligned with the Board's January 14 resolution, and maintaining education and workforce funding) and the 2013 State Legislative Agenda (except Item 3). Following a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), the Board voted 4-0 in open session to approve agricultural conservation easements on two farm properties (8848 Roxboro Road and 12459 Hampton Road).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. announced that Commissioner Wendy Jacobs was absent due to a family emergency, and the Board voted 4-0 to excuse her. Commissioners then unanimously approved the minutes of the January 14 and January 28, 2013 Regular Sessions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-I, excluding Item E)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Michael D. Page requested pulling Item E (2013 State Legislative Agenda) to Item 10 to inquire about adding a citizen-suggested legislative proposal. The remaining Consent Agenda items A through I (excluding E) passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $400,000 Economic Development Investment Funds for bioMérieux, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a $400,000 General Fund economic development incentive for bioMérieux, Inc. at Treyburn Corporate Park (108 local manufacturing employees producing blood culture bottles) to compete against expansion sites in Brazil, India, and China, subject to site-preparation reimbursement and clawback terms, a JobLink job fair, and LEED construction goals. Following public remarks from Site Director Brian Riley and citizen Victoria Peterson, the Board approved the allocation 4-0.

agenda_items.title: FY 2013-2014 Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing (HOME Consortium Funds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Wilma Conyers presented the required initial public hearing for the FY 2013-2014 City-County HOME Consortium Annual Action Plan due to HUD by May 15, estimating $652,712 in consortium funds (with a $32,636 county pro-rata share and $146,860 required non-federal match) for homeownership, rehabilitation, and first-time homebuyer programs. Citizen April Johnson began speaking during the public hearing prior to transcript truncation.

agenda_items.title: Federal Legislative Agenda Priorities (Gun Safety, Mental Health, Unfunded Mandates, Education & Workforce)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following transcript truncation, commissioners discussed framing the federal legislative agenda around gun safety and mental health funding rather than the phrase 'gun control,' while ensuring alignment with the Board's January 14, 2013 resolution supporting bans on high-caliber semi-automatic weapons and high-capacity magazines, universal background checks, and mental health early-intervention funding. Commissioner Michael D. Page also emphasized school safety concerns before the Board voted 4-0 to approve three federal priorities: opposing unfunded mandates, gun safety and mental health funding, and maintaining education and workforce development funding.

agenda_items.title: 2013 Durham County State Legislative Agenda (Pulled Consent Item E)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Michael D. Page raised a constituent request regarding legal protections for grandparents caring for adopted or foster grandchildren and asked whether items could still be added ahead of the March 20 local bill deadline; staff confirmed additional items could be drafted by the County Attorney and approved separately. Commissioners then voted 4-0 to adopt the 2013 State Legislative Agenda except Item 3, while requesting to review revised wording before distribution.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Conservation Easement Acquisitions (Tilley and Day Farms)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 4-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding open space acquisition at 1003 Santee Road and conservation easements on two farm properties at 8848 Roxboro Road (George P. and Elizabeth Tilley) and 12459 Hampton Road (Douglas Day). Upon returning to open session at 01:49:51, the Board voted 4-0 to approve acquiring the conservation easements on the Tilley and Day farm properties.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 4, 2013 Worksession presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners received an update from Durham Technical Community College President Dr. Bill Ingram on the needs-based Durham Challenge Award funded by 1/4-cent sales tax proceeds, before the middle portion of the transcript truncated at the start of the 2013 Legislative Agenda briefing. Following truncation, the Board unanimously (5-0) suspended the rules to address the deferred Raleigh-Durham (RDU) Airport Authority appointment and engaged in a sharp policy disagreement over term limits: Ellen W. Reckhow argued for placing a termed-out incumbent on the ballot to allow service as chair, while Brenda A. Howerton opposed overriding term limits when qualified new applicants had applied. Ultimately no motion was made to override the policy, and after a 2-2-1 tie between Clay Wheeler and Larry Jenkins on the first ballot, the Board elected Clay C. Wheeler (transcribed as Clay C. Quiller) on the second ballot. Commissioners also criticized four-month delays in receiving Durham Public Schools enrollment data under Board directives and voted 5-0 to enter closed session for attorney-client consultations.

agenda_items.title: Durham Tech Update on Quarter-Cent Sales Tax Financial Assistance (Durham Challenge Award)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Tech President Dr. Bill Ingram reported that the College implemented its 1/4-cent sales tax financial aid program on a needs basis using FAFSA after Pell Grants, providing roughly $2,500 per semester through work-study and expanding toward off-campus internships in public schools. Commissioners questioned an approximately $103,000 variance between the $888,000 budget allocation and $785,000 accounted for (proposed as unrestricted), suggested branding the award as 'Durham Scholars,' and reviewed state funding mechanics where $8 million in student tuition reverts to Raleigh and counts toward the state allocation.

agenda_items.title: 2013 Durham County Legislative Agenda Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Deborah Craig-Ray began presenting staff revisions to the 2013 Durham County Legislative Agenda following the prior month's work session before the middle of the transcript truncated.

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham (RDU) Airport Authority Appointment and Term-Limit Policy Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a 5-0 vote to suspend the rules to act on the deferred RDU Airport Authority appointment, commissioners debated whether to place a termed-out applicant on the ballot (Ellen W. Reckhow citing prior 10-year precedent for an incoming chair) versus enforcing adopted term limits in fairness to new applicants (Brenda A. Howerton). No motion to override the appointment policy was pursued, and on the second written ballot—breaking a 2-2-1 first-ballot tie between Larry Jenkins and Clay Wheeler—the Board elected Clay C. Wheeler (transcribed as Clay C. Quiller).

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
disagreements.issue: Term-Limit Exception for Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Appointment
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed over whether to suspend or waive the Board's appointment term-limit rules to place an incumbent/former appointee on the RDU Airport Authority ballot despite having exceeded term limits.
disagreements.side_a_position: Allow an exception to place the termed-out candidate on the ballot
side_a_arguments: Because RDU Airport Authority terms are only two years and officer progression takes multiple terms, a member can reach the threshold of becoming chair only after extended tenure.
The Board previously allowed a fifth two-year term (10 years total) for Steve Toler so he could serve as RDU chair.
disagreements.side_b_position: Enforce adopted term-limit rules and consider only eligible applicants
side_b_arguments: Supporting an applicant who has already exceeded term limits violates the Board's adopted appointment rules in bad faith.
Other qualified citizens applied in accordance with the rules and deserve fair consideration rather than being displaced for an incumbent.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Fred Foster Jr. offered to entertain a motion to add the name, which Ellen W. Reckhow declined to pursue; the Board voted exclusively among the six eligible applicants on the ballot and elected Clay C. Wheeler on the second ballot.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 14, 2013 Regular Session presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners debated a board-appointment swap requested by Michael D. Page and Ellen W. Reckhow—Page keeping Operation Breakthrough and Reckhow taking Page's seat on Triangle Transit Authority (TTA)—before voting 5-0 to add the matter as Item 13 (after Chair Foster initially abstained and was reminded he was required to vote). The Board also voted 5-0 to approve four sets of November and December 2012 minutes and recognized Alice Sharpe for Downtown Durham Inc.'s 2012 Visionary Award, while Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton introduced Item 6, a resolution supporting federal regulatory reform of firearms and ammunition and expanded mental health funding in response to the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting, prior to middle transcript truncation. Upon returning to Item 13 after a recess, the Board voted 5-0 to appoint Reckhow to Page's unexpired TTA term through November 30, 2013, and—following a procedural debate over whether the Board could suspend rules governing the Chair's appointment authority—voted 5-0 on a compromise allowing Page to continue serving on Operation Breakthrough until the matter returned for formal reconsideration, before entering closed session.

Reckhow so Page could attend Thursday's Operation Breakthrough meeting (complementing his childcare board roles) while Reckhow, past TTA Chair assisting with TTA's general counsel search, could take Page's TTA term expiring November 30, 2013. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Chair Appointment Authority vs. Suspending Board Rules for Operation Breakthrough Seat Swap
disagreements.summary: Commissioners Michael D. Page and Ellen W. Reckhow clashed with Chair Fred Foster Jr. and the County Attorney over whether the Board could immediately swap Reckhow out of the Operation Breakthrough Board by suspending its rules rather than awaiting a new Chair appointment or work-session rule amendment.
disagreements.side_a_position: Treat commissioner board swaps as routine and suspend Board rules to enact the Operation Breakthrough swap immediately
side_a_arguments: Commissioner seat swaps for scheduling convenience or subject-matter alignment have historically been treated as routine the same evening.
Under Robert's Rules of Order, voluntarily adopted Board rules that do not violate state or local law can be suspended by Board vote, as the Board routinely does at work sessions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve Chair appointment authority and avoid amending or suspending external-effect rules mid-meeting without work-session review
side_b_arguments: Board rules assign Operation Breakthrough appointments to the Chair, subject to Board ratification.
The County Attorney advised that under Robert's Rules, rules granting external authority beyond meeting procedure cannot be suspended—only amended after prior work-session discussion.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted a 5-0 compromise motion allowing Michael D. Page to continue serving on Operation Breakthrough (covering the upcoming Thursday meeting) until the matter returns before the Board for formal reconsideration.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 7, 2013 Worksession presided over by Chair Fred Foster Jr., the Durham Board of County Commissioners took no formal votes and experienced no split votes, focusing on citizen comments, Durham Public Schools (DPS) capital bond reallocation requests, the 2013 State Legislative Agenda, and pending board directives. During Citizens' Comments, John Tarantino welcomed the newly seated Board with a modified song and another speaker raised jail facility cleanliness, $8-$9 phone call fees, and commissary revenue reporting. Commissioners declined to place DPS's request to reallocate unissued 2007 school bond proceeds on the consent agenda, with Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs demanding current 40-day enrollment/capacity figures and full written project descriptions before the item is reconsidered in regular session. Following a truncated middle section, staff and commissioners reviewed draft 2013 State Legislative Agenda proposals—including design-build contracting authority for wastewater plant upgrades, expanded deer hunting (while preserving the 2001 ban on hunting with dogs), EMS memorial support, and Medicaid ALS/BLS reimbursement alignment—and agreed to add all five commissioners to the Holton Career & Resource Center Advisory Committee mailing list.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Comments: New Board Welcome and Jail Conditions/Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Tarantino sang an adapted version of The Hollies' 'He Ain't Heavy, He's My Brother' to welcome the newly installed five-member Board. A second speaker urged contracting for cleaner public restrooms downstairs and raised concerns about detainees representing themselves lacking paper/literature, high jail phone fees ($8-$9 for two to three minutes), and the absence of public budget reporting on commissary and phone revenues generated from detainees.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Request to Reallocate Authorized Unissued 2007 School Bond Proceeds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Superintendent Dr. Eric Becoats and staff requested reallocation of unissued 2007 school bond proceeds, but Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow objected that DPS had still not delivered updated 40-day enrollment and capacity data requested months earlier or project-by-project written descriptions explaining transfers (such as Burton restroom modifications, roof/kitchen hood work, and High School A). Commissioner Wendy Jacobs also queried the Bacon Street central services facility and residual funds retained only for prior High School A land/design costs, and the Board directed staff to bring the full backup to the next regular session rather than the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: 2013 State Legislative Agenda Review (Jail Site, Design-Build, Deer Hunting, and EMS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle segment, staff updated commissioners that nonconforming zoning grandfathering on the former state prison/jail site had expired and the state declined to lease it, while County Engineer Glenn Whisler requested legislative authority for design-build project delivery to handle proprietary wastewater treatment plant processes. Assistant County Manager Deborah Craig-Ray also reviewed northern Durham resident requests to expand deer hunting (without lifting the 2001 ban on hunting with dogs), conceptual support for an EMS memorial, and legislation aligning Medicaid ALS/BLS reimbursement rules with federal definitions, with a revised package slated to return January 28.

agenda_items.title: Review of Board of County Commissioners Directives and Holton Center Communications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant to the County Manager Ellen Weiland-Wease reviewed Board directives, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requesting an update on the pending Rougemont groundwater item. Commissioners noted that only two members had been receiving Holton Career & Resource Center Advisory Committee notices and requested adding all five commissioners to the mailing list alongside a planned DPS career and technical education (CTE) bus tour.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 10, 2012 regular session—presided over by newly elected Chair Fred Foster Jr.—the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved the November 5 work session and November 26 regular session minutes, heard citizen comments on electronic gaming privilege taxes and board email deliberation practices, and presented a resolution honoring Sam and Audrey Sellers for 21 years of operating Talk of the Town in downtown Durham. Following public hearings, the Board voted unanimously (5-0) to adopt three Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) text amendments: rural sign standards, TC1200007 (allowing graduated building floor area increases based on acreage for paintball and similar facilities in the rural tier), and TC1200006 (defining electronic gaming/internet sweepstakes operations in CG, CC, and IL districts with a 500-foot separation requirement). The Board also completed balloted appointments to four citizen advisory boards and unanimously entered closed session for economic development and attorney-client consultations (including Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser et al.), returning with no action taken and zero split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Announcements, and Eno River Calendar Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements covered county broadcast schedules, volunteer board vacancies, the December 13 FY 2013-2014 nonprofit funding pre-application deadline, a December 13 northern Durham community meeting at the Bahama Ruritan Club, and Welcome Baby's winter coat and diaper drive. Eno River Association Executive Director Robin Jacobs presented the 2013 Eno River calendar and thanked the Board for restoring Durham Open Space and Trails funding.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (November 5, 2012 Work Session and November 26, 2012 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the minutes from the November 5, 2012 work session and November 26, 2012 regular session without modification.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens addressed post-election community unity, county vs. city collection of the $5 statutory privilege license tax on video games and the proposed 500-foot separation for electronic gaming (Allen Lane), and staffing/workload concerns as well as open-meetings risks from 'reply all' email exchanges among commissioners, which the chair noted the Board would review under advisement.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Audrey and Sam Sellers, Owners of Talk of the Town
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a resolution honoring Sam and Audrey Sellers for opening Talk of the Town in downtown Durham on September 27, 1991, hosting prominent musicians, athletes, and community events over 21 years, and donating food to local charities such as Feed the Children and Durham Rescue Mission. Vice Chair Brenda A. Howerton commended their early investment in downtown revitalization.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Rural Sign Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a UDO text amendment regarding rural sign standards, noting the Planning Commission recommended approval 13-0 and the City Council had already approved it. No speakers signed up for the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Paintball or Similar Recreation Facilities on Natural Sites (TC1200007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC1200007, requested by Morningstar Law Group to replace the flat 750-square-foot building limit with a graduated floor-area allowance based on acreage in the rural tier only (Planning Commission 11-0; City Council approved). Attorney Patrick Byker, representing G&B Business Ventures (a 44-acre paintball facility on Highway 98), noted Orange and Wake counties impose no square-footage cap and argued larger groups need space for storage and team preparation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Electronic Gaming Operations (TC1200006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC1200006 defining electronic gaming (internet sweepstakes) as an indoor recreation use permitted in CG, CC, and IL zoning districts with a 500-foot property-line separation from residences, schools, daycares, parks, places of worship, and other electronic gaming sites, plus signage, outdoor activity, lighting, and alcohol restrictions (Planning Commission 11-0; City Council approved). Staff clarified in response to citizen Allen Lane's comment that North Carolina counties lack statutory authority to levy privilege license fees on video machines, and agreed to email him.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voted by written ballot, and the County Attorney announced selections: Gregory E. Ward (Citizens Advisory Committee), Stephen Watson (Community Child Protection Team / Child Fatality Prevention Team), Janice Brahms Butler and Ernest Dean L. McCoy (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee), and Gilda Wambel (Women's Commission).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Economic Development and Attorney-Client Consultations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location/expansion and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with counsel regarding Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser et al. Upon returning to open session at 02:13:58, the Board reported no action was taken and adjourned at 9:16 p.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 5, 2012 Work Session and November 26, 2012 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Routine approval of prior regular and work session minutes.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment — Rural Sign Standards (Item 12)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted rural sign standards text amendment following a public hearing with no speakers.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment TC1200007 — Paintball or Similar Recreation Facilities on Natural Sites
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted text amendment allowing graduated building floor-area increases based on site acreage in the rural tier for paintball facilities.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted electronic gaming use regulations in CG, CC, and IL districts with 500-foot separation from sensitive and similar uses.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4))
votes.notes: Board proceeded directly into closed session following motion and second; returned at 02:13:58 with no action taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved to enter closed session for business/industry location matters and attorney-client consultation on Geraldine Robinson v. Joe Bowser et al.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 3, 2012 organizational meeting, Board of Elections Director Michael Perry presented election certificates, and Chief District Court Judge Marcia H. Morey administered oaths of office to the Soil and Water Conservation District supervisor, Register of Deeds Willie Covington, and incoming/returning County Commissioners Fred Foster Jr., Wendy Jacobs, Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, and Ellen W. Reckhow. The Board held two contested leadership elections by show of hands: for Board Chair, Fred Foster Jr. defeated nominee Ellen W. Reckhow by a majority show-of-hands vote (the transcript records 'that's a majority' without stating the numerical tally or naming which individual commissioners raised their hands for each candidate); for Vice Chair, Brenda A. Howerton defeated nominee Ellen W. Reckhow by a majority show-of-hands vote (again recorded as 'that's a majority' without individual hand-raise names or numerical tally). Chair Fred Foster Jr. then presided over the unanimous approval of public official bonds for the Register of Deeds, followed by swearing-in remarks from all five commissioners before adjourning for a reception.

agenda_items.title: Board of Elections Certificates and Oaths of Office Ceremony
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board of Elections Director Michael Perry presented election certificates. Chief District Court Judge Marcia H. Morey administered oaths of office to the Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor, Register of Deeds Willie Covington, newly elected Commissioners Fred Foster Jr. and Wendy Jacobs, and returning Commissioners Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, and Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With both Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow placed in nomination for Board Chair, the presiding official closed nominations and called for a show-of-hands vote. A majority of commissioners raised their hands for Fred Foster Jr., who then assumed the chair.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Majority show of hands; Foster over Reckhow)

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Fred Foster Jr. opened nominations for Vice Chair, with Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton both nominated. Following a motion and second to close nominations, a majority of commissioners voted by show of hands to elect Brenda A. Howerton as Vice Chair.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Majority show of hands; Howerton over Reckhow)

agenda_items.title: Approval of Public Official Bonds for Register of Deeds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered and approved the statutory public official bond for Register of Deeds Willie Covington without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Remarks and Adjournment for Reception
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Each commissioner—Michael D. Page, Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow (noting her 11th term and thanking Page for four years as Chair), and Chair Fred Foster Jr.—thanked voters, family, and campaign volunteers and pledged collaborative governance before adjourning to a public reception.

votes.item_title: Election of Fred Foster Jr. as Board Chair (over Ellen W. Reckhow)
votes.notes: Show-of-hands vote; transcript records only 'That's a majority' for Fred Foster Jr. without stating the numerical tally or naming individual members' hand raises.
votes.discussion_detail: Contested leadership election between nominees Fred Foster Jr. and Ellen W. Reckhow conducted by show of hands.

votes.item_title: Election of Brenda A. Howerton as Board Vice Chair (over Ellen W. Reckhow)
votes.notes: Show-of-hands vote; transcript records only 'That's a majority' for Brenda A. Howerton without stating the numerical tally or naming individual members' hand raises.
votes.discussion_detail: Contested leadership election between nominees Brenda A. Howerton and Ellen W. Reckhow conducted by show of hands after closing nominations.

votes.item_title: Approval of Public Official Bonds for Register of Deeds
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; individual mover and seconder were not spoken on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted and approved public official bonds for Register of Deeds Willie Covington.
